text: Which Hawthorn great was nicknamed "Lethal"?
fact: Matthews was named Player of the Century and an inaugural Legend of the Hall of Fame.

text: Who coached Hawthorn to three premierships in a row, from 2013 to 2015?
fact: Clarkson had also coached Hawthorn to the 2008 flag.

text: Which club did Richmond beat in the 2017 AFL Grand Final?
fact: Adelaide went in as favourites, but Richmond won by 48 points.

text: Which VFL/AFL club merged with the Brisbane Bears to form the Brisbane Lions?
fact: Fitzroy's last AFL season was 1996.

text: Before Perth Stadium opened in 2018, which ground was West Coast's home from 1987?
fact: The last AFL game there was West Coast v Adelaide in round 23, 2017.

text: What nickname did Tasmania's AFL club unveil in 2024?
fact: Its colours are myrtle green, primrose yellow and rose red.

text: Who coached Collingwood to the 2023 premiership?
fact: Collingwood beat Brisbane by four points, and Bobby Hill won the Norm Smith Medal.

text: If a kick for goal hits a goal post, what score is recorded?
fact: A goal only counts if the ball crosses the line untouched by a player or a goal post.

text: Which club's theme song is "We Are the Navy Blues"?
fact: It is sung to the tune of the old music hall song Lily of Laguna.

text: At which ground did Melbourne win its 2021 premiership?
fact: A Victorian lockdown moved it to Perth. Christian Petracca won the Norm Smith Medal.

text: Which club won the first AFLW premiership, in 2017?
fact: Adelaide beat the undefeated Lions by six points, 35 to 29.

text: Norm Smith, after whom the Grand Final medal is named, coached which club to six premierships?
fact: He also played in four Melbourne premierships.

text: Who coached North Melbourne to its first two VFL premierships, in 1975 and 1977?
fact: The 1977 flag came in a replay, after a drawn Grand Final against Collingwood.

text: Who won the Norm Smith Medal in both of Adelaide's premierships, 1997 and 1998?
fact: He was the first player to win the medal in consecutive seasons.

text: Which club stopped the Brisbane Lions winning a fourth flag in a row, in the 2004 Grand Final?
fact: It was Port's first AFL Grand Final, and they won by 40 points.

text: Whose mark in the dying seconds sealed Sydney's 2005 premiership?
fact: Sydney held on to win 8.10 (58) to 7.12 (54).

text: Who kicked the match-winning goal from near the boundary in the 2018 Grand Final?
fact: West Coast beat Collingwood 11.13 (79) to 11.8 (74).

text: Chris Judd won a Brownlow with West Coast in 2004. Which club did he win his second with?
fact: He polled 30 votes both times, in 2004 and 2010.

text: As of the end of 2025, who was the last player to kick 100 goals in a VFL/AFL season?
fact: Franklin kicked 113 goals for Hawthorn in 2008.

text: Which AFLW star is the daughter of Port Adelaide great Greg Phillips?
fact: Erin's 2025 induction made them the first father and daughter in the AFL Hall of Fame.

text: A 2019 photo of which AFLW player's soaring kick was later turned into a statue?
fact: The photo was taken in round 7, 2019, by AFL Media photographer Michael Willson.

text: Which club drew with Collingwood in the 2010 Grand Final?
fact: Collingwood won the replay by 56 points. Extra time replaced Grand Final replays from 2016.

text: As of the end of 2025, who was the only player to have won three Norm Smith Medals?
fact: Martin won it in 2017, 2019 and 2020, all for Richmond.

text: Which Richmond legend was nicknamed "Captain Blood"?
fact: A journalist borrowed the name from the Errol Flynn film Captain Blood.

text: Who shared the 1996 Brownlow Medal with Michael Voss?
fact: North Melbourne's Corey McKernan also polled 21 votes but was ineligible through suspension.

text: Who won the first Norm Smith Medal, in the 1979 Grand Final?
fact: Harmes was a great-nephew of Norm Smith himself.

text: Which TV commentator made the "Jesaulenko, you beauty!" call in the 1970 Grand Final?
fact: Jesaulenko took the mark over Collingwood's Graeme Jenkin.

text: Whose late behind won St Kilda the 1966 Grand Final by one point?
fact: Breen was 18 at the time.

text: At which ground did Nicky Winmar make his famous 1993 stand against racist abuse?
fact: After the siren he lifted his jumper and pointed to his skin.

text: Which Western Bulldog polled the most Brownlow votes in 1997 but was ineligible through suspension?
fact: Grant polled 27 votes. Robert Harvey won the medal with 26.

text: Jobe Watson's 2012 Brownlow was later awarded jointly to Trent Cotchin and which player?
fact: Watson gave the medal back in 2016 after the Essendon supplements saga.

text: As of the end of 2025, who had played in a record seven VFL/AFL premierships?
fact: All seven came with Hawthorn, from 1976 to 1991. He played in 11 Grand Finals.

text: Which club left the VFL after the 1914 season, having lost its last 51 games?
fact: University joined the VFL in 1908.

text: Who was the first player to kick 100 goals in a VFL season?
fact: The Collingwood full-forward kicked 124 goals in 1929.

text: Which of these players won three Brownlow Medals?
fact: Haydn Bunton Sr, Dick Reynolds and Ian Stewart also won three.

text: Which club won the first VFL premiership, in 1897?
fact: There was no Grand Final that year. A round-robin finals series decided it.

text: In what year was the VFL renamed the AFL?
What is the minimum distance a kick must travel for a mark to be paid?
fact: The 15-metre minimum has applied since 2002.

text: How many seasons did Kevin Sheedy coach Essendon?
fact: He coached them from 1981 to 2007, winning flags in 1984, 1985, 1993 and 2000.

text: By how many points did Geelong beat Port Adelaide in the 2007 Grand Final, a record margin?
fact: The score was 24.19 (163) to 6.8 (44).

text: In what year did South Melbourne move its home games to Sydney?
How many goals did Gary Ablett Sr kick for Geelong in the 1989 Grand Final?
fact: He won the Norm Smith Medal even though Hawthorn won by six points.

text: How many goals did Fred Fanning kick for Melbourne in one match in 1947, a VFL/AFL record?
fact: He kicked 18.1 against St Kilda in his final VFL game.

text: How many games did Brent Harvey play, a VFL/AFL record when he retired in 2016?
fact: Collingwood's Scott Pendlebury has since passed it.

text: How many points did Geelong score against the Brisbane Bears in 1992, a VFL/AFL record score?
fact: Geelong kicked 37.17 at Carrara.

Howard Carter found Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922 in which burial ground?
fact: The first step down to the tomb was uncovered on 4 November 1922.

text: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is the only one still standing?
The Rosetta Stone has been in the collection of which museum since 1802?
fact: French soldiers led by Pierre-François Bouchard found it in Egypt in July 1799.

text: Which Athenian philosopher was sentenced to death and drank hemlock?
fact: He had been found guilty of impiety and of corrupting the young.

text: Which Greek thinker is said to have shouted "Eureka!" after an idea came to him in the bath?
fact: The story was first told by the Roman writer Vitruvius, about 200 years later.

text: The Parthenon stands on which rocky hill above Athens?
fact: Pericles launched the building project and the sculptor Phidias oversaw the work.

text: Which gladiator led a huge slave revolt against Rome from 73 to 71 BC?
fact: It began when about 70 gladiators broke out of a training school in Capua.

text: Which emperor ruled Rome when the Great Fire destroyed much of the city in AD 64?
fact: The historian Tacitus says he was away at Antium, on the coast, when it broke out.

text: The Art of War, written in China about 2,500 years ago, is credited to which author?
fact: The book is divided into 13 chapters.

text: Which woman ruled Egypt for about 20 years, took the title of pharaoh and was often shown with a false beard?
fact: She started out as regent for her young stepson, Thutmose III.

text: In an Egyptian tomb, what were canopic jars made to hold?
fact: There were usually four, for the lungs, liver, stomach and intestines.

text: Which temples of Ramesses II were cut into blocks and moved in the 1960s to escape a rising lake?
fact: They were rebuilt 65 m higher, clear of Lake Nasser behind the Aswan High Dam.

text: Which Greek writer, who told the story of the Persian Wars, is known as the Father of History?
fact: The title was given to him by the Roman orator Cicero.

text: Winners at the ancient Olympic Games were crowned with a wreath of what?
fact: Laurel was the prize at the Pythian Games, and wild celery at the Nemean Games.

text: What was garum, a favourite in Roman kitchens?
fact: It was made by leaving salted fish, such as mackerel or anchovies, to ferment in the sun.

text: In a Roman bath house or villa, what was a hypocaust?
fact: Hot air from a furnace was sent through a space under the floor.
wrong: A shrine to the household gods

text: Which Roman emperor wrote the Stoic notebook known as the Meditations?
fact: He wrote it in Greek, not Latin, and partly while on campaign.

text: Which Roman seaside town was buried by the same eruption of Vesuvius that destroyed Pompeii?
fact: It lies under the modern town of Ercolano, buried far deeper than Pompeii was.

text: Which queen of the Iceni led a revolt against Roman rule in Britain in AD 60 or 61?
fact: Her forces burned Colchester, London and St Albans before they were beaten.

text: Which Mesopotamian script was made by pressing a reed into wet clay, leaving wedge-shaped marks?
fact: The name comes from cuneus, the Latin word for wedge.

text: Which king founded the Persian Empire and captured Babylon in 539 BC?
fact: His son and successor went on to conquer Egypt.

text: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were great cities of which Bronze Age civilisation?
fact: Both sites are in modern Pakistan. The civilisation peaked from about 2600 to 1900 BC.

text: Which dynasty, founded by Liu Bang, gave its name to China's largest ethnic group?
fact: Its four centuries were split in two by the short Xin dynasty of the usurper Wang Mang.

text: Egypt's first pyramid, the Step Pyramid at Saqqara, was built for which king?
fact: Its design is credited to his vizier, Imhotep.

text: At Kadesh, one of the biggest chariot battles ever fought, Ramesses II faced which empire?
fact: The two sides later made peace by treaty. A copy hangs at UN headquarters in New York.

text: What name was given to the unfree people who farmed the land for Sparta's citizens?
fact: They made up most of the population of Laconia and Messenia.

text: According to legend, which Greek playwright died when an eagle dropped a tortoise on his head?
fact: He died at Gela in Sicily. The eagle is said to have mistaken his bald head for a rock.

text: Which head of the Library of Alexandria worked out the Earth's circumference from a shadow cast at midsummer noon?
fact: He was born in Cyrene, in what is now Libya.

text: At which battle in 216 BC did Hannibal surround and destroy a much larger Roman army?
fact: One of the two Roman consuls, Aemilius Paullus, was killed in the battle.

text: Who joined Julius Caesar and Pompey in the alliance known as the First Triumvirate?
fact: He died in 53 BC during his failed invasion of Parthia.

text: Which emperor began building the Colosseum, which was opened by his son Titus?
fact: Titus's brother Domitian later added the underground level, the hypogeum.

text: Which Visigoth king led the sack of Rome in AD 410?
fact: It was the first time in almost 800 years that Rome had fallen to a foreign enemy.

text: Which Chinese court official is traditionally credited with inventing paper, in AD 105?
fact: Cruder paper already existed. He improved it using tree bark and hemp waste.

text: Which Indian emperor turned to Buddhism after his brutal conquest of Kalinga?
fact: He was the third ruler of the Maurya Empire and reigned from Pataliputra.

text: Which Maya city in the rainforest of northern Guatemala is home to the Temple of the Great Jaguar?
fact: Tikal National Park became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979.

text: The great library of the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal was found in the ruins of which city?
fact: More than 30,000 clay tablets and fragments were recovered from it.

text: Ancient Rome was famously built on how many hills?
fact: They include the Palatine, the Capitoline and the Aventine.

text: Julius Caesar was killed on the Ides of March. Which day of the month is that?
fact: He was stabbed at a meeting of the Senate.

text: The Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta lasted for how many years?
fact: It ran from 431 to 404 BC and ended with the surrender of Athens.

text: By Roman tradition, in what year BC was the city of Rome founded?
fact: The traditional date, 21 April 753 BC, comes from the Roman scholar Varro.

text: By tradition, in what year BC were the first ancient Olympic Games held?
fact: At first the only event was the stadion, a sprint of about 192 m.

text: In what year BC did Cleopatra die?
fact: She died in Alexandria in August of that year.

text: The ancient Maya counted in a number system built on which base?
fact: They wrote numbers with dots for ones, bars for fives and a shell for zero.

text: In what year BC did Rome destroy the city of Carthage?
fact: The city fell to Scipio Aemilianus at the end of the Third Punic War.

text: In what year AD did Constantine dedicate his new capital, Constantinople?
fact: The city, built on the site of Byzantium, was dedicated on 11 May.

text: Put these people in order of when they died, earliest first.
Put these Roman numerals in order of value, smallest first.
Put these ancient cities in order from west to east, westernmost first.

Which is the largest living species of penguin?
fact: Adults weigh from about 22 to 45 kg.

text: Which are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight?
What is the largest living species of fish?
fact: The largest reliably recorded was about 18.8 metres long.

text: The Komodo dragon, the world's largest lizard, lives wild in which country?
fact: Males can reach about three metres long.

text: In the wild, clownfish shelter among the stinging tentacles of what?
What does a blue whale eat almost exclusively?
The orca, or killer whale, is the largest member of which family?
fact: Adult males typically grow six to eight metres long.

text: Which is Australia's largest bird of prey?
fact: Its wings can span 2.3 metres or more.

text: What is a baby echidna called?
Which Australian animal has fingerprints almost identical to a human's, even under a microscope?
fact: University of Adelaide researchers described the prints in a 1997 paper.

text: Under its white coat, what colour is a polar bear's skin?
fact: The fur has no pigment. It looks white because of the way it scatters light.

text: Which bird has the longest wingspan of any living bird?
fact: Its wings can span more than three metres.

text: The dodo lived only on which island?
The name "orangutan" comes from Malay words meaning what?
fact: Orang means "person" and hutan means "forest".

text: A narwhal's long spiral tusk is actually what?
fact: It is a canine tooth that grows from the left side of the upper jaw, up to 3 metres long.

text: Velociraptor, far bigger in Jurassic Park than in life, was about the size of which bird?
fact: It lived in Asia about 75 to 71 million years ago, and it had feathers.

text: Outbreaks of which coral-eating animal are a major threat to the Great Barrier Reef?
fact: It is named for the venomous spines that cover its upper surface.

text: The redback belongs to the same genus as which famous overseas spider?
fact: The genus is Latrodectus.

text: Which insects fly to the Australian Alps each spring to shelter in cool caves all summer?
fact: They were listed as endangered on the IUCN Red List in 2021.

text: Which scaly, ant-eating mammal is often called the world's most trafficked wild mammal?
fact: Its scales are made of keratin, the same material as fingernails.

text: After a female emu lays her eggs, who sits on them until they hatch?
fact: He goes about eight weeks without eating or drinking and loses a third of his weight.

text: What happens to most barramundi as they get older?
fact: Most mature as males and turn female after at least one spawning season.
wrong: They return to the sea for good

text: How does a honeybee tell her hive-mates where to find food?
fact: The angle of the dance gives the direction relative to the sun; its length gives the distance.
wrong: A scent trail to the flowers

text: Which is the only bear native to South America?
fact: It is the last surviving member of the short-faced bears.

text: What are the closest living relatives of whales and dolphins?
fact: The two lines split about 55 million years ago.

text: Wild axolotls survive only in lakes and canals on the edge of which city?
fact: Critically endangered in the wild, they keep their feathery gills for life.

text: Which is the only primate known to have a venomous bite?
fact: It licks a gland on its upper arm; the secretion is activated when it mixes with saliva.

text: Which marsupial was known only from fossils until one was found alive at Mount Hotham in 1966?
fact: It was described in 1896 from fossil jaws found at Wombeyan Caves in NSW.

text: What is a male swan called?
fact: A female is a pen and a young swan is a cygnet.

text: Which is the only snake known to build an above-ground nest for its eggs?
fact: The female heaps up leaf litter and guards the nest. It is also the longest venomous snake.

text: The tuatara of New Zealand is the last living member of which order of reptiles?
fact: It looks like a lizard, but its order was once widespread and varied.

text: Queensland's extinct "platypus frogs" were famous for raising their young where?
fact: Better known as gastric-brooding frogs, they were last seen in the 1980s.
wrong: In pouches on the father's hips
Under skin on the mother's back

text: Which is the only living member of the kangaroo superfamily that does not hop?
fact: It weighs about 500 grams, lives in north Queensland rainforest and bounds on all fours.

text: The bluebottle that stings Australian swimmers is not a true jellyfish. What is it?
fact: Each bluebottle is a floating colony of specialised individuals called zooids.

text: The bee hummingbird, the world's smallest bird, lives only in which country?
fact: Males are about 5.5 cm long and weigh around two grams.

text: Which eucalypt is Australia's tallest tree species?
fact: The tallest known, Centurion in Tasmania, was measured at about 100 metres in 2018.

text: How many eyes do most spiders have?
fact: They are arranged in four pairs.

text: How many compartments does a cow's stomach have?
fact: They are the rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum.

text: Roughly how many million years ago did an asteroid wipe out the non-bird dinosaurs?
fact: The impact left the Chicxulub crater on the Yucatán Peninsula.

text: In what year was Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born?
fact: She was born on 5 July at the Roslin Institute in Scotland.

text: How many toes does an ostrich have on each foot?
fact: Most birds have four toes on each foot.

text: In what year was the Wollemi pine, the "dinosaur tree", discovered in a NSW gorge?
fact: David Noble and two companions found it in Wollemi National Park, north-west of Sydney.

text: In what year did Thomas Austin release wild rabbits at Barwon Park, Victoria, starting a plague?
fact: He wanted them for hunting. Rabbits had first arrived with the First Fleet in 1788.

text: How many living species of egg-laying mammal are there?
fact: The platypus and four species of echidna.

text: How many living species of sea turtle are there?
fact: The largest, the leatherback, can grow to more than 1.8 metres long.

In Frozen, Anna and Elsa are princesses of which kingdom?
fact: Corona is Rapunzel's kingdom in Tangled.

text: Who voices Donkey in the Shrek films?
fact: John Lithgow voices Lord Farquaad in the first film.

text: In Toy Story (1995), what is the name of the boy next door who destroys toys for fun?
fact: Scud is his dog, who goes after Woody and Buzz.

text: Which studio makes the Despicable Me and Minions films?
fact: Chris Meledandri founded the studio in 2007.

text: In Disney's animated Beauty and the Beast, Lumiere has been turned into what?
fact: Cogsworth became the mantel clock and Mrs Potts the teapot.

text: At the start of Monsters, Inc., what does the city of Monstropolis run on?
fact: By the end, Sulley has the factory collecting laughter instead.

text: Who voices the demigod Maui in Disney's Moana?
fact: Temuera Morrison voices Moana's father, Chief Tui.

text: In Madagascar (2005), Alex, Marty, Melman and Gloria start out in a zoo in which city?
fact: Their home is the Central Park Zoo.

text: In Disney's animated Aladdin, what is the name of Aladdin's pet monkey?
fact: Iago is Jafar's parrot and Rajah is Jasmine's tiger.

text: Phil Collins won an Oscar for You'll Be in My Heart, a song from which Disney film?
fact: He also wrote the songs for Disney's Brother Bear (2003).

text: In Coco (2017), what is the name of the street dog who follows Miguel to the Land of the Dead?
fact: He is a Xoloitzcuintle, a hairless Mexican breed.

text: In How to Train Your Dragon, what species of dragon is Toothless?
fact: Astrid's dragon, Stormfly, is a Deadly Nadder.

text: Which studio made Ice Age (2002) and its four cinema sequels?
fact: Disney shut the studio in April 2021.

text: In Disney's animated The Little Mermaid, what does Scuttle the seagull call a fork?
fact: He says humans use it to straighten their hair. A snarfblatt is his name for a pipe.

text: Which stop-motion studio made Coraline and Kubo and the Two Strings?
fact: The studio is based near Portland, Oregon.

text: In Spirited Away, what are Chihiro's parents turned into?
fact: The film won Best Animated Feature at the 2003 Oscars.

text: Which was the first Pixar film to win the Oscar for Best Animated Feature?
fact: It won at the 2004 ceremony. Monsters, Inc. had been nominated two years earlier but lost.

text: Which cheese is the favourite of Wallace, of Wallace and Gromit?
fact: He likes it on crackers.

text: Who voices Spider-Man Noir in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018)?
fact: John Mulaney voices Spider-Ham, the cartoon pig.

text: Who wrote the songs for Encanto and co-wrote the songs for Moana?
fact: His Encanto songs include We Don't Talk About Bruno.

text: In Cinderella (1950), what is the name of the stepmother's cat?
fact: The mice he chases are Jaq and Gus.

text: Which film won Best Animated Feature at the 2026 Oscars?
fact: Its song Golden won Best Original Song on the same night.

text: In Sing (2016), what kind of animal is theatre owner Buster Moon?
fact: He is voiced by Matthew McConaughey.

text: Who directed The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993)?
fact: Tim Burton produced it and wrote the story it is based on.

text: In Finding Nemo, which Australian voices Bruce the great white shark?
fact: Eric Bana and Bruce Spence voice his shark mates, Anchor and Chum.

text: Brad Bird directed The Incredibles. Which of its characters did he also voice?
fact: Syndrome is Jason Lee and the Underminer is John Ratzenberger.

text: Which Saturday Night Live star was first cast as Shrek and recorded most of the part?
fact: Mike Myers took over the part after Farley died in 1997.

text: A113, the code hidden in Pixar films, is a classroom number at which college?
fact: John Lasseter, Brad Bird and Pete Docter all studied there.

text: Which conductor shakes hands with Mickey Mouse in Disney's Fantasia (1940)?
fact: He conducted the Philadelphia Orchestra for seven of the film's eight pieces.

text: Walt Disney died in 1966 while making which film, the last animated feature he produced?
fact: He died in December 1966; the film opened in October 1967.

text: Which Sydney studio animated Happy Feet and The Lego Movie?
fact: It also animated The Lego Batman Movie and Peter Rabbit.

text: Which Australian made the claymation features Mary and Max and Memoir of a Snail?
fact: His short film Harvie Krumpet won an Oscar in 2004.

text: Flow, Best Animated Feature at the 2025 Oscars, won which country its first Academy Award?
fact: Gints Zilbalodis made the wordless film with Blender, a free animation program.

text: Who wrote the lyrics for Disney's The Little Mermaid (1989) and Beauty and the Beast (1991)?
fact: He died in March 1991, eight months before Beauty and the Beast opened.

text: Whose Zulu chant opens Circle of Life in Disney's animated The Lion King?
fact: The South African composer also arranged the choirs for Hans Zimmer's score.

text: Shaun the Sheep first appeared in which Wallace and Gromit film?
fact: It first aired on Christmas Eve 1995 and won the Oscar for best animated short.
wrong: A Matter of Loaf and Death

text: In what year was Disney's animated The Lion King first released in cinemas?
fact: Elton John and Tim Rice wrote the songs.

text: Walt Disney's honorary Oscar for Snow White came with how many miniature statuettes?
fact: The little ones stood on a stepped base beside one full-size statuette.

text: In the Cars films, what racing number does Lightning McQueen wear?
fact: It marks 1995, the year Pixar's first feature film came out.

text: In Disney's animated The Little Mermaid, how old is Ariel?
In WALL-E, how many years before the film begins did humans leave Earth for a five-year cruise?
fact: The film is set in 2805, with the passengers' descendants still aboard the Axiom.

text: In what year did Mickey Mouse make his official screen debut, in Steamboat Willie?
fact: It premiered at Universal's Colony Theatre on 18 November that year.

text: In One Hundred and One Dalmatians (1961), how many puppies are Pongo and Perdita's own?
fact: The other 84 were bought in shops for Cruella de Vil.

text: In what year did Pixar first show Luxo Jr., the short film starring its hopping desk lamp?
fact: John Lasseter directed it. It premiered at the SIGGRAPH conference in Dallas.

text: In what year did Disney buy Pixar?
fact: The deal, worth about US$7.4 billion in shares, was completed in May.

fact: The studio was founded in June 1985.

text: In Spirited Away, what kind of business does the witch Yubaba run?
fact: Her twin sister, Zeniba, lives far from the bathhouse.

text: In the Pokémon anime, which of Team Rocket's Pokémon talks like a human?
fact: Meowth, Jessie and James were the show's villains for its first 25 seasons.

text: In Naruto, what title does Naruto Uzumaki dream of earning?
fact: The Hokage is the leader of his village.

text: In One Piece, what did eating a Devil Fruit do to Luffy's body?
fact: Luffy ate the Gum-Gum Fruit by accident. His crew are the Straw Hat Pirates.

text: In Sailor Moon, what kind of animal is Luna, the heroine's talking adviser?
fact: Luna finds Usagi and teaches her to become Sailor Moon.

text: Anime is animation from Japan. What is manga?
In Death Note, which fruit can the death god Ryuk not go without?
fact: Ryuk dropped his notebook into the human world out of boredom.

text: In Dragon Ball Z, Goku learns that he belongs to which alien race?
fact: He was sent to Earth as a baby.

text: Which Hayao Miyazaki film won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature at the 2024 ceremony?
fact: It beat Elemental, Nimona, Robot Dreams and Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse.

text: In Fullmetal Alchemist, what is Alphonse Elric's soul bound to?
fact: His brother Edward gave up his right arm to seal it there.

text: In My Hero Academia, which hero ranks number two behind All Might when the story begins?
fact: All Might passes his own power, One For All, to Izuku Midoriya.

text: In Jujutsu Kaisen, how many cursed fingers hold the power of Ryomen Sukuna?
fact: Yuji Itadori becomes Sukuna's host by swallowing one of them.

text: In Neon Genesis Evangelion, what are the giant beings that attack Tokyo-3 called?
fact: The teenage pilots fight them for an organisation called Nerv.

text: In Yu-Gi-Oh!, which monster is Seto Kaiba's signature card?
In Digimon Adventure, which Digimon is the partner of Tai Kamiya?
fact: Tai holds the Crest of Courage.

text: Which weekly manga magazine launched Dragon Ball, Naruto and One Piece?
fact: Shueisha launched it in 1968. Its record print run for one issue is 6.53 million copies.

text: In anime and manga, what happens to the hero of an 'isekai' story?
fact: The word is Japanese for 'another world' or 'different world'.
wrong: They join a school sports team

text: Which Network Ten show, hosted by Ryan and Jade, put Pokémon and Dragon Ball Z on before school?
fact: It began in 1995. Toasted TV took over its slot in August 2005.

text: Which film passed Spirited Away in December 2020 to become Japan's highest-grossing film ever?
fact: Spirited Away had held the record for 19 years.

text: Which artist, called 'the god of manga', created Astro Boy and Kimba the White Lion?
fact: Tezuka qualified as a doctor but chose manga over medicine.

text: In Attack on Titan, what is the name of Eren's home district, where the story begins?
fact: The Colossal Titan destroys its gate at the start of the series.

text: In Spy x Family, what is the codename of Loid Forger's fellow spy Fiona Frost?
fact: Twilight is Loid himself. Thorn Princess is his wife Yor, an assassin.

text: Which author wrote the novel that Howl's Moving Castle is based on?
fact: Her novel came out in 1986. The film was nominated for an Oscar in 2006.

text: Hayao Miyazaki's first feature film as director, in 1979, starred which manga character?
fact: The film is The Castle of Cagliostro.

text: How does Fullmetal Alchemist creator Hiromu Arakawa draw herself in author portraits?
fact: She grew up on a dairy farm in Hokkaido.
wrong: A chicken in a witch's hat

text: Which studio, founded in 2011 by former Gainax staff, made Promare and Little Witch Academia?
fact: Hiroyuki Imaishi and Masahiko Otsuka were among its founders, in August 2011.

text: A Silent Voice and Violet Evergarden are the work of which studio?
fact: The studio is based in Uji, in Kyoto Prefecture.

text: Which singer provided the singing voice of Uta in One Piece Film: Red (2022)?
fact: The film's theme song is New Genesis.

text: Sony bought the anime streaming service Crunchyroll in 2021 from which company?
fact: The deal closed on 9 August 2021 for US$1.175 billion.

text: Which Melbourne company began in 1996 as a mail-order business selling imported anime?
fact: Tim Anderson and Paul Wiegard founded it.

text: In Cowboy Bebop, what is the name of Spike Spiegel's own fighter craft?
fact: Hammerhead is Jet's ship and Red Tail is Faye's.

text: Who directed the 1995 film Ghost in the Shell?
fact: It is based on Masamune Shirow's manga and follows Major Motoko Kusanagi.

text: Which Japanese rock band wrote and performed the songs in the film Your Name?
fact: The band's singer, Yojiro Noda, composed the score.

text: Which voice actor has played Pikachu in the Pokémon anime since its very first episode?
fact: She also voices Tony Tony Chopper in One Piece.

text: Which manga artist created Sailor Moon?
fact: The manga ran in the girls' magazine Nakayoshi.

text: In Dragon Ball, how many Dragon Balls must be gathered to summon the wish-granting dragon?
fact: The story was inspired by the Chinese novel Journey to the West.

text: In the Pokémon anime, how old is Ash Ketchum when he sets out from Pallet Town?
In One Punch Man, Saitama's daily training includes a run of how many kilometres?
fact: Plus 100 push-ups, 100 sit-ups and 100 squats, every day for three years.

text: In what year did the Pokémon anime first air in Japan?
fact: It began on TV Tokyo on 1 April.

text: In what year did the Sailor Moon anime begin on Japanese television?
fact: Toei Animation made it. The first episode went out on TV Asahi on 7 March.

text: In what year was the film Akira released in Japan?
fact: The story is set in Neo-Tokyo in 2019. It is based on a manga that began in 1982.

text: In what year did the first Astro Boy anime series begin on Japanese television?
fact: It began on New Year's Day on Fuji TV. Its Japanese title means Mighty Atom.

text: How many episodes of Naruto: Shippuden were made?
fact: It ran on TV Tokyo from February 2007 to March 2017.

text: How many episodes does the Death Note anime run for?
fact: They went out on Nippon TV from October 2006 to June 2007.

text: Put these anime series in order of their Japanese TV debut, earliest first.
Put these Japanese animated films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these Makoto Shinkai films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these manga in order of when their serialisation began, earliest first.
Put these anime series in order of first broadcast in Japan, earliest first.
Who painted the Mona Lisa?
fact: It is painted in oil on a panel of poplar wood, not on canvas.

text: Michelangelo spent four years painting the ceiling of which chapel?
fact: He painted it between 1508 and 1512 for Pope Julius II.

text: Which painter took a razor to his own left ear after a row with fellow artist Paul Gauguin?
fact: It happened in Arles, in the south of France, two days before Christmas.

text: The painter Frida Kahlo, famous for her self-portraits, came from which country?
fact: Her family home in Mexico City, the Blue House, is now the Frida Kahlo Museum.

text: In 1962 Andy Warhol first showed his 32 paintings of cans of which brand of soup?
fact: The 32 canvases are now in the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

text: In 2018, what did Banksy's Girl with Balloon do moments after it sold at auction?
fact: Renamed Love Is in the Bin, the half-shredded picture sold in 2021 for £18.6 million.

text: The ancient Greek statue known as the Venus de Milo is famous for missing what?
fact: A farmer found it on the Greek island of Milos in 1820. It has been in the Louvre since 1821.

text: Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama is best known for covering her work in what?
fact: She was born in Matsumoto, Japan, in 1929.

text: Which Melbourne laneway is a tourist attraction for its street art?
Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper on a convent wall in which Italian city?
fact: It fills one wall of the dining hall at Santa Maria delle Grazie.

text: A fresco is a painting made on what?
fact: The name comes from the Italian word for fresh.

text: Impressionism took its name from a painting of a harbour at sunrise by which artist?
fact: Impression, Sunrise shows the port of Le Havre, where Monet grew up.

text: Seurat's A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte is a leading example of which technique?
fact: It builds a picture from tiny dots of pure colour. Critics coined the name to mock the style.

text: Fountain, the 1917 artwork credited to Marcel Duchamp, was which object signed 'R. Mutt'?
fact: The three wrong answers were other Duchamp 'readymades'.

text: Jeff Koons's giant Puppy, which sits outside the Guggenheim Bilbao, is covered in what?
fact: Over the summer of 1995-96 it stood outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art.

text: Maurizio Cattelan's artwork Comedian, which sold for US$6.2 million in 2024, is what?
fact: The buyer, crypto entrepreneur Justin Sun, ate the banana at a press conference.
answer: A banana taped to a wall

text: In 1986 the 'Australian Cultural Terrorists' stole a painting by which artist from the NGV?
fact: The Weeping Woman was found 17 days later in a locker at Spencer Street station.

text: Albert Namatjira is best known for landscapes of Central Australia painted in what?
fact: A Western Arrernte man, he held his first solo exhibition in 1938.

text: How did David Walsh, founder of the MONA art museum, make his fortune?
fact: He built a betting system for horse racing and other sports.

text: The Heidelberg School of painters is named after an area that is now a suburb of which city?
fact: Its best-known painters include Arthur Streeton, Frederick McCubbin and Charles Conder.

text: The Archibald Prize is judged by the trustees of which gallery?
fact: The gallery staff who receive, unpack and hang the entries pick a Packing Room Prize.
answer: Art Gallery of New South Wales

text: Which artist designed the cover of Kanye West's 2007 album Graduation?
fact: The two worked together again on the art for Kids See Ghosts in 2018.

text: In painting, what does the Italian term chiaroscuro describe?
fact: The word joins the Italian for light, chiaro, and dark, scuro.
answer: Bold contrast of light and dark

text: Why did the painter Caravaggio flee Rome in 1606?
fact: The victim was Ranuccio Tomassoni. Caravaggio died in 1610, still seeking a pardon.

text: Which two philosophers stand at the centre of Raphael's The School of Athens?
fact: The painting is in the Raphael Rooms of the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican.

text: Picasso's Guernica has hung in which Madrid museum since 1992?
fact: It came to Spain from New York's Museum of Modern Art in 1981.

text: Rodin's The Thinker was first made as a figure for which larger work?
fact: The figure was first called The Poet.

text: In 1990, thieves posing as police stole 13 works from which Boston museum?
fact: The empty frames were left hanging on the museum's walls.

text: Hermann Göring was taken in by Dutch forger Han van Meegeren's fake of which old master?
fact: Arrested for aiding the enemy, he confessed that he had painted it himself.

text: What kind of shark floats in the tank of formaldehyde in Damien Hirst's famous 1991 work?
fact: The first shark was caught off Hervey Bay in Queensland by a fisherman hired for the job.

text: In 2010 Ai Weiwei covered a London gallery floor with 100 million porcelain copies of what?
fact: Each one was made by hand in Jingdezhen, known as China's porcelain capital.

text: Which artist won the Archibald, Wynne and Sulman prizes all in the same year, 1978?
fact: His Archibald winner that year was called Art, Life and the Other Thing.

text: The Western Desert dot painting movement began in 1971 at which Northern Territory community?
fact: It grew out of a school mural project led by the teacher Geoffrey Bardon.

text: The Japanese art term ukiyo-e translates as 'pictures of' what?
Which architect designed the glass pyramid that opened at the Louvre in 1989?
In November 2025 a portrait by which artist fetched US$236 million, then an auction record for modern art?
fact: Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer was sold by Sotheby's in New York.

text: How many panels make up a triptych?
fact: The panels are often hinged together.

text: How many apostles sit with Jesus in Leonardo da Vinci's The Last Supper?
In what year did Vincent van Gogh die?
fact: He was 37.

text: In what year did MONA, the Museum of Old and New Art, open in Hobart?
fact: It opened on 21 January, within the Moorilla winery on the Berriedale peninsula.

text: In what year did London's Tate Modern open?
fact: It is housed in the former Bankside Power Station.

text: Hokusai's Great Wave belongs to a series named after how many views of Mount Fuji?
fact: The series sold so well that ten more prints were added, making 46.

text: In what year was the first Impressionist exhibition held in Paris?
fact: It was held in the former studio of the photographer Nadar.

text: In what year was the National Gallery of Victoria founded?
fact: It is Australia's oldest public art museum.

text: How old was the New York painter Jean-Michel Basquiat when he died in 1988?
fact: He first made his name in the late 1970s with graffiti signed SAMO.

Put these Australian artists in order of birth, earliest first.

text: What did Abel Tasman name the island we now call Tasmania?
fact: The name honoured Anthony van Diemen, who ran the Dutch East Indies and sent him.

text: Which governor, once cast adrift by the Bounty mutineers, was overthrown in the Rum Rebellion?
fact: The NSW Corps marched on Government House on 26 January 1808 and arrested him.

text: In 1813, Blaxland, Lawson and Wentworth found a route for settlers across what?
fact: They kept to the ridges instead of the valleys and were across in three weeks.

text: Which prime minister delivered the National Apology to the Stolen Generations in 2008?
fact: He moved the apology in the House of Representatives on 13 February 2008.

text: Gough Whitlam, 1975: "Well may we say God save the Queen, because nothing will save the..." what?
fact: He said it on the steps of Parliament House on 11 November, hours after being dismissed.

text: In May 2000, about 250,000 people walked across which landmark in support of reconciliation?
fact: So many people came that the walk, on 28 May, took nearly six hours.

text: On the night of 31 May 1942, what slipped into Sydney Harbour and attacked ships?
fact: Three took part. A torpedo fired at the cruiser USS Chicago sank the depot ship Kuttabul.

text: At the Sydney 2000 closing ceremony, IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch called the Games what?
fact: They were his last Games as president of the IOC.

text: Cobb & Co, started in gold-rush Melbourne by the young American Freeman Cobb, was famous for what?
fact: Its first coaches ran to the diggings in January 1854. The last ran in Queensland in 1924.

text: Mungo Lady and Mungo Man, some 40,000 years old, were found in which present-day state?
fact: Mungo Lady's cremation is among the oldest known. Mungo Man was returned to Country in 2017.

text: At Budj Bim in Victoria, the Gunditjmara built stone channels and weirs to trap and farm what?
fact: Parts of the system are at least 6,600 years old. It joined the World Heritage List in 2019.

text: Which Wangal man, a go-between for Governor Phillip, sailed with him to England in 1792?
fact: He and Yemmerrawanne left on the Atlantic in December 1792 and landed in May 1793.

text: Which French explorer sailed into Botany Bay in January 1788, just days after the First Fleet?
fact: His two ships were sighted on 24 January and entered the bay two days later.

text: The Castle Hill convict uprising of 1804 was led by men transported after a 1798 rebellion where?
fact: Its last fight was nicknamed Australia's Vinegar Hill, after a battle of the 1798 rising.

text: Who led the rebel miners at the Eureka Stockade and lost an arm in the fight?
fact: He went on to be Speaker of Victoria's Legislative Assembly in the 1880s.

text: Henry Parkes gave his famous 1889 speech calling for federation in which NSW town?
fact: He spoke at the town's School of Arts on 24 October 1889.

text: The Immigration Restriction Act 1901 let officials keep out unwanted migrants by setting what?
fact: An officer could dictate 50 words in any European language he chose.

text: In a 1933 referendum, which state voted about two to one to leave the Commonwealth?
fact: About two-thirds voted to go, but secession never happened.

text: During the Great Depression of the 1930s, what was "the susso"?
fact: It is short for "sustenance". A song of the time went "We're on the susso now".
wrong: A shanty town for the homeless

text: In August 1944, hundreds of Japanese prisoners of war broke out of a camp near which NSW town?
fact: The breakout began in the early hours of 5 August, when a prisoner sounded a bugle.

text: The "Dollar Bill" jingle that taught Australians about decimal currency was sung to which folk tune?
fact: Ted Roberts wrote the words. The new money arrived on 14 February 1966.

text: Which diplomat from the Soviet embassy in Canberra defected in 1954, setting off a royal commission?
fact: His wife, Evdokia, defected later that month at Darwin airport.

text: As a boy in Bowral, Don Bradman sharpened his batting by hitting a golf ball with what?
fact: He hit the ball against the brick base of the family's water tank.

text: Which cyclone hit far north Queensland in March 2006 and destroyed most of Australia's banana crop?
fact: It crossed the coast near Innisfail on 20 March. Bananas were scarce for the rest of the year.

text: A 2017 study dated human occupation of which Northern Territory rock shelter to about 65,000 years ago?
fact: It lies on Mirarr country, in the Kakadu region of the Top End.

text: In 1963, Yolngu people sent bark petitions to federal parliament from which Arnhem Land community?
fact: They were protesting a bauxite mine on their land. Two are on show in Parliament House.

text: Before 1907, Makasar crews from Sulawesi sailed to Arnhem Land each year mainly to gather what?
fact: The catch, known as trepang, was dried and sold on to China.

text: Before settling on Botany Bay, what did James Cook first call the bay in his journal?
fact: He renamed it for the great quantity of new plants that Banks and Solander collected there.

text: Mary Reibey, the businesswoman on the $20 note, was sentenced to transportation at 13 for stealing what?
fact: She was arrested dressed as a boy, under the name James Burrow.

text: To dodge Victoria's tax on Chinese arrivals, thousands of gold seekers landed at which SA port and walked?
fact: From 1855, Victoria charged ten pounds for every Chinese passenger a ship landed.

text: The bushranger Frederick Ward, shot near Uralla in 1870, was better known by what name?
fact: He had escaped from the prison on Cockatoo Island, in Sydney Harbour, in 1863.

text: Which judge handed down the Harvester Judgement of 1907, setting a basic wage for workers?
fact: He set it at seven shillings a day, enough to keep a family of five.

text: Which suffragist ran for the Senate in Victoria in 1903, the first federal election women could contest?
fact: The four women who stood were the first in the Empire to run for a national parliament.

text: Who was Phar Lap's strapper, at the champion's side when he died in 1932?
fact: Telford trained him, Pike rode him in the Melbourne Cup and Davis owned him.

text: Which town was moved in the 1950s to make way for the Snowy scheme's Lake Eucumbene?
fact: Buildings were trucked to a new site. Ruins of the old town reappear in droughts.

text: Who took charge of the relief effort in Darwin in the days after Cyclone Tracy?
fact: A major-general, he headed the Natural Disasters Organisation, set up earlier that year.

text: In the 1950s and 60s, how many pounds did a British adult pay for an assisted passage to Australia?
fact: Hence the nickname "Ten Pound Poms".

text: How many British colonies joined together to form the Commonwealth of Australia?
fact: Each colony became a state of the new nation.

text: In what year did work begin on the Snowy Mountains Hydro-Electric Scheme?
fact: The first blast was fired on 17 October. The scheme was finished in 1974.

text: In what year did regular television broadcasts begin in Australia?
fact: Bruce Gyngell opened on TCN-9 Sydney with "Good evening, and welcome to television".

text: In what year was Newcastle, NSW, struck by a deadly earthquake?
fact: It struck at 10.27 am on 28 December.

text: In what year did the last convict ship to Australia, the Hougoumont, arrive at Fremantle?
fact: Its arrival ended 80 years of convict transportation to Australia.

text: In what year was Canberra officially given its name?
fact: Lady Denman announced the name on 12 March, at a ceremony on what is now Capital Hill.

text: In what year did Australia's road signs and speed limits switch from miles to kilometres?
fact: The switch began on 1 July, and signs on major roads were to be replaced within the month.

text: In what year was the title to Uluru handed back to its Anangu traditional owners?
fact: Sir Ninian Stephen handed over the title deeds at the base of the rock on 26 October.

Put these moments in the First Nations rights movement in order, earliest first.

text: Put these in order of becoming a colony in their own right, earliest first.
Slim Dusty's 1957 hit is about a pub with no what?
fact: It was the first Australian single to earn a gold record, and it reached No. 3 in the UK.

text: Chrissy Amphlett sang I Touch Myself as the frontwoman of which band?
fact: The band formed in Sydney in 1980 around Amphlett and guitarist Mark McEntee.

text: Crowded House said farewell in 1996 with a huge concert on the steps of which building?
fact: Rain pushed the show back a day, to 24 November. More than 100,000 people came.

text: 5 Seconds of Summer got their big break in 2013 opening for which band on a world tour?
fact: The support slot was announced on 14 February 2013, Valentine's Day.

text: Am I Ever Gonna See Your Face Again, famous for the crowd's shouted reply, is by which band?
fact: The single came out in 1976. Singer Doc Neeson first heard the crowd's reply in 1983.

text: Which Australian pop star became famous for performing behind a huge wig that hid her face?
fact: She took up the wig for her album 1000 Forms of Fear, to protect her privacy.

text: Which ABC show began playing music videos through the night on weekends in 1987?
fact: It first went to air on Friday 17 April 1987.

text: Jessica Mauboy first found fame in 2006 as the runner-up on which TV show?
fact: She was born and raised in Darwin. Damien Leith won that season.

text: Melbourne's G Flip is best known for singing while playing which instrument?
fact: They started playing at the age of nine. Their 2023 album is called Drummer.

text: Country star Keith Urban, raised in Queensland, was born in which country?
fact: He was born in Whangārei in 1967 and moved to Caboolture at the age of two.

text: Gotye came to Australia as a toddler. In which country was he born?
fact: He was born Wouter De Backer in Bruges in 1980, and goes by Wally.

text: Fans of Paul Kelly's How to Make Gravy mark 'Gravy Day' on which date?
fact: It is the date on which Joe, the song's narrator, writes his letter home from prison.

text: Royel Otis went viral in 2024 with a Like a Version cover of which song?
fact: Their take on the Sophie Ellis-Bextor hit later reached No. 1 on US alternative radio.
wrong: Can't Get You Out of My Head

text: At the Sydney 2000 closing ceremony, Midnight Oil played in black outfits printed with which word?
fact: They played Beds Are Burning. The government had refused to apologise to the Stolen Generations.

text: Tina Arena first became famous as a child star of which TV show?
fact: She was on the show from 1976 to 1983, where she was known as Tiny Tina.

text: In 1977 Molly Meldrum famously fumbled a Countdown interview with which royal?
fact: A nervous Meldrum told him he had seen 'your mum' in a carriage in London.

text: Which song topped Triple J's Hottest 100 of Australian Songs in July 2025?
fact: More than 2.65 million votes were cast. The three wrong answers all made the top five.

text: Which Courtney Barnett song is about house hunting in Melbourne's northern suburbs?
fact: It is on her 2015 debut album, Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit.

text: Before his solo career, Daryl Braithwaite was the lead singer of which 1970s pop band?
fact: He joined the band in March 1970, at the age of 21.

text: Harley Streten is the real name of which electronic producer?
fact: He was born in Sydney in 1991 and grew up on the Northern Beaches.

text: Which Archie Roach song, his debut single, tells the story of the Stolen Generations?
fact: Archie Roach, a Gunditjmara and Bundjalung man, was himself taken from his family as a child.

text: Rapper Iggy Azalea grew up in which northern NSW town?
fact: She was born in Sydney as Amethyst Kelly. Her single Fancy topped the US chart in 2014.

text: Which band's Cartoon Darkness won the ARIA for Album of the Year in 2025?
fact: The band won four awards on the night, at the Hordern Pavilion in Sydney.

text: The five Easybeats, all migrants from Europe, met in 1964 at which Sydney migrant hostel?
fact: Two were born in England, two in the Netherlands and one in Scotland.

text: A song by which band was the first ever played on Double J, the station that became Triple J?
fact: The song, You Just Like Me 'Cos I'm Good in Bed, had been banned by commercial radio.

text: Silverchair's demo of Tomorrow won a national contest run by Triple J and which SBS TV show?
fact: The contest was called Pick Me. The band was still known as Innocent Criminals.

text: Savage Garden took their name from a phrase in the novels of which author?
fact: The phrase comes from her Vampire Chronicles.

text: How did Regurgitator record their 2004 album Mish Mash!?
fact: The 'Band in a Bubble' sat in Melbourne's Federation Square for three weeks.
answer: Sealed in a public glass studio

text: Before music, Vance Joy played for which club in the VFL, Victoria's state football league?
fact: Under his real name, James Keogh, he was the club's best first-year player in 2008.

text: The 1991 dance remix that made a hit of Yothu Yindi's Treaty was by which Melbourne team?
fact: The remix reached No. 11 on the ARIA chart. The original single had not charted.

text: Gurrumul was born and raised on which island off the coast of Arnhem Land?
fact: Born blind, the Gumatj singer was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame in 2026.

text: Kasey Chambers spent much of her childhood with her family living and hunting where?
fact: Her parents hunted foxes and rabbits there for their pelts. She was born in Mount Gambier.

text: The sudden closure of which Melbourne pub in January 2010 set off rallies in defence of live music?
fact: Thousands filled the Collingwood streets outside. The pub reopened that June.

text: Midnight Oil's Blue Sky Mine is about the asbestos miners of which Western Australian town?
fact: The 'blue' is blue asbestos. It was the first single from the album Blue Sky Mining.

text: Icehouse's 1987 hit Electric Blue was co-written by Iva Davies and which American musician?
fact: It reached No. 1 in Australia and No. 7 in the US.

text: The Falls Festival began as Rock Above the Falls, outside which Victorian coastal town?
In what year did Sia release her hit single Chandelier?
fact: It was the first single from her album 1000 Forms of Fear and reached No. 2 in Australia.

text: In what year did Australia first compete at Eurovision, with Guy Sebastian singing Tonight Again?
fact: He went straight into the final and finished fifth.

text: In what year did Kylie Minogue play the Sunday 'legends' slot at Glastonbury?
fact: She had been booked to headline the festival in 2005 but had to pull out.

text: Double J, the station that became Triple J, began broadcasting in what year?
fact: It went to air in Sydney on 19 January, on the AM band, under the call sign 2JJ.

text: In what year did Powderfinger play their farewell Sunsets tour?
fact: The last show was at Brisbane's Riverstage on 13 November.

text: In what year were the Sound Relief benefit concerts held at the MCG and the SCG?
fact: Held on 14 March, they raised money after the Victorian bushfires and Queensland floods.

text: In what year did Johnny O'Keefe release Wild One, later a hit for Iggy Pop as Real Wild Child?
fact: Its release, on 5 July, is often called the birth of Australian rock and roll.

text: In what year was the first Sunbury Pop Festival held, on a farm outside Melbourne?
fact: It ran each Australia Day long weekend until 1975. Deep Purple headlined the last one.

text: The ARIA Hall of Fame began with six inductees, among them AC/DC and Slim Dusty. In what year?
fact: Joan Sutherland, Johnny O'Keefe and Col Joye were among the others.

text: Who was Australia's first prime minister, sworn in on 1 January 1901?
fact: He left in 1903 to become one of the first three judges of the High Court.

text: Who became Australia's first female prime minister in June 2010?
fact: She was sworn in on 24 June 2010 by the Governor-General, Quentin Bryce.

text: What is the name of the prime minister's official residence in Canberra?
fact: It was finished in 1927. Kirribilli House is the prime minister's Sydney residence.

text: On election day, what is a "democracy sausage"?
fact: The Australian National Dictionary Centre made it the word of the year for 2016.
answer: A snag sold at a polling place
wrong: A free lunch for new MPs

text: Which prime minister disappeared while swimming at Cheviot Beach, Victoria, in December 1967?
fact: He had been prime minister for a little under two years.

text: Which prime minister served the longest, with more than 18 years in the job across two stints?
fact: He held the office from 1939 to 1941 and again from 1949 to 1966.

text: By law, on which day of the week must a federal election be held?
fact: The very first federal election, in 1901, was spread over a Friday and a Saturday.

text: Which Labor leader won the 1972 federal election with the slogan "It's Time"?
fact: The win ended 23 years of Coalition government.

text: What do Australians call a ballot paper numbered 1, 2, 3 straight down the page?
fact: If every box is numbered as the rules require, it still counts as a formal vote.

text: Which prime minister gave the Redfern speech in Sydney in December 1992?
fact: He gave it in Redfern Park on 10 December to launch the Year of the World's Indigenous People.

text: After the 1983 America's Cup win, which PM said any boss who sacked a worker for skipping work was "a bum"?
fact: He said it at Royal Perth Yacht Club early on 27 September 1983, Perth time.

text: In 1943, who became the first woman elected to the House of Representatives?
fact: Dorothy Tangney won a Senate seat at the same election.

text: Who in 1990 became the first woman to be premier of an Australian state?
fact: She led Western Australia from February 1990. Victoria's Joan Kirner followed in August.

text: Which museum opened in Old Parliament House in Canberra in 2009?
fact: Federal Parliament sat in the building for 61 years, until 1988.

text: Which ABC chief election analyst stepped down from his on-air role after the 2025 federal election?
fact: He first appeared on air at the 1991 New South Wales election.

text: Don Chipp founded which party, promising to "keep the bastards honest"?
fact: Chipp was a former Liberal minister. The party was launched in 1977.

text: Which architect won the 1912 international competition to design Canberra?
fact: His was entry No. 29 of 137. His wife, Marion Mahony Griffin, drew the plans.

text: Which term for the closed world of federal politics was the National Dictionary Centre's 2018 word of the year?
In Question Time, what is a "Dorothy Dixer"?
fact: The name comes from Dorothy Dix, an American advice columnist.

text: In the final ballot of the August 2018 Liberal leadership spill, whom did Scott Morrison defeat?
fact: The vote was 45 to 40. Julie Bishop had gone out in the first round.

text: Who in 2010 became the first Indigenous member of the House of Representatives?
fact: He won the WA seat of Hasluck and gave his first speech in a kangaroo-skin cloak.

text: Which prime minister lost his own seat of Bennelong at the 2007 federal election?
fact: He had held the Sydney seat since 1974. Labor's Maxine McKew won it.

text: Up to 2025, a joint sitting to pass blocked bills had followed only one double dissolution. In which year?
fact: The sitting, on 6 and 7 August 1974, passed all six bills put to it.

text: Which caretaker prime minister served for about a week in July 1945, after John Curtin died?
fact: Up to 2025, his 6 to 13 July stint was the shortest term of any prime minister.

text: In 1904, who became Australia's first Labor prime minister?
fact: He took office at 37, and no PM up to 2025 was younger. He was probably born in Valparaíso, Chile.

text: Which prime minister, sworn in in January 1968, was a senator at the time?
fact: Up to 2025 he was the only PM sworn in while a senator. He soon won the lower house seat of Higgins.

text: In 1929 Stanley Bruce became the first sitting prime minister to lose his own seat. Which seat?
fact: He won it back in 1931, then resigned in 1933 to be High Commissioner in London.

text: In the "Hopetoun Blunder" of December 1900, which premier was first asked to form a federal government?
fact: He was premier of NSW. Unable to find ministers to serve under him, he gave up the task.

text: Who in 1931 became the first Australian-born Governor-General?
fact: He was Chief Justice of the High Court when James Scullin put his name to the King.

text: Who in 1987 became the first woman appointed to the High Court of Australia?
fact: She sat on the court until 2003.

text: After the 2010 election, which independent ended a 17-minute speech by backing a Labor government?
fact: Tony Windsor spoke first, for about five minutes. It was 17 days after polling day.

text: In the 1983 miniseries The Dismissal, who played Gough Whitlam?
fact: John Meillon played Sir John Kerr and John Stanton played Malcolm Fraser.

text: As of 2025, Tasmania's lower house and the ACT Assembly were both elected by which voting system?
fact: It is named after English lawyer Thomas Hare and Tasmania's Andrew Inglis Clark.

text: Which NSW seat was won by the party forming government at every election from 1972 to 2013?
fact: The run ended in 2016, when Labor took the seat but the Coalition kept government.

text: Which NSW governor dismissed Premier Jack Lang in May 1932?
fact: Up to 2025, Lang was the only state premier to have been dismissed by a governor.

text: The Tree of Knowledge, where striking shearers met in 1891, stood in which Queensland town?
fact: Labor folklore treats the ghost gum as the birthplace of the party.

text: From what age can Australians vote in federal elections?
fact: It was lowered from 21 in 1973.

text: In what year did Anthony Albanese become prime minister?
fact: Labor won the election on 21 May and he was sworn in two days later.

text: In what year was the "misogyny speech" delivered in the House of Representatives?
fact: Soon afterwards the Macquarie Dictionary widened its definition of misogyny.

text: From 1906 to 2023, Australians voted on 45 proposals to change the Constitution. How many passed?
fact: The last of the eight to pass were three proposals put to the people in 1977.

text: How many seats were there in the House of Representatives at the 2025 federal election?
fact: There had been 151 at the 2022 election.

text: From 1901 to 2025, how many Australian prime ministers died while in office?
fact: The first was Joseph Lyons, in April 1939.

text: What is the number of the section of the Constitution that sets out how it can be changed?
fact: It is headed "Mode of altering the Constitution".

text: Before 2010, in what year did a federal election last produce a hung parliament?
fact: Two Victorian independents, Arthur Coles and Alex Wilson, held the balance of power.

text: The Constitution says the national capital must be at least how many miles from Sydney?
fact: Section 125 also says the capital must be in New South Wales.

Put these political parties in order of founding, earliest first.
Put these Labor prime ministers in order of first taking office, earliest first.

The proclamation is read on the steps

text: "That's not a knife. That's a knife" is a line from which Australian film?
fact: Paul Hogan's Mick Dundee says it to a New York mugger armed with a switchblade.

text: In The Castle, where does Darryl Kerrigan say his favourite presents are going "straight to"?
fact: Michael Caton plays Darryl. Rob Sitch directed the film for Working Dog.

text: Which Home and Away character is known for saying "stone the flamin' crows"?
fact: Ray Meagher first played him in the show's pilot, which aired in January 1988.

text: What breed of dog is Bluey?
fact: Joe Brumm created the show, which is made by Ludo Studio in Queensland.

text: In the comedy Colin from Accounts, who or what is Colin?
fact: Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer, who are married, created the show and play the leads.

text: In the film Lion, what does Saroo use to track down his childhood home in India?
fact: Dev Patel plays the adult Saroo, who was raised in Hobart by Sue and John Brierley.

text: A farmer tells his sheep-herding animal "That'll do, pig" in which Australian-made film?
fact: James Cromwell plays Farmer Hoggett. It was filmed around Robertson in NSW.

text: Margot Robbie spent three years as Donna Freedman on which Australian soap?
fact: She was in the show from 2008 to 2011.

text: Play School's three "magic windows" were round, square and which other shape?
fact: The original windows are now in the National Museum of Australia.

text: Which ABBA song do Muriel and Rhonda mime to at a resort talent contest in Muriel's Wedding?
fact: Toni Collette plays Muriel and Rachel Griffiths plays Rhonda. P. J. Hogan directed.

text: Geoffrey Rush won the Best Actor Oscar for playing which pianist in Shine?
fact: Noah Taylor plays him as a teenager. Scott Hicks directed.

text: Cate Blanchett won the Best Actress Oscar for which film?
fact: She plays Jasmine, a former socialite. It was her second Oscar.

text: Nicole Kidman was born in which city?
fact: Her first films, both in 1983, were Bush Christmas and BMX Bandits.

text: Mad Max: Fury Road was mostly filmed in the desert of which country?
fact: Heavy rain had covered the planned location near Broken Hill in wildflowers.

text: Neighbours ended in July 2022. Which company brought it back the following year?
fact: Amazon's revival began in September 2023 and ran until December 2025.

text: Which Blue Heelers star won the Gold Logie four years running, from 1997 to 2000?
fact: She played Maggie Doyle.

text: Which ABC comedian won the Gold Logie in 2019?
fact: He was nominated for Hard Quiz, which he began hosting in 2016.

text: The music quiz Spicks and Specks takes its name from a song by which band?
fact: Adam Hills hosted the 2005 to 2011 run, with Myf Warhurst and Alan Brough as team captains.

text: Foxtel's drama Wentworth was a modern reimagining of which earlier Australian series?
fact: Wentworth began on the SoHo channel and ended in 2021 with its 100th episode.

text: Who played the hard-living Sydney barrister Cleaver Greene in Rake?
fact: Rake ran for five series on the ABC, from 2010 to 2018.

text: Jacki Weaver was Oscar-nominated for playing crime matriarch "Smurf" Cody in which film?
fact: David Michôd's film had a record 18 nominations at the 2010 AFI Awards and won 10.

text: Who played ballroom rebel Scott Hastings in Strictly Ballroom?
fact: Tara Morice played Fran, the beginner who becomes his partner.

text: Baz Luhrmann's Elvis (2022) was filmed in which Australian city?
fact: It was made at Village Roadshow Studios, with Austin Butler as Elvis.

text: Russell Crowe and Jane Campion were both born in which city?
fact: Campion was born there in 1954 and Crowe in 1964.

text: Who directed Babe?
fact: George Miller co-wrote and produced it. It earned seven Oscar nominations.

text: Who sang the original Neighbours theme song?
fact: He sang it on the show from 1985 to 1992. Tony Hatch and Jackie Trent wrote the song.

text: Diver Dan's boatshed in SeaChange is in which Victorian seaside town?
fact: The show's town was called Pearl Bay. Sigrid Thornton starred as Laura Gibson.

text: Who played bad boy Bogdan Drazic in the original Heartbreak High?
fact: He joined in 1997 for the fifth series, the first to air on the ABC rather than Ten.

text: In 2007 The Chaser drove a fake motorcade into Sydney's APEC security zone. Which country's was it meant to be?
fact: All charges against the team were dropped in April 2008.

text: SBS's RocKwiz was recorded in the Gershwin Room of which Melbourne pub?
fact: Julia Zemiro hosted and Brian Nankervis kept score at the St Kilda pub known as the Espy.

text: Before his film career, Eric Bana was a writer and performer on which sketch comedy show?
fact: He joined in 1993, after his TV debut on Steve Vizard's Tonight Live.

text: David McCormack, the voice of Bandit in Bluey, fronts which Brisbane band?
fact: Melanie Zanetti voices Bluey's mum, Chilli.

text: Hugh Jackman's first big TV job was in which 1995 ABC drama set in a prison?
fact: It ran for 10 episodes, with Deborra-Lee Furness as a prison psychologist.

text: Which film won Best Film at the first AACTA Awards, held in January 2012?
fact: The awards took over from the AFI Awards. Snowtown won the most overall, with six.

text: As of the 2026 Oscars, which designer holds the most wins by an Australian, with four?
fact: She won two each for Moulin Rouge! and The Great Gatsby, for her costumes and her sets.

text: Skippy the Bush Kangaroo was set in which fictional national park?
fact: Garry Pankhurst played Sonny Hammond. The show ran to 91 episodes.

text: How many Hemsworth brothers are actors?
fact: Luke is the eldest, then Chris, then Liam.

text: In what year was Mad Max: Fury Road released?
fact: It came 30 years after the third film, Beyond Thunderdome.

text: In Picnic at Hanging Rock, in what year do the schoolgirls vanish on Valentine's Day?
fact: The film is based on Joan Lindsay's 1967 novel.

text: In what year was The Castle released?
fact: It opened in Australian cinemas on 10 April.

text: In what year was The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert released?
fact: Terence Stamp, Hugo Weaving and Guy Pearce star. Stephan Elliott wrote and directed.

text: In what year did Australian TV stations make the full switch to colour?
fact: C-Day, the official start, was 1 March. Stations had run colour test patterns since October 1974.

text: In what year did Hey Hey It's Saturday end its original run on Nine?
fact: The last show was on 20 November. It came back for two reunion specials in 2009.

text: How many episodes of Blue Heelers were made?
fact: That equalled Homicide's record for an Australian weekly prime-time drama.

text: In what year did Kylie Minogue win the Gold Logie?
fact: The Gold Logie goes to the most popular personality on Australian television.
