Cafe owners in which two countries both claim to have invented the flat white?
Which country has been the world's biggest coffee grower for about 150 years?
fact: It grows about a third of the world's coffee.

text: The croissant takes its name from the French word for which shape?
fact: It was modelled on the kipferl, a curved roll from Austria.

text: In Hindi, what does the word "chai" simply mean?
fact: The spiced, milky drink is masala chai, which means spiced tea.

text: A babycino is a small cup of what, usually dusted with chocolate?
Which Hollywood actor became the face of Nespresso's advertising in 2006?
The cappuccino is named after the brown robes of which religious order?
fact: Vienna's coffee houses were serving a "Kapuziner" in the 1700s.

text: "Macchiato", as in a caffè macchiato, is Italian for what?
fact: The stain is a dash of milk, usually foamed, on a shot of espresso.

text: On an espresso machine, what is the handled basket that holds the ground coffee called?
fact: It locks into the group head, where hot water is forced through the coffee.

text: Kopi luwak is made from coffee cherries eaten and passed by which animal?
fact: It comes mainly from the Indonesian islands of Sumatra, Java, Bali and Sulawesi.

text: According to legend, the goatherd Kaldi discovered coffee after noticing what?
fact: The tale first appeared in print in 1671, in a Latin treatise published in Rome.

text: Starbucks takes its name from the first mate in which novel?
The Coffee Club opened its first cafe in 1989 in which Australian city?
fact: The first store was at Eagle Street Pier.

text: Traditional Vietnamese iced coffee is sweetened with what?
fact: It is brewed through a small metal drip filter called a phin.

text: Which coffee species has almost twice the caffeine of arabica?
fact: Its beans run to about 2.7% caffeine; arabica beans to about 1.5%.

text: Tiramisu, the coffee-soaked dessert, has an Italian name meaning what?
A friand, the little cake of Australian cafe counters, is classically made with which nut meal?
fact: The other main ingredients are egg whites, butter and icing sugar.

text: Dalgona coffee, the whipped craze of 2020, is named after a honeycomb toffee from which country?
Which business grew out of Edward Lloyd's London coffee house, opened in the 1680s?
fact: It was popular with ship owners and captains, and grew into Lloyd's of London.

text: Rooibos, or "red bush" tea, grows in which country?
fact: It is farmed in the Cederberg mountains, north of Cape Town, and has no caffeine.

text: In which country is "fika", a daily break for coffee and something sweet, a social institution?
What is a coffee cherry's single round seed, grown in place of the usual two, called?
fact: The Spanish name for it is caracolillo.

text: The prized Geisha coffee variety made its name in the 2000s on farms in which country?
fact: It came from Ethiopia's Gori Gesha forest. Hacienda La Esmeralda made it famous in 2004.

text: Which Italian's 1938 patent for a steam-free machine opened the way to high-pressure espresso?
Before the AeroPress, its inventor Alan Adler was best known for inventing what?
fact: The ring was the Aerobie, which he patented and sold in the 1980s.

text: In the Hario V60 pour-over dripper, what does the 60 stand for?
fact: Hario, a Japanese glassmaker, brought it out in 2005.

text: What is the small long-handled pot used to make Turkish coffee called?
fact: It is also known as an ibrik or a briki.

text: The frappé, iced coffee shaken to a foam from instant granules, is a cafe staple of which country?
fact: The usual story has it first shaken up at a trade fair in Thessaloniki in 1957.

text: England's 17th-century coffee houses have come to be known as "penny" what?
fact: A penny bought a coffee and a seat among the newspapers and the debate.

text: Caffeine keeps you alert by blocking the brain's receptors for which chemical?
fact: It is the chemical that would otherwise make you feel drowsy.

text: In Melbourne cafes, what do you get if you order a "magic"?
fact: It is served in a smaller cup than a flat white.

text: Which Australian won the World Barista Championship in 2003?
fact: Sestic (2015), Douglas (2022) and Simpson (2025) won it later.

text: In making matcha, what is a chasen?
fact: The bowl is a chawan and the scoop is a chashaku.

text: How many shots of espresso are in a doppio?
fact: Doppio is Italian for double.

text: The Starbucks cup size "venti" is the Italian word for which number?
fact: A hot venti holds 20 US fluid ounces.

text: About how many bars of pressure does a cafe espresso machine use to brew a shot?
fact: Italy's national espresso institute sets the standard at 9 bar, give or take 1.

text: In what year did Starbucks add the flat white to its menus in the United States?
fact: It went on sale in American stores on 6 January.

text: In what year did KeepCup launch its reusable coffee cup in Melbourne?
fact: Siblings Abigail and Jamie Forsyth started it after running cafes in the city.

text: In what year did Angelo Moriondo of Turin patent his steam-driven forerunner of the espresso machine?
fact: It won a bronze medal at that year's General Expo in Turin.

text: In what year did Caffè Florian open in St Mark's Square, Venice?
fact: It is the oldest coffee house in continuous operation in Italy.

text: In what year did Nestlé launch Nescafé instant coffee?
fact: It went on sale in Switzerland on 1 April.

text: Food safety agencies in the US and Europe put a safe daily caffeine limit for most adults at how many mg?
fact: Europe's food safety agency halves the figure, to 200 mg, during pregnancy.

text: Under what name did Muhammad Ali win Olympic gold in Rome in 1960?
fact: Born Cassius Marcellus Clay Jr, he won the light heavyweight gold.

text: Who did Muhammad Ali knock out in the Rumble in the Jungle?
fact: Ali won in the eighth round in Kinshasa, in what was then Zaire.

text: In 1986, who became the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history, aged 20?
fact: He was 20 years and four months old when he won the WBC belt.

text: Which Australian beat Manny Pacquiao at Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium in 2017?
fact: Horn won a unanimous decision and the WBO welterweight title in front of 51,052 people.

text: Which sport did Anthony Mundine play professionally before he turned to boxing in 2000?
fact: He played for St George and the Brisbane Broncos, then won the WBA super-middleweight title.

text: In 2016, who became the first fighter to hold UFC titles in two weight classes at the same time?
fact: Already featherweight champion, he stopped Eddie Alvarez for the lightweight belt at UFC 205.

text: Before her UFC career, Ronda Rousey won an Olympic bronze medal in which sport?
fact: Her bronze at Beijing 2008 was the first Olympic judo medal won by an American woman.

text: Which UFC fighter is nicknamed "The Last Stylebender"?
fact: The name is a nod to the cartoon series Avatar: The Last Airbender.

text: Which combat sport is known as "the art of eight limbs"?
fact: The eight limbs are the fists, elbows, knees and shins.

text: In 2024, who became boxing's first undisputed heavyweight champion of the four-belt era?
fact: He won a split decision in Riyadh to hold the WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO belts together.

text: Who handed Mike Tyson his first professional defeat, in Tokyo in 1990?
fact: Douglas was a 42-1 outsider and won by knockout in the tenth round.

text: Tyson Fury became unified heavyweight champion in Düsseldorf in 2015 by beating which fighter?
fact: Fury won a unanimous decision to take the WBA, IBF and WBO belts.

text: Under boxing's 10-point must system, how is a round with one knockdown usually scored?
fact: The winner of a round gets 10 points. A round with no knockdown is usually scored 10-9.

text: With what perfect professional record did Floyd Mayweather retire in 2017?
fact: That 50th win took him one past Rocky Marciano's famous 49-0 record.

text: George Kambosos Jr became unified lightweight world champion in New York in 2021 by beating whom?
fact: Kambosos won a split decision at Madison Square Garden's Hulu Theater in November 2021.

text: Which American great did Danny Green stop in the first round in Sydney in 2009?
fact: It was over in two minutes and two seconds. Green kept his IBO cruiserweight belt.

text: Which Australian won the WBC featherweight world title in Las Vegas in April 2024?
fact: She had won Commonwealth Games gold on the Gold Coast in 2018.

text: Who won the eight-man tournament at the first UFC event?
fact: He won the final with a rear-naked choke in under two minutes.

text: Robert Whittaker won the UFC interim middleweight title in 2017 by beating which fighter?
fact: Born in Auckland and raised in Sydney, he is billed by the UFC as Australia's first champion.

text: Who did Alexander Volkanovski beat at UFC 245 to win the featherweight title?
fact: Volkanovski, from Wollongong, won a unanimous decision in December 2019.

text: Jack Della Maddalena, who won the UFC welterweight title in 2025, comes from which city?
fact: He beat Belal Muhammad on points in Montreal at UFC 315.

text: Who ended Ronda Rousey's unbeaten run at UFC 193 in Melbourne in 2015?
fact: The crowd of 56,214 at Docklands Stadium was a UFC record at the time.

text: What is the highest rank in professional sumo?
fact: Below it, in order, come ozeki, sekiwake, komusubi and maegashira.

text: In judo, what is the highest score, which ends a contest at once?
fact: An ippon comes from a clean throw, a 20-second pin or a submission.

text: Which Australian knocked out Vic Toweel in round one in 1952 to win the world bantamweight title?
fact: It happened in Johannesburg. He stopped Toweel again there in a rematch four months later.

text: Who did Kostya Tszyu stop in two rounds in 2001 to unify the WBA, WBC and IBF light-welterweight titles?
fact: It happened at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas that November.

text: Who won the world heavyweight title at Sydney Stadium on Boxing Day 1908?
fact: Johnson beat Canada's Tommy Burns to become the first Black world heavyweight champion.

text: Harry Garside's bronze at Tokyo 2020 was Australia's first Olympic boxing medal since which Games?
fact: Grahame Cheney won light welterweight silver in Seoul.

text: Who beat Muhammad Ali in his final fight, in the Bahamas in 1981?
fact: The ten-round bout in Nassau was billed as the "Drama in Bahama".

text: Jon Jones became the UFC's youngest champion, aged 23, by beating which fighter?
fact: Jones stopped him in the third round at UFC 128 to take the light heavyweight title.

text: Which strike, long banned under MMA's unified rules, became legal from November 2024?
fact: The name comes from a clock face: the elbow travels straight down from 12 to 6.

text: Which Japanese MMA promotion did the UFC's owners buy in 2007?
fact: The Fertitta brothers announced the deal in March 2007.

text: Which US city hosted the first UFC event, in 1993?
fact: UFC 1 was held at the McNichols Sports Arena on 12 November 1993.

text: Which American ended Aleksandr Karelin's 13-year unbeaten run to win wrestling gold at Sydney 2000?
fact: It was the Greco-Roman 130 kg final. Karelin had won the previous three Olympic titles.

text: Which New Zealander won kickboxing's K-1 World Grand Prix in Tokyo in 2001?
fact: The "Super Samoan" went on to fight in the UFC from 2010 to 2018.

text: What is the ritual dance performed before a Muay Thai fight called?
fact: The mongkhon is the headband worn into the ring, and the pra jiad are the armbands.

text: How many rounds is a men's world title fight in boxing scheduled for?
fact: Title fights were once 15 rounds. The WBC cut its bouts to 12 from 1983.

text: How many minutes does one round last in a UFC fight?
fact: Most fights are three rounds. Title fights and main events are five.

text: How old was George Foreman when he knocked out Michael Moorer in November 1994 to regain the heavyweight title?
fact: He took Moorer's WBA and IBF belts, almost 22 years after first winning the title in 1973.

text: How many fights did Khabib Nurmagomedov win in his unbeaten MMA career?
fact: He retired as UFC lightweight champion in October 2020.

text: In what year were Olympic medals first awarded in women's boxing?
fact: It joined the programme in London, 108 years after men's boxing.

text: How many times in a row did Joe Louis successfully defend his world heavyweight title?
fact: The "Brown Bomber" was champion from 1937 to 1949.

text: Manny Pacquiao was the first boxer to win world titles in how many weight divisions?
fact: He entered the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2025, in his first year of eligibility.

text: For how many days did Anderson Silva hold the UFC middleweight title?
fact: His reign ran from UFC 64 in October 2006 to UFC 162 in July 2013.

text: In what year did the UFC hold its first event in Australia?
fact: UFC 110 was held at Sydney's Acer Arena in February of that year.

fact: They play most of their home games at Bellerive Oval.

What is an over called in which no runs are scored against the bowler?
fact: Byes and leg byes don't count against the bowler, so a maiden can still include them.

text: Which ground is known as the "Home of Cricket"?
fact: It belongs to the MCC, the club that still writes the Laws of Cricket.

text: Ellyse Perry has also played for Australia at a World Cup in which other sport?
fact: She scored for the Matildas against Sweden in the 2011 World Cup quarter-final.

text: Which former Australian captain became the cream-jacketed voice of Channel Nine's cricket?
fact: Kerry Packer suggested the jacket so he would stand out from the other commentators.

text: Bradman's 1948 side went through its whole tour of England unbeaten. What is it known as?
fact: They played 34 matches on the tour, winning 25 and drawing nine.

text: Who captained India to its first men's World Cup title in 1983?
fact: India beat the West Indies by 43 runs at Lord's after making just 183.

text: Who captained Australia to the 2020 Women's T20 World Cup title at the MCG?
fact: The crowd of 86,174 set a record for a women's sporting event in Australia.

text: Which England bowler was hit for six sixes in an over by Yuvraj Singh in 2007?
fact: It was the first time anyone had hit six sixes in an over in a T20 international.

text: Test cricket's first tie, at the Gabba in 1960, was between Australia and which team?
fact: The second tied Test came in 1986: India v Australia in Madras.

text: In the 2007 World Cup final, Adam Gilchrist made 149 with what tucked inside his glove?
fact: The MCC ruled it broke neither the Laws nor the spirit of the game.

text: Which fast bowler was nicknamed the "Rawalpindi Express"?
fact: He was clocked at 161.3 km/h against England at the 2003 World Cup.

text: Who made 84 not out to help England tie the 2019 World Cup final at Lord's?
fact: The Super Over was also tied, so England won on boundary count.

text: Running out a non-striker who leaves the crease early is often named after which Indian?
fact: He ran out Australia's Bill Brown that way in the Sydney Test of December 1947.

text: In 2023, Angelo Mathews became the first international batter given out in which way?
fact: His helmet strap broke, and he wasn't ready to face within the two minutes allowed.

text: India beat which team in the final to win the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup?
fact: It was the first Women's World Cup final with neither Australia nor England in it.

text: Which team won the first Big Bash League title, in 2011-12?
fact: They beat the Perth Scorchers by seven wickets in the final at the WACA.

text: Which South African was run out to end the tied 1999 World Cup semi-final against Australia?
fact: Australia went through because they had finished above South Africa in the Super Sixes.

text: In cricket, a score of 111 is known by which name?
fact: Umpire David Shepherd would lift a foot off the ground on 111 to ward off bad luck.

text: The doosra, made famous by Saqlain Mushtaq, is bowled by which kind of bowler?
fact: Doosra means "second" or "other" in Hindi and Urdu.

text: Whose record Test score of 365 not out did Brian Lara beat in 1994?
fact: Sobers made it against Pakistan in Jamaica in 1958. Lara made 375.

text: In Test matches played in Australia in the 1960s, how many balls were in an over?
fact: Australia switched to six-ball overs for good in the 1979-80 season.

text: Belinda Clark made the first double century in ODI cricket in 1997. Against which team?
fact: She made 229 not out in Mumbai, over 12 years before any man made 200 in an ODI.

text: In 2014, Rohit Sharma set the record for an ODI innings with 264. Against which team?
fact: He hit 33 fours at Eden Gardens, passing Virender Sehwag's 219.

text: Which team won the first Women's Cricket World Cup, in 1973?
fact: It was held two years before the first men's World Cup.

text: Who made 171 not out against Australia in the 2017 Women's World Cup semi-final?
fact: She faced just 115 balls in a rain-shortened 42-over game at Derby.

text: At Eden Gardens in 2001, who made 281 after India were made to follow on against Australia?
fact: India won by 171 runs, ending Australia's record run of 16 straight Test wins.

text: In his final Test in 2016, Brendon McCullum hit a record 54-ball century against which team?
fact: It beat the 56-ball record shared by Viv Richards and Misbah-ul-Haq.

text: Which Zimbabwe player joined Henry Olonga in the black armband protest at the 2003 World Cup?
fact: They said they were mourning "the death of democracy" in Zimbabwe.

text: Which Irish batter hit a 50-ball century to beat England at the 2011 World Cup?
fact: Ireland were 111 for 5 chasing 328 before he finished on 113 off 63 balls.

text: In 1987, who became the first batter to reach 10,000 Test runs?
fact: He got there with a cut for two off Ijaz Faqih against Pakistan in Ahmedabad.

text: Under the Laws, at delivery, how many fielders other than the keeper may be behind the popping crease on the on side?
fact: Any more is a no-ball. The limit dates from 1957.

text: In 1990, who became the first bowler to take 400 Test wickets?
fact: He reached it against India in Christchurch and finished with 431.

text: The Basin Reserve Test ground is in which city?
fact: It first hosted a Test in 1930, against England.

text: In what year did the first Big Bash League season begin?
In what year did Australia win its first men's T20 World Cup?
fact: They beat New Zealand in the final in Dubai, with Mitchell Marsh player of the match.

text: How many wickets did Jim Laker take in the 1956 Old Trafford Test against Australia?
fact: He took 9 for 37 and 10 for 53, conceding 90 runs in all.

text: In a Test of five days, how big a first-innings lead lets a side enforce the follow-on?
By how many runs did England win the 2005 Ashes Test at Edgbaston?
fact: Michael Kasprowicz was last out, caught behind off Steve Harmison.

text: What is the highest team total in Test cricket, made by Sri Lanka against India in 1997?
fact: Sri Lanka declared at 952 for 6 in Colombo.

text: What is the lowest completed team total in Test cricket, made by New Zealand in 1955?
fact: England bowled them out at Eden Park, Auckland.

text: How many runs did Don Bradman score in his Test career?
fact: He made them in 52 Tests, with 29 centuries.

text: The first ODI was played at the MCG after a Test was washed out. In what year?
fact: Australia beat England by five wickets in a game of 40 eight-ball overs a side.

fact: The jury found him guilty on five counts. He later served time on Alcatraz.

text: The island prison of Alcatraz sits in the bay of which American city?
fact: The island is now a tourist site run by the US National Park Service.

text: Con man Victor Lustig is remembered as 'the man who sold' which landmark?
fact: The story has him posing as a French official in 1925 and inviting bids from scrap dealers.

text: Which kind of fraud did New York financier Bernie Madoff run for years?
fact: The judge who sentenced him called his crimes 'extraordinarily evil'.

text: Elizabeth Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors in which blood-testing company?
fact: A jury found her guilty on four counts in January 2022. An appeal court upheld that in 2025.

text: In the film Catch Me If You Can, who plays teenage con man Frank Abagnale?
fact: Tom Hanks plays the FBI agent chasing him. Steven Spielberg directed the 2002 film.

text: What did the hijacker known as D. B. Cooper do after collecting his ransom?
fact: He was never identified. The FBI stopped actively investigating in 2016.
wrong: Hid in the plane's cargo hold

text: Who played Mark 'Chopper' Read in the 2000 film Chopper?
fact: It was the first feature film by director Andrew Dominik.

text: Which Netflix series is about a young woman who conned New York's elite as a fake German heiress?
fact: Julia Garner plays Anna Sorokin, who went by the name Anna Delvey.

text: The pirate Blackbeard is usually identified as which man?
fact: Old records also spell his surname Thatch or Thack.

text: Great Train Robber Ronnie Biggs lived in which country for several years before fleeing to Brazil?
fact: He escaped from prison in 1965 with a rope ladder and later settled in Melbourne.

text: The Hatton Garden safe deposit burglary of 2015 was carried out over which long weekend?
fact: The gang used a heavy drill to bore through the wall of the vault.

text: What did the three prisoners who famously escaped Alcatraz use to make their raft?
fact: They left dummy heads with real hair in their beds to fool the guards.

text: Which sheriff shot the outlaw Billy the Kid in New Mexico?
fact: Billy the Kid is thought to have been born Henry McCarty. He also went by William Bonney.

text: The Brink's-Mat gang raided a Heathrow warehouse expecting cash. What did they find instead?
fact: There were about three tonnes of it, and most has never been recovered.

text: The Watergate burglars were caught inside the headquarters of which organisation?
fact: Five men were arrested. The scandal ended Richard Nixon's presidency.

text: The Somerton Man's scrap of paper reading 'Tamam Shud' was torn from a copy of which book?
fact: The Persian words mean 'ended' or 'finished'. He was found on an Adelaide beach.

text: Fine Cotton, at the centre of a famous Australian betting scandal, was what?
fact: A faster horse was painted to look like him and run in his place at Eagle Farm.

text: 'Stockholm syndrome' takes its name from a 1973 hostage siege at what kind of business?
fact: Four staff were held for six days at Kreditbanken on Norrmalmstorg square.

text: Alfred Dreyfus, the French officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894, was sent to which prison?
fact: The penal colony lay off French Guiana. Dreyfus was fully cleared in 1906.

text: What is unusual about the host of the hit Australian true-crime podcast Casefile?
fact: He says it keeps the focus on the victims and survivors.

text: The outlaws Bonnie and Clyde were killed in a police ambush in which US state?
fact: Their full names were Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow. They died in May 1934.

text: How did the thieves in the October 2025 Louvre jewel theft get up to the gallery's balcony window?
fact: They cut through the glass of the Galerie d'Apollon and were inside for about four minutes.
answer: A lift mounted on a truck

text: A half-eaten salami sandwich helped police catch the gang behind which heist?
fact: It lay in rubbish the thieves dumped beside a motorway. Most of the loot was never found.

text: Charles Ponzi told investors he was making huge profits by trading what?
fact: He worked out of Boston and paid early investors with newcomers' money.

text: Which bushranger led the gang that robbed the gold escort at Eugowra in NSW?
fact: His gang ambushed the gold coach from Forbes in June 1862 at what is now called Escort Rock.

text: After the Great Train Robbery, fingerprints on which board game helped police identify the gang?
fact: They had played it at their farm hideout, reportedly with real banknotes.

text: Ned Kelly's 56-page statement of 1879, defending his actions, is named after which NSW town?
fact: Kelly dictated it to gang member Joe Byrne. It is held by State Library Victoria.

text: What was the name of Blackbeard's flagship, which ran aground off North Carolina?
fact: The wreck was found in 1996 near Beaufort Inlet.

text: Robert Stroud, the 'Birdman of Alcatraz', actually kept his birds at which other prison?
fact: He raised canaries and wrote two books on their diseases. Alcatraz allowed him no birds.

text: Dr Crippen, fleeing to Canada by ship in 1910, was caught thanks to which new technology?
fact: The captain of the SS Montrose recognised him and sent a message back to Britain.

text: Before fingerprints took over, Alphonse Bertillon's system identified criminals mainly by what?
fact: He also standardised the police mug shot.

text: Bank robber John Dillinger was shot dead by federal agents outside which Chicago cinema?
fact: He had just watched the Clark Gable film Manhattan Melodrama.

text: Mata Hari, shot by a French firing squad as a German spy in 1917, was born in which country?
fact: Born Margaretha Zelle in Leeuwarden, she found fame across Europe as a dancer.

text: The 1925 Scopes 'Monkey Trial', over the teaching of evolution, was held in which US state?
fact: Teacher John Scopes was found guilty in the town of Dayton and fined $100.

text: Who shot the outlaw Jesse James dead, hoping to collect the reward on his head?
fact: Ford's brother Charley was in the gang. James died in St. Joseph, Missouri.

text: How many fugitives does the FBI's famous 'Most Wanted' list normally hold?
fact: The list began in March 1950.

text: How many men were in the Kelly Gang, counting Ned Kelly himself?
fact: Ned and Dan Kelly, Joe Byrne and Steve Hart.

text: In what year was Guy Fawkes caught in the Gunpowder Plot?
fact: He was found in a cellar beneath Parliament, guarding barrels of gunpowder.

text: In what year did the hijacker known as D. B. Cooper vanish with his ransom?
fact: He boarded in Portland, Oregon, under the name Dan Cooper.

text: Bernie Madoff was sentenced to how many years in prison?
fact: It was the maximum the court could give. His lawyer had asked for 12.

text: Al Capone was sentenced in 1931 to how many years in federal prison?
fact: He was freed in 1939, having served about seven and a half.

text: In what year did Alec Jeffreys discover DNA fingerprinting?
fact: He made the discovery in his laboratory at the University of Leicester.

text: For how many years was Alcatraz a federal prison?
fact: It opened as a federal prison in 1934 and closed in March 1963.

text: In what year did the Watergate break-in take place?
fact: The burglars were arrested in Washington on 17 June.

fact: It is shaken with ice and served in a cocktail glass with a twist of lemon.

fact: The style grew out of heavily hopped pale ales that English brewers shipped to India.

text: Tequila is made from which plant?
fact: The official tequila standard allows only the blue variety of Agave tequilana Weber.

text: What is the wine expert who looks after a restaurant's wine list called?
On a wine label, what does the vintage year tell you?
fact: In Australia at least 85 per cent of the wine must come from that year.
wrong: When it is best to drink

text: A Virgin Mary is a Bloody Mary made without which ingredient?
If you order a whisky "neat", how does it come?
fact: Ask for it "on the rocks" and it comes over ice.
answer: On its own, with no ice

text: Which bitter ingredient, from the bark of the cinchona tree, flavours tonic water?
fact: The first commercial tonic water was patented in London in 1858.

text: A Gibson is a Martini garnished with what, in place of the usual olive or lemon twist?
The Bellini, prosecco with white peach purée, was created at Harry's Bar in which city?
fact: Giuseppe Cipriani named it after the Renaissance painter Giovanni Bellini.

text: The grape Australians call shiraz goes by which name in France?
fact: DNA tests in the late 1990s found its parents are two obscure grapes of south-east France.

text: How does most rosé wine get its pink colour?
fact: Rosé Champagne is the exception: most of it is made by adding a little red wine.
answer: A short soak on red grape skins

text: A wine that is "corked" has which fault?
fact: The culprit is a compound called TCA, which smells of damp cardboard.
answer: A musty taint from the cork
wrong: Bits of cork floating in it

text: What does "Veuve" mean in the name of the Champagne house Veuve Clicquot?
fact: Barbe-Nicole Clicquot took over the family firm when her husband died in 1805.

text: What is the main thing that separates a lager from an ale?
fact: Lager yeast works at about 9 to 14°C; ale yeast likes it warmer.
answer: The yeast and a cooler ferment

text: A 285 ml glass of beer is a middy in Sydney. What is it called in Melbourne and Brisbane?
fact: In Darwin the same glass is a handle, and in Adelaide it is a schooner.

text: Galaxy, Vic Secret and Pride of Ringwood are Australian-bred varieties of what?
fact: Pride of Ringwood was bred at a Carlton & United research station in Ringwood, Melbourne.

text: Laphroaig, Lagavulin and Ardbeg are smoky whiskies from which Scottish island?
fact: The three distilleries sit within about two miles of each other on the south coast.

text: What does "London Dry" on a gin label tell you?
fact: A London Dry gin can legally be distilled anywhere in the world.
answer: How it was made, not where
wrong: It was rested in dry oak casks

text: In a whisky warehouse, what is the "angels' share"?
fact: In Scotland's cool climate, about 2 per cent of a cask evaporates each year.
wrong: The first run off the still
A cask kept for the owners
The last dram in the bottle

text: Calvados, from Normandy in France, is a brandy made from which fruit?
fact: Cider is distilled, then aged in oak for at least two years.

text: Which soft drink was invented in wartime Germany when Coca-Cola syrup could not be imported?
fact: The first version was made from whey and apple pomace, whatever could be found.

text: A Boulevardier is a Negroni with the gin swapped for which spirit?
fact: The IBA stirs it over ice with Campari and sweet red vermouth.

text: In a classic Sazerac, what is the chilled glass rinsed with before the drink goes in?
fact: The IBA recipe then adds cognac, a sugar cube and Peychaud's bitters.

text: The Tommy's Margarita, a modern classic made with no orange liqueur, was created in which city?
fact: Julio Bermejo devised it in about 1990 at Tommy's Mexican Restaurant.

text: The Last Word is equal parts gin, lime juice, maraschino liqueur and which other liqueur?
fact: Carthusian monks have made Chartreuse to a secret recipe since the 1700s.

text: Which of these words on a Champagne label means the driest wine?
fact: Brut has under 12 g of sugar a litre. Extra dry, despite the name, has 12 to 17 g.

text: Barolo, the great red of Piedmont in Italy, must be made entirely from which grape?
fact: It comes from 11 communes around the village of Barolo, in the province of Cuneo.

text: The Victorian town of Rutherglen is famous for which style of wine?
fact: The red-skinned grape behind it is known locally as brown muscat.

text: Which South Australian region is famous for cabernet grown on a strip of red "terra rossa" soil?
fact: The red soil lies in a narrow strip over limestone; iron oxide gives it its colour.

text: Belgian lambic beer is fermented in an unusual way. How?
fact: The hot wort cools overnight in a wide, shallow open vessel called a coolship.
answer: By wild yeast, with none added

text: Which was the last Australian state to end six o'clock closing in its pubs, in 1967?
fact: Early closing began in 1916. Its nightly rush at the bar was the "six o'clock swill".

text: Sake is brewed from rice with the help of which mould, which turns the starch into sugar?
fact: Moromi is the main mash, shubo the yeast starter and kasu the lees left after pressing.

text: Behind a bar, what is a Hawthorne?
fact: It is named after the Hawthorne Café, a Boston bar of the 1890s.

text: The black label of Jack Daniel's Tennessee whiskey reads "Old No." followed by which number?
fact: Nobody knows for sure why. The distillery itself calls it a mystery.

text: In what year did national Prohibition end in the United States?
fact: The 21st Amendment was ratified on 5 December, when Utah became the 36th state to approve it.

text: In the United States, a spirit labelled 100 proof is what percentage alcohol by volume?
fact: American proof is simply twice the alcohol by volume.

text: How many millilitres does a standard Australian jug of beer hold?
fact: That is about 40 fluid ounces, or two imperial pints.

text: In what year was the Reinheitsgebot, Bavaria's famous beer purity law, issued?
fact: Duke Wilhelm IV issued it at Ingolstadt on 23 April.

text: In what year was Penfolds founded, at Magill near Adelaide?
fact: Dr Christopher and Mary Penfold arrived from England that June, bringing vine cuttings.

text: In what year did the Royal Navy pour its last daily rum ration, on "Black Tot Day"?
fact: The date was 31 July. Sailors wore black armbands and held mock funerals.

text: Since 2018, a Cognac labelled XO must be aged in oak for at least how many years?
fact: Before April 2018 the minimum was six years.

text: In what year was Aperol launched, at a trade fair in the Italian city of Padua?
fact: It was created by the brothers Luigi and Silvio Barbieri.

text: Which club won the first Premier League title, in 1992-93?
fact: Aston Villa finished runners-up.

text: Which club went through the 2003-04 Premier League season without losing a game?
Kevin Keegan's famous "I would love it if we beat them" rant came while he managed which club?
fact: He said it live on Sky Sports, aiming it at Alex Ferguson's Manchester United.

text: Who managed Liverpool to the 2024-25 Premier League title in his first season at the club?
Which Premier League club did Tim Cahill play for from 2004 to 2012?
fact: He joined from Millwall for about £1.5 million.

text: Sergio Agüero's stoppage-time winner that clinched the 2011-12 title came against which club?
fact: It gave Manchester City their first top-flight title since 1968.

text: Who managed Leicester City to the 2015-16 Premier League title?
Who replaced Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013?
In the Women's Super League, which club did Matildas star Sam Kerr win her titles with?
fact: She won the WSL Golden Boot in both 2020-21 and 2021-22.

text: Which Australian scored all four Leeds goals in a 4-3 win over Liverpool in November 2000?
fact: Liverpool had led 2-0 before he took over.

text: Which Australian goalkeeper played Premier League football for Middlesbrough, Fulham, Chelsea and Leicester?
Who managed Blackburn Rovers to the 1994-95 Premier League title?
At which ground did Eric Cantona leap into the crowd and kick a fan in January 1995?
Steven Gerrard's slip against Chelsea at Anfield in April 2014 let which player run through to score?
fact: Chelsea won 2-0, a huge blow to Liverpool's title hopes.

text: Which club played at Roker Park until 1997?
fact: They moved to the Stadium of Light.

text: Liverpool keeper Alisson headed a stoppage-time winner in May 2021 against which club?
fact: He was the first goalkeeper ever to score a competitive goal for Liverpool.

text: Whose late goal at Anfield in May 1989 snatched the league title for Arsenal?
fact: Arsenal needed to win by two goals and won 2-0.

text: Which club won the last old First Division title, in 1991-92, before the Premier League began?
Who was the first manager from outside the UK and Ireland to win the English league title?
fact: Manuel Pellegrini became the first from outside Europe, with Man City in 2013-14.

text: Which club were relegated from the Premier League in 2007-08 with only 11 points?
fact: It was still the lowest total in Premier League history at the end of 2025-26.

text: Which club were the first Premier League champions to later be relegated from the Premier League?
fact: Blackburn went down in 1999, four years after winning the title.

text: Which club sacked Ange Postecoglou in October 2025 after just 39 days in charge?
fact: He failed to win any of his eight games in charge.

text: Who scored the first ever Premier League goal, in August 1992?
fact: He scored for Sheffield United against Manchester United.

text: Who scored against Watford in April 2019 after just 7.69 seconds?
fact: It was still the fastest goal in Premier League history at the end of 2025-26.

text: Jamie Vardy scored in 11 Premier League games in a row in 2015, breaking whose record?
fact: The record-breaking 11th goal came against Manchester United.

text: Who was the first Premier League manager to be sacked, by Chelsea in February 1993?
fact: David Webb took over from him.

text: Which club conceded 100 goals in its only Premier League season, 1993-94?
Who scored the first Premier League hat-trick, for Leeds against Tottenham in 1992?
fact: Leeds won 5-0 at Elland Road.

text: Which club went unbeaten to win the first Football League title, in 1888-89?
fact: Aston Villa finished runners-up.

text: Who scored at Old Trafford to clinch Arsenal's 2001-02 title?
Who won the first Premier League Golden Boot, in 1992-93?
fact: He scored one for Nottingham Forest and 21 for Tottenham.

text: Which Match of the Day pundit said Man United's young side "can't win anything with kids" in 1995?
fact: United went on to win the league and FA Cup double that season.

text: Andy Cole scored five times in a 9-0 Manchester United win in March 1995 against which club?
Sadio Mané scored a hat-trick in 2 minutes 56 seconds in May 2015 playing for which club?
fact: Southampton beat Aston Villa 6-1.

text: Chelsea clinched the 2009-10 title with an 8-0 final-day win over which club?
fact: Carlo Ancelotti's side won the title by one point from Manchester United.

text: From which club did Liverpool sign Mohamed Salah in 2017?
fact: He joined Chelsea in 2014 but was loaned to Fiorentina and Roma a year later.

text: How many points did Manchester City finish with in their record-setting 2017-18 season?
How many Premier League titles did Sir Alex Ferguson win with Manchester United?
fact: The last came in 2012-13, his final season.

text: How many league matches in a row did Arsenal go unbeaten between May 2003 and October 2004?
How many clubs played in the first Premier League season, 1992-93?
fact: The league was cut to 20 clubs in 1995.

text: How many Premier League goals did Erling Haaland score in 2022-23?
fact: It broke Andy Cole and Alan Shearer's record, set when seasons had 42 games.

text: How many Premier League goals did Alan Shearer score in his career?
fact: He was still the competition's record scorer at the end of 2025-26.

text: In what year did Chelsea win their first English league title?
fact: They won the 1954-55 First Division, with Wolves runners-up.

text: How many goals were scored in total when Portsmouth beat Reading in September 2007?
fact: Portsmouth won 7-4, still the highest-scoring Premier League game at the end of 2025-26.

text: Ryan Giggs scored in how many consecutive Premier League seasons, starting in 1992-93?
fact: He scored in every season from 1992-93 to 2012-13.

text: Put these managers in order of starting at their club, earliest first.
Put these clubs in order of their first Premier League title, earliest first.
Put these clubs in order of their first Premier League relegation, earliest first.

Who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole?
fact: The Norwegian's team of five relied on sled dogs to cover the distance.

text: Which Sherpa reached the summit of Everest with Edmund Hillary in 1953?
fact: The British expedition was led by John Hunt. Hillary was a New Zealander.

text: Which American pilot vanished over the Pacific in 1937 while trying to fly around the world?
fact: She and navigator Fred Noonan were last heard from near Howland Island on 2 July.

text: What was the name of James Cook's ship on his first voyage to the Pacific, from 1768 to 1771?
fact: Resolution, Discovery and Adventure all sailed on his later voyages.

text: What was the name of the plane Charles Lindbergh flew alone from New York to Paris?
fact: The flight took 33 and a half hours and was the first solo non-stop Atlantic crossing.

text: The Americas are named after which Italian navigator?
fact: Mapmaker Martin Waldseemüller put the name America on his world map of 1507.

text: Henry Morton Stanley is said to have greeted which missing explorer with "..., I presume?"
fact: They met in 1871 at Ujiji, by Lake Tanganyika. The New York Herald had sent Stanley.

text: Which film director made the first solo dive to the deepest point of the ocean, in 2012?
fact: His submersible, Deepsea Challenger, was built in Sydney.

text: Ferdinand Magellan was killed in 1521 in what is now which country?
fact: He died in a fight on the island of Mactan on 27 April.

text: The 14th-century traveller Ibn Battuta set out from his home in which present-day country?
fact: Born in Tangier in 1304, he covered about 117,000 km in some 30 years of travel.

text: Which Chinese admiral led seven great "treasure fleet" voyages in the early 1400s?
fact: The voyages ran from 1405 to 1433 and reached the coast of East Africa.

text: Which of these great Silk Road cities is in present-day Uzbekistan?
fact: It grew rich on trade between China, Persia and Europe, and Timur made it his capital.

text: After the Endurance was lost, Shackleton sailed a lifeboat about 1,300 km to which island for help?
fact: Six men made the crossing in the James Caird. Three then crossed the island on foot.

text: Sir John Franklin's lost Arctic expedition of 1845 sailed in HMS Erebus and which other ship?
fact: All 129 men were lost while searching for the Northwest Passage.

text: Which geologist led the Australasian Antarctic Expedition of 1911 to 1914?
fact: The expedition sailed from Hobart in the Aurora and set up its main base at Cape Denison.

text: Asked why he wanted to climb Everest, which British climber is said to have replied "Because it's there"?
fact: He vanished high on the mountain in 1924. His body was found there in 1999.

text: Which climber was hailed in 1986 as the first to reach the top of every mountain over 8,000 metres?
fact: He finished on Lhotse that October. Jerzy Kukuczka of Poland completed the set a year later.

text: Which lake did John Hanning Speke reach in 1858 and declare to be the source of the Nile?
fact: His expedition partner Richard Burton disagreed and backed Lake Tanganyika.

text: Wylie, a Noongar man from King George Sound, finished an 1841 trek to Albany beside which explorer?
fact: The party left Fowlers Bay in February. Only Eyre and Wylie completed the journey.

text: The Overland Telegraph Line was built along the route of which explorer's south-to-north crossing?
fact: The highway from Port Augusta to Darwin also follows his route and carries his name.

text: Where was James Cook killed in 1779, on his third Pacific voyage?
fact: He died at Kealakekua Bay on 14 February, in a clash after one of his boats was taken.

text: Bert Hinkler, the first person to fly solo from England to Australia, came from which Queensland city?
fact: He made the flight in under 16 days in an Avro Avian, landing in Darwin.

text: What was the name of Jacques Cousteau's famous research ship?
fact: She was built as a wartime minesweeper and later worked as a ferry in Malta.

text: What was the name of the balsa raft Thor Heyerdahl sailed from Peru to Polynesia in 1947?
fact: Six men spent 101 days at sea before the raft struck a reef at Raroia in the Tuamotus.

text: Vasco da Gama's fleet, the first to sail from Europe to India, reached which city in 1498?
fact: The fleet arrived in May. The city, on the Malabar Coast, is now called Kozhikode.

text: Francis Drake's Golden Hind began its voyage around the world under what name?
fact: Drake renamed it in 1578 to honour his patron Christopher Hatton, whose crest bore a hind.

text: Tupaia, the priest and navigator who sailed with James Cook from 1769, came from which island group?
fact: Born on Ra'iatea, he was a star navigator and artist, and interpreted for Cook in New Zealand.

text: In which small ship did Roald Amundsen become the first to sail through the Northwest Passage?
fact: He had a crew of six, and the voyage lasted from 1903 to 1906.

text: A team from which country made the first ascent of K2, in 1954?
fact: Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni reached the summit on 31 July.

text: Sacagawea helped Lewis and Clark obtain horses to cross the Rockies from which people?
fact: She set out with the expedition in April 1805, carrying her two-month-old son.

text: Charles Kingsford Smith vanished in 1935 on a record attempt, off the coast of which country?
fact: He and Tommy Pethybridge were flying the Lady Southern Cross from India to Singapore.

text: In 1931, South Australian explorer Hubert Wilkins tried to reach the North Pole in what?
fact: The old US Navy boat dived under the Arctic ice but was too damaged to reach the Pole.

text: British explorer Percy Fawcett vanished in Brazil in 1925 while hunting for a lost city he called what?
fact: He set out into the Mato Grosso with his eldest son, Jack, and one of Jack's friends.

text: Wilfred Thesiger's book Arabian Sands describes his crossings of which desert in the 1940s?
fact: He crossed it twice between 1946 and 1948. Its Arabic name is Rub' al Khali.

text: Galmahra, a young Aboriginal guide also known as Jackey Jackey, was hailed for his part in whose 1848 expedition?
fact: Kennedy died just short of Cape York. Galmahra, from the Hunter Valley, went on alone to the ship.

text: Which Aboriginal man sailed right around Australia with Matthew Flinders in the Investigator, in 1802-03?
fact: He is the first Aboriginal person known to have circumnavigated the continent.

text: How many ships sailed on Christopher Columbus's first voyage across the Atlantic?
fact: They were the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María.

text: In what year did 16-year-old Jessica Watson sail back into Sydney Harbour after 210 days alone at sea?
fact: She had left Sydney in October 2009 in a 10-metre yacht called Ella's Pink Lady.

text: How many mountains on Earth rise more than 8,000 metres above sea level?
fact: All of them stand in the Himalaya and Karakoram ranges of Asia.

text: In what year did Amy Johnson become the first woman to fly solo from England to Australia?
fact: She took 19 days from Croydon to Darwin in a Gipsy Moth she had named Jason.

text: In what year did Robert Falcon Scott's party reach the South Pole?
fact: The polar party was Scott, Wilson, Bowers, Oates and Edgar Evans.

text: In what year was the wreck of HMS Erebus, one of Franklin's lost ships, found in the Canadian Arctic?
fact: Inuit knowledge helped guide the Parks Canada search. The second ship was found in 2016.

text: Counting Shackleton, how many men were in the Endurance party stranded in the Antarctic? All survived.
fact: The ship was crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea and sank in November 1915.

text: In 1889-90 reporter Nellie Bly raced around the world to beat a fictional record. How many days did she take?
fact: The record she set out to beat was Phileas Fogg's 80 days, from the Jules Verne novel.

text: In what year did Junko Tabei of Japan become the first woman to reach the summit of Everest?
fact: She reached the top on 16 May as part of an all-women Japanese expedition.

text: Which Formula 1 team's badge is a prancing horse?
fact: The horse was the emblem of Italian WWI flying ace Francesco Baracca.

text: In 2020, Lewis Hamilton equalled which driver's record of seven world titles?
fact: Hamilton sealed his seventh title at the 2020 Turkish Grand Prix.

text: In Formula 1, what did the letters DRS stand for?
fact: DRS was used from 2011 to 2025, then replaced by active aerodynamics in 2026.

Max Verstappen won his first four world titles with which team?
fact: He won four in a row, from 2021 to 2024.

text: The Interlagos circuit is in which city?
fact: Its official name is the Autódromo José Carlos Pace.

text: What is the name of the titanium hoop over the cockpit that became compulsory in F1 in 2018?
Lewis Hamilton left Mercedes to join which team for the 2025 season?
Which F1 team is nicknamed the Silver Arrows?
Formula 1's first ever night race was held in 2008 in which country?
fact: Fernando Alonso won it for Renault.

text: In Pirelli's colour code since 2019, what colour marks the soft dry tyre?
fact: Medium is yellow, hard is white, intermediate is green and full wet is blue.

text: Under the points system used since 2010, how many points does a Grand Prix win earn?
Alan Jones won the 1980 world title driving for which team?
fact: It was also Williams' first constructors' title.

text: Which four-time world champion was nicknamed "The Professor"?
Ayrton Senna was killed in a crash at which circuit in 1994?
fact: He crashed at the Tamburello corner during the San Marino Grand Prix.

text: Niki Lauda's fiery 1976 crash happened at which circuit?
fact: He was back racing just six weeks later, at Monza.

text: Who won the very first Formula 1 world drivers' championship, in 1950?
fact: Farina drove an Alfa Romeo.

text: Which team won both world titles in 2009, the only season it ever raced?
fact: Jenson Button was its champion. The team became Mercedes for 2010.

text: Which driver won the 2008 finale in Brazil but lost the title by a single point?
fact: Hamilton passed Timo Glock on the final lap to finish fifth and take the title.

text: Daniel Ricciardo won his first Grand Prix in 2014 in which country?
fact: He passed Nico Rosberg's ailing Mercedes on lap 68 of 70 in Montreal.

text: Not counting sprints, Oscar Piastri won his first Grand Prix in 2024 in which country?
fact: He was the fifth Australian to win a Grand Prix.

text: Maggotts, Becketts and Chapel are corners at which circuit?
Whose tyre blew out in Adelaide in 1986, costing him the world title?
fact: Alain Prost won the race and the title.

text: Senna and Prost collided to settle the title in both 1989 and 1990 at which circuit?
fact: The 1989 clash went Prost's way; in 1990 it was Senna's.

text: Who founded the Lotus team?
fact: Chapman founded Lotus in 1952.

text: How many Grands Prix did Michael Schumacher win in his F1 career?
How many of the 22 Grands Prix in 2023 did Max Verstappen win?
fact: The other three went to Sergio Pérez (two) and Carlos Sainz (Singapore).

text: In what year did Mark Webber win his first Grand Prix?
fact: He won the German GP at the Nürburgring from pole, despite a drive-through penalty.

text: How old was Sebastian Vettel when he won his first world title, in 2010?
Put these circuits in order of their first world championship Grand Prix, earliest first.
Put these champions in order of their first world title, earliest first.
Put these Australians in order of their F1 race debut, earliest first.
Who was the race director at the disputed 2021 Abu Dhabi title decider?
fact: Masi, an Australian, was removed from the role in February 2022.

text: Jack Brabham won his first two titles, in 1959 and 1960, driving for which team?
Which team won a Grand Prix with a six-wheeled car, in 1976?
fact: The Tyrrell P34 won the 1976 Swedish GP, the only win ever for a six-wheeler.

text: Who won the only race entered by Brabham's "fan car", in Sweden in 1978?
fact: Brabham withdrew the BT46B after that single win.

text: Red Bull's "Multi 21" team orders row happened at which 2013 race?
fact: Vettel ignored the order to stay behind Webber and passed him for the win.

text: Montreal's Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is built on which island?
fact: The man-made island was largely built up for Expo 67.

text: Which driver won the 1982 world title despite winning only one race that year?
fact: His only win of 1982 was the Swiss GP, held at Dijon in France.

text: Who was Ferrari's last drivers' champion before Michael Schumacher?
fact: Scheckter won in 1979. Ferrari then waited until Schumacher's title in 2000.

text: Who became the first American Formula 1 world champion, in 1961?
fact: He clinched it at Monza, where teammate Wolfgang von Trips was killed.

text: Mark Webber scored points on his F1 debut, at his home race in Melbourne, for which team?
fact: He finished fifth after a string of first-lap retirements.

text: Daniel Ricciardo made his F1 race debut at the 2011 British Grand Prix for which team?
fact: Red Bull loaned him to the Spanish team for the last 11 races of 2011.

text: Monza's Parabolica corner was renamed in 2021 to honour which Italian driver?
How many laps long was the 2025 Monaco Grand Prix?
fact: Monaco is the only Grand Prix shorter than the usual 305 km minimum.

text: How many pole positions did Ayrton Senna take in his F1 career?
fact: He held the all-time pole record from 1989 until 2006.

text: In what year did Ferrari win its first world championship Grand Prix?
fact: José Froilán González won the British GP at Silverstone.

text: As of the end of 2025, how many constructors' titles had Ferrari won?
fact: The most recent was in 2008.

text: Each of these teams won exactly one constructors' title. Put them in order, earliest first.
Put these drivers in order of career Grand Prix wins, most first.
In The Lord of the Rings, where must the One Ring be taken to be destroyed?
fact: The Ring was forged there, in the land of Mordor.

text: What is the name of Harry Potter's snowy owl?
fact: She was a birthday present from Hagrid in the first book.

text: At the start of Star Wars: A New Hope, Luke Skywalker lives on which desert planet?
fact: Tatooine orbits twin suns.

text: In Star Trek, which planet is Mr Spock's home world?
fact: His father, Sarek, is a Vulcan. His mother, Amanda Grayson, is human.

text: In The Hunger Games, which district is Katniss Everdeen's home?
fact: District 12 mines coal for the country of Panem.

text: In Doctor Who, what does the Doctor's TARDIS look like from the outside?
fact: Its chameleon circuit is broken, so it cannot change shape to blend in.

text: In The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, which sweet does the White Witch tempt Edmund with?
fact: Mr Tumnus, the first Narnian that Lucy meets, is a faun.

text: Which actor played both Agent Smith in The Matrix and Elrond in The Lord of the Rings?
fact: Born in Nigeria to British parents, he has lived in Australia since 1976.

text: In Rick Riordan's novels, Percy Jackson is the son of which Greek god?
fact: The first book, The Lightning Thief, came out in 2005.

text: In House of the Dragon, what is the Targaryen civil war over the throne called?
fact: The series is based on George R. R. Martin's book Fire & Blood.
wrong: The War of the Five Kings

text: In Game of Thrones, which Valyrian steel sword is Lord Commander Mormont's gift to Jon Snow?
fact: Kit Harington plays Jon in the HBO series.

text: In Dune, Paul's Fremen name Muad'Dib is taken from which desert animal?
fact: Frank Herbert's glossary calls it the adapted kangaroo mouse of Arrakis.

text: In James Cameron's Avatar, which precious mineral have humans come to Pandora to mine?
fact: The first film is set in the year 2154.

text: In Jurassic Park, on which island off Costa Rica is the dinosaur park built?
fact: The island exteriors were shot in Hawaii, mostly on Kauai.

text: In Terry Pratchett's Discworld, the four elephants that carry the world stand on a giant what?
fact: The star turtle is called Great A'Tuin.

text: Which Australian actor took over from Henry Cavill as Geralt in season 4 of The Witcher?
fact: Season 4 reached Netflix on 30 October 2025.

text: In His Dark Materials, what is the animal companion that holds a person's soul called?
fact: Lyra's is Pantalaimon, known as Pan.

text: In The Last of Us, which real kind of fungus is behind the outbreak?
fact: In the HBO series Pedro Pascal plays Joel and Bella Ramsey plays Ellie.

text: Which dragon does Harry Potter face in the first task of the Triwizard Tournament?
fact: The other three were faced by Viktor Krum, Cedric Diggory and Fleur Delacour.

text: Who finished The Wheel of Time novels after Robert Jordan died in 2007?
fact: The main series runs to 14 books. The last, A Memory of Light, came out in 2013.

text: In Twilight, Bella Swan moves from Phoenix to which rainy town in Washington state?
fact: Stephenie Meyer's novel was published in 2005.

text: In the Fallout TV series, who plays the bounty hunter known as the Ghoul?
fact: The series began on Prime Video in April 2024, with Ella Purnell as Lucy.

text: In Star Trek, which Starfleet Academy test is designed so that cadets cannot win?
fact: It first appeared in Star Trek II (1982). Kirk beat it by reprogramming the simulation.

text: Which linguist created the Dothraki and High Valyrian languages for Game of Thrones?
fact: He won the job in a contest run by the Language Creation Society.

text: Who directed The Empire Strikes Back (1980)?
fact: George Lucas wrote the story and was executive producer.

text: Which director spent years in the 1970s planning a film of Dune that was never made?
fact: Salvador Dalí was to play the Emperor, with music by Pink Floyd and Magma.

text: Which Queensland-born composer wrote the Doctor Who theme tune?
fact: Delia Derbyshire turned his score into electronic sound at the BBC Radiophonic Workshop.

text: In The Matrix, what is the name of the hovercraft that Morpheus commands?
fact: The Matrix won all four Oscars it was nominated for.

text: Who sang Into the West, the Oscar-winning song from The Return of the King?
fact: Lennox wrote it with Fran Walsh and Howard Shore. The film won every Oscar it was up for.

text: Which actor spent weeks filming as Marty McFly before Michael J. Fox replaced him?
fact: Stoltz was let go in January 1985, more than a month into the shoot of Back to the Future.

text: Mad Max 2 was filmed in the desert around which outback mining city?
fact: In the United States the film was released as The Road Warrior.

text: In Asimov's Foundation, what is Hari Seldon's science of predicting the future of societies?
fact: The first Foundation novel was published in 1951.

text: Who wrote The Three-Body Problem, winner of the 2015 Hugo Award for Best Novel?
fact: Ken Liu translated it into English.

text: In which Octavia Butler novel is a writer pulled back in time from 1976 to a Maryland plantation?
fact: Kindred was first published in 1979.

text: Which 1995 novel began Garth Nix's Old Kingdom series?
fact: It won two Aurealis Awards, for best fantasy novel and best young adult novel.

text: Which author won the Hugo Award for Best Novel three years in a row, from 2016 to 2018?
fact: She won for all three books of one trilogy, ending with The Stone Sky.

text: In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, what number is the answer to life, the universe and everything?
fact: The story began as a BBC radio comedy in 1978. The first novel followed in 1979.

text: In the first Back to the Future film, to what year does Marty McFly travel back?
fact: Robert Zemeckis directed, and Michael J. Fox played Marty.

text: In what year was Frank Herbert's novel Dune first published as a book?
fact: It shared the 1966 Hugo Award and won the first Nebula Award for Best Novel.

text: The film Blade Runner came out in 1982. In what year is its story set?
fact: It is based on a 1968 novel by Philip K. Dick.

text: Katniss Everdeen first enters the arena in which numbered Hunger Games?
fact: The 75th Games follow a year later, in Catching Fire.

text: Add up the rings in Tolkien's ring verse: for Elves, Dwarves, Men and the Dark Lord. How many in all?
fact: Three for the Elves, seven for the Dwarves, nine for Men and the One Ring.

text: How many novels are there in Terry Pratchett's Discworld series?
fact: The last, The Shepherd's Crown, was published in 2015, after his death.

text: In the Harry Potter story, in what year is the Battle of Hogwarts fought?
fact: The books date his parents' deaths to 31 October 1981, when he was one. The battle is on 2 May.

text: In what year was The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of The Lord of the Rings, published?
fact: The third and last volume, The Return of the King, followed in 1955.

text: Put these science fiction films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these Star Wars films in the order their stories take place, earliest first.
Put these actors in order of when they first played the Doctor in Doctor Who, earliest first.
Put these Star Trek series in order of first broadcast, earliest first.
Put these novels in order of first publication, earliest first.

items.label: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe

text: Which French house makes the Birkin bag, named after the actress Jane Birkin?
fact: The bag was introduced in 1984.

text: Chuck Taylor, whose signature is on a famous canvas sneaker, was a salesman for which company?
fact: Taylor, a semi-professional basketball player, joined the company in 1921.

text: Which designer's simple black dress, pictured in Vogue in 1926, made the "little black dress" a staple?
fact: Vogue dubbed it the Chanel "Ford", likening it to the Model T car.

text: Which shoe designer is famous for the glossy red soles on his high heels?
fact: The idea is said to have come from an assistant's red nail polish in the early 1990s.

text: Traditional ugg boots are made from what?
fact: The fleece faces inwards, against the foot.

text: Who took over as Versace's head designer after Gianni Versace died in 1997?
fact: Gianni's younger sister led the house's design until 2025.

text: The fast-fashion chain H&M was founded in which country?
fact: It began in 1947 as a women's clothing shop called Hennes, Swedish for "hers".

text: Which swimwear brand began in Sydney and got its name in 1928 from a staff slogan contest?
fact: The winning slogan was "Speed on in your Speedos".

text: London's Savile Row is world famous for which trade?
fact: Henry Poole & Co, founded in 1806, is thought to be the first tailor to open on the Row itself.

text: What was Louis Vuitton's trade when he opened his own workshop in Paris?
fact: His flat-topped trunks could be stacked, unlike the usual domed ones.

text: Which American designer revived Gucci as its creative director from 1994 to 2004?
fact: He left in 2004 and launched his own label the following year.

text: Which designer launched "Le Smoking", a tuxedo for women, in 1966?
fact: It was part of his autumn-winter haute couture collection that year.

text: Rudolf Dassler fell out with his brother Adi, the founder of Adidas, and started which rival brand?
fact: Both companies are still based in the brothers' home town, Herzogenaurach.

text: Nike co-founder Bill Bowerman made an early running-shoe sole using which kitchen appliance?
fact: He poured urethane into the family's iron, a wedding present, and glued it shut.

text: The bikini, first shown in Paris just after World War II, was named after what?
fact: Bikini Atoll was in the news when Louis Réard unveiled the swimsuit on 5 July 1946.

text: The word "denim" comes from the name of which French city?
fact: The cloth was known as serge de Nîmes, which English clipped to denim.

text: Who designed the dress Catherine Middleton wore to marry Prince William in 2011?
fact: Burton was then creative director of Alexander McQueen.

text: Kate Moss was spotted by a model scout in 1988, aged 14, at which airport?
fact: She was spotted by Sarah Doukas, founder of the Storm model agency.

text: The letters YKK, stamped on zips around the world, belong to a company from which country?
fact: They stand for Yoshida Kogyo Kabushikigaisha, founded in Tokyo in 1934.

text: Which British model caused a stir at Flemington on Derby Day 1965 in a minidress, with no hat or gloves?
fact: She was in Melbourne to judge Fashions on the Field.

text: Akubra hats are made from felt of which animal's fur?
fact: The hats have been made in Kempsey, NSW, since the 1970s.

text: In The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda schools Andy on the exact shade of her blue jumper. What is it?
fact: The screenwriter has said the fashion history in the speech was made up.

text: In Zoolander (2001), which of Derek's looks stops a throwing star in mid-air?
fact: The villain, fashion mogul Mugatu, is played by Will Ferrell.

text: So many people searched for a dress Jennifer Lopez wore in 2000 that Google built what?
fact: It was a green Versace dress, worn to the Grammy Awards that February.

text: Who designed the black "revenge dress" that Princess Diana wore in June 1994?
fact: Diana wore it to a Vanity Fair dinner at the Serpentine Gallery in London.

text: Who designed the yellow fur-trimmed cape Rihanna wore to the 2015 Met Gala?
fact: It weighed about 25 kg, and three people carried the train.

text: Which Paris couturier is known as the pioneer of the bias-cut dress?
fact: Cloth cut diagonally across the grain stretches and clings to the body.

text: Thomas Burberry invented which weatherproof fabric in 1879?
fact: Ernest Shackleton wore it on his Antarctic expeditions.

text: Marc Jacobs was dismissed by which American label after his 1992 "grunge" collection?
fact: He became creative director of Louis Vuitton in 1997.

text: In August 1974, who became the first Black model on the cover of American Vogue?
fact: Donyale Luna had appeared on the cover of British Vogue in 1966.

text: Anna Wintour's first cover as editor of Vogue, in November 1988, was the magazine's first to show what?
fact: Michaela Bercu wore US$50 jeans with a US$10,000 Christian Lacroix couture jacket.
wrong: A model in a leather jacket

text: Vivienne Westwood and Malcolm McLaren's shop, the home of punk fashion, stood on which London street?
fact: At number 430, it was Let It Rock, Sex and Seditionaries before becoming Worlds End in 1980.

text: Which Japanese designer made the black turtlenecks that became Steve Jobs's uniform?
fact: Jobs told his biographer that the designer made him "like a hundred of them".

text: Which Australian designer made the koala jumper Princess Diana wore to the polo in 1982?
fact: The "Blinky" knit took its name from Blinky Bill.

text: The first Zara shop opened in 1975 in which Spanish city?
fact: Amancio Ortega opened it that May, in the city's Juan Flórez street.

text: The fabric name "seersucker" comes from Persian words meaning what?
fact: The name is thought to describe its mix of smooth and puckered stripes.

text: What three-digit number names Levi's original button-fly jeans?
fact: Levi's first used the lot number around 1890 and says nobody knows why it was chosen.

text: In what year did Kim Kardashian wear Marilyn Monroe's "Happy Birthday, Mr President" dress to the Met Gala?
fact: Monroe wore it in 1962 to sing to President John F. Kennedy.

text: In what year did Christian Dior show his first collection, soon nicknamed the "New Look"?
fact: Carmel Snow, editor of Harper's Bazaar, gave it the name.

text: Nike's first Air Jordan sneaker reached the shops in what year?
fact: Peter Moore designed it for Michael Jordan, then a rookie with the Chicago Bulls.

text: The Dr. Martens 1460 boot is named after the date it was first made. In what year was that?
fact: The date was 1 April 1960, or 1/4/60.

text: In what year did Guccio Gucci found his leather goods business in Florence?
fact: As a young man he had worked at the Savoy Hotel in London.

text: In what year was the first issue of Vogue published in New York?
fact: It began as a weekly society paper and cost ten cents.

text: In what year was the first Met Gala held, as a midnight supper?
fact: Publicist Eleanor Lambert started it to raise money for the Costume Institute.

text: In what year was the first Australian Fashion Week held in Sydney?
fact: Simon Lock founded it. Akira Isogawa, unable to afford shoes, sent his models out in red socks.

text: Put these youth styles in order of their heyday, earliest first.
Put these fashion houses in order of founding, earliest first.

Pho, a noodle soup in a fragrant broth, comes from which country?
Which cheese goes into a classic Greek salad?
What is the main ingredient of hummus?
Tahini is a paste made from which seed?
Marzipan is made mainly from sugar and which ground nut?
Matcha is a powdered form of which kind of tea?
fact: The leaves are shaded for weeks before harvest to boost their colour and flavour.

text: The Queensland town of Bundaberg is famous for which spirit?
fact: It is distilled from molasses left over from the local sugar cane mills.

text: Fairy bread is white bread, butter and what?
In which state is the Margaret River wine region?
Which spirit is the base of a Moscow mule?
fact: It is traditionally served in a copper mug with ginger beer and lime.

text: Arborio rice is mainly used to make which dish?
Baba ganoush is a dip made mainly from which vegetable?
Which Italian city gives its name to a famous meat ragù?
fact: In Bologna the ragù is served with tagliatelle, not spaghetti.

text: Which Japanese word names the savoury "fifth taste"?
What does the Scoville scale measure?
The tagine, both a dish and a cone-lidded clay pot, is most associated with which country?
Ceviche, raw fish cured in citrus juice, is the national dish of which country?
Pierogi are filled dumplings most associated with which country?
Beef rendang originated with the Minangkabau people of which country?
fact: The dish comes from West Sumatra and is slow-cooked until the coconut milk dries out.

text: Goulash is regarded as the national dish of which country?
Saffron is made from which part of the crocus flower?
Outside Japan, the "wasabi" served with sushi is usually made mostly from what?
fact: Real wasabi is a rhizome that is notoriously hard to grow.

text: Which fish gives Worcestershire sauce its savoury depth?
Which spice is the dried flower bud of a tree?
fact: The name comes from the Latin for "nail", after the bud's shape.

text: Penfolds Grange is made mainly from which grape?
fact: Winemaker Max Schubert made the first experimental vintage in 1951.

text: Earl Grey tea is flavoured with oil from which citrus fruit?
The Tim Tam biscuit is named after what?
fact: An Arnott's executive saw the horse Tim Tam win in 1958.

text: Which company makes the Golden Gaytime ice cream?
Coopers Brewery is based in which Australian city?
fact: It is still family-owned, more than 160 years after Thomas Cooper's first brew.

text: Which company makes Weet-Bix in Australia?
In which country was Milo invented?
fact: Thomas Mayne created it for Nestlé in New South Wales in 1934.

text: The pavlova is named after a ballerina from which country?
fact: Anna Pavlova toured Australia and New Zealand in 1926.

text: What does the cooking term "sous vide" literally mean?
A roux, used to thicken sauces, is cooked flour and what?
Which French phrase means having all ingredients prepared before you start cooking?
What is the browning reaction between sugars and proteins in searing meat called?
fact: It is named after French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard.

text: North African couscous is usually made from semolina of which grain?
Vanilla comes from the pods of which kind of plant?
fact: Each flower opens for about a day and is often pollinated by hand.

text: Kensington Pride is Australia's classic variety of which fruit?
fact: It is often sold as the Bowen mango.

text: Poutine, chips with cheese curds and gravy, comes from which Canadian province?
Which Italian dessert's name means "cooked cream"?
Which spice gives Spanish chorizo its red colour?
By law, bourbon must be made from at least 51 per cent of which grain?
The pie floater, a meat pie in pea soup, is a classic of which city?
The Moreton Bay bug is a type of what?
Bobotie, spiced mince baked under an egg topping, is a classic dish of which country?
Which spice comes from the same fruit as nutmeg?
fact: Mace is the red seed covering (aril) wrapped around the nutmeg seed.

text: Pu-erh, a fermented and aged tea, comes from which Chinese province?
Which famous chef created the peach Melba for singer Nellie Melba?
fact: Escoffier was running the kitchen at London's Savoy Hotel at the time.

text: Which chilli held the Guinness record as the world's hottest from 2013 to 2023?
fact: It was overtaken by Pepper X, bred by the same grower.

text: Guanciale, the cured pork used in a true carbonara, comes from which part of the pig?
fact: Its name comes from "guancia", Italian for cheek.

text: Roquefort cheese is made from which animal's milk?
fact: By law it must be aged in the natural caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

text: Which nut grows hanging beneath a fruit known as an "apple"?
fact: Cashews are sold shelled because the shell holds an oil that irritates skin.

text: Katsuobushi, the shaved flakes used to make dashi, come from which fish?
In which country was the Caesar salad invented?
fact: It is credited to Italian immigrant Caesar Cardini, at his Tijuana restaurant in 1924.

text: Injera, a spongy flatbread made from teff, is a staple of which country?
What is "Bombay duck"?
fact: It is a lizardfish, traditionally dried in the sun.

text: Which pasta's name means "little tongues" in Italian?
What was Pepsi originally called when it was invented in 1893?
fact: Pharmacist Caleb Bradham renamed it Pepsi-Cola in 1898.

text: Red Bull was adapted from an energy drink from which country?
fact: The Thai original, Krating Daeng, means "red gaur", a type of wild bull.

text: In what year did Vegemite first go on sale?
In what year did William Arnott open his bakery in Newcastle, NSW?
In what year was the first Granny Smith apple found growing in Sydney?
How many grams of pure alcohol are in one Australian standard drink?
How many millilitres is one Australian tablespoon?
How many millilitres are in a standard bottle of wine?
KFC says its Original Recipe uses how many herbs and spices?
How many "varieties" does the famous Heinz slogan claim?
In what year was Coca-Cola first sold?
In what year did Australia's first McDonald's open, in Yagoona, Sydney?
In what year was pre-sliced bread first sold?
Scotch whisky must be aged for at least how many years?
How many kilojoules of energy are in one gram of fat?
How many millilitres are in a standard Australian can of soft drink?
Put these chillies in order of heat, mildest first.
Put these food brands in order of founding, earliest first.
Put these drinks in order of typical alcohol content, weakest first.
