In Minecraft, which block do you build a Nether portal frame from?
Pikachu evolves into which Pokémon when it is given a Thunder Stone?
fact: Pichu is the baby form that evolves into Pikachu.

text: In Among Us, what are the players who secretly sabotage and kill the crew called?
What is the made-up language spoken by the characters in The Sims called?
In Fortnite Battle Royale, what do players jump out of at the start of a match?
In Mario Kart, which item chases down the racer in first place and blows them up?
fact: Its official name is the Spiny Shell.

text: What are the cartoon avatars that players create on the Nintendo Wii called?
fact: The name blends "Wii" and "me".

text: In Angry Birds, which animals have stolen the birds' eggs?
Sonic the Hedgehog is the mascot of which games company?
Which company bought Minecraft's maker, Mojang, in 2014?
fact: The price was US$2.5 billion.

text: In the Halo games, what is the name of Master Chief's AI companion?
In Skyrim, the player's hero can absorb dragon souls and is known as the what?
Which company created Fortnite?
Supercell, the maker of Clash of Clans, is based in which country?
fact: Its head office is in Helsinki.

text: Charizard is part Fire type. What is its other type in its normal form?
fact: Only its Mega Charizard X form is part Dragon.

text: After its licence deal with FIFA ended, what did EA rename its football series in 2023?
fact: FIFA 23 was the last game under the old name.

text: In The Sims, what is the green crystal that hovers over the Sim you control called?
Who is the main character of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas?
fact: Everyone calls him CJ.

text: The line "The cake is a lie" comes from which game?
fact: Portal was released by Valve in 2007.

text: Which professor gives you your first Pokémon in Pokémon Red and Blue?
The Xbox 360's infamous hardware failure, shown by three red lights, was nicknamed what?
Captain Price and "Soap" MacTavish are the heroes of which branch of Call of Duty?
Which outlaw do you play for most of Red Dead Redemption 2?
fact: He rides with the Van der Linde gang.

text: Which Nintendo designer created both Mario and The Legend of Zelda?
fact: He also created Donkey Kong, Star Fox and Pikmin.

text: The tiny multiplayer map Nuketown first appeared in which Call of Duty game?
wrong: Call of Duty: Black Ops II

text: Which studio created Rocket League?
fact: It followed their 2008 game Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars.

text: Fruit Ninja was made by Halfbrick, a studio based in which Australian city?
fact: Halfbrick also made Jetpack Joyride.

text: In Minecraft, which boss drops the Nether Star needed to craft a beacon?
Luigi made his first appearance in which game?
fact: In the 1983 arcade game he was the character for player two.

text: Which designer created The Sims?
fact: He had the idea for a virtual doll's house after losing his home in a 1991 fire.

text: Flappy Bird, pulled from app stores in 2014, was made by a developer from which country?
fact: Dong Nguyen's game came out in 2013 and was removed in February 2014.

text: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, what is the name of Link's fairy guide?
fact: She is famous for calling out "Hey! Listen!"

text: Which game beat Red Dead Redemption 2 to Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2018?
Which was the first FIFA game to include women's national teams?
Nintendo was founded in 1889 to make what?
fact: They were handmade Japanese cards called hanafuda.

text: What is the name of the main five-a-side map in League of Legends?
Up to how many players drop into a standard Fortnite Battle Royale match?
How many Pokémon can you carry in your party at once in the main Pokémon games?
In what year was Pokémon Go released?
fact: Australia was one of the first three countries to get it, on 6 July.

text: In what year was the Nintendo DS first released?
In what year did Minecraft get its full official release, after its alpha and beta versions?
fact: The full release came on 18 November.

text: In what year was the first The Sims game released?
How many Power Stars are there to collect in the original Super Mario 64?
In what year was the very first Grand Theft Auto game released?
fact: It was made by DMA Design, which later became Rockstar North.

text: How many different falling pieces are there in standard Tetris?
fact: They are I, O, T, J, L, S and Z. The mirror-image pairs J/L and S/Z count separately.

text: Put these Nintendo consoles in order of first release, earliest first.
Put these Grand Theft Auto games in order of release, earliest first.
Put these games in order of first release, earliest first.
Put these pairs of Pokémon games in order of first release, earliest first.
Put these Call of Duty games in order of release, earliest first.
What is the capital of Canada?
fact: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

text: Which country's flag is a yellow cross on a blue background?
fact: All five Nordic countries fly an off-centre cross. Denmark's is the oldest.

text: Which strait separates Tasmania from mainland Australia?
fact: It is about 250 km wide and named after the explorer and surgeon George Bass.

text: Which river flows through the centre of Paris?
fact: The Seine runs 777 km and reaches the English Channel at Le Havre.

text: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
fact: Asia closes it off to the north.

text: The River Nile flows into which sea?
fact: It fans out into a delta that meets the sea between Alexandria and Port Said.

text: Table Mountain overlooks which South African city?
fact: The cloud that often spills over its flat top is called the tablecloth.

text: Which Australian capital city is built on the Swan River?
fact: The river's Noongar name is Derbarl Yerrigan.

text: Which is the largest US state by area?
fact: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas, the second largest.

text: What is the capital of Fiji?
fact: Suva is on Viti Levu. It was named capital in place of Levuka in 1877 and took over in 1882.

text: Ceuta and Melilla, two cities on the north coast of Africa, belong to which country?
fact: Both border Morocco, which has claimed them since 1956.

text: Which country's flag shows the temple of Angkor Wat?
fact: The temple appears in white on a red band between two blue ones.

text: How many official time zones does China use?
fact: China is wide enough to span five, but the whole country keeps Beijing time.

text: Which strait separates the Malay Peninsula from the Indonesian island of Sumatra?
Which Indian city was officially called Madras until 1996?
fact: The name changed on 17 July 1996.

text: Which desert covers much of southern Mongolia and northern China?
fact: It is a cold desert of about 1.3 million square km.

text: Which Pacific nation skipped 30 December 2011 to move west of the International Date Line?
fact: The jump put it on the same calendar day as Australia and New Zealand.

text: What is the world's largest sand island?
fact: It lies off the Queensland coast and was officially renamed K'gari in 2023.

text: What is the most easterly point of mainland Australia?
fact: The most westerly is Steep Point in WA. The most southerly is South Point in Victoria.

text: Niagara Falls is on the river that flows from Lake Erie into which other Great Lake?
fact: The falls span the border between Canada and the United States.

text: Ushuaia, long promoted as the world's southernmost city, is in which country?
fact: Chile's far smaller Puerto Williams lies further south and makes the same claim.

text: Victoria Falls is on which African river?
fact: The falls' local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means "the smoke that thunders".

text: Which is the only South American country with both a Pacific and a Caribbean coast?
fact: Its Caribbean coast is the longer of the two.

text: The flag Mozambique adopted in 1983 shows an AK-47 rifle crossed with which tool?
fact: They lie over an open book. The three stand for defence, production and education.

text: The WA border settlement of Eucla unofficially keeps its clocks how far ahead of Perth?
fact: Its UTC+8:45 sits exactly halfway between WA time and South Australia's standard time.

text: Which country is "doubly landlocked", bordered only by countries that are themselves landlocked?
fact: The only other is Liechtenstein, tucked between landlocked Switzerland and Austria.

text: Which is Australia's largest desert?
fact: It is more than 700 km wide and spans Western Australia and South Australia.

text: K2, the world's second-highest mountain, is in which mountain range?
fact: K2 stands 8,611 m high on the border of Pakistan and China.

text: After Tasmania, which is Australia's largest island?
fact: It is one of the Tiwi Islands, north of Darwin, and covers 5,786 square km.

text: Flying Fish Cove is the main settlement of which Australian territory?
fact: It is named after a British survey ship. Many maps just call it The Settlement.

text: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
fact: The move inland from Dar es Salaam was decided in the 1970s and took decades.

text: Russia's Kaliningrad exclave lies on the Baltic Sea between Poland and which country?
fact: Its main city was called Königsberg until 1946.

text: Which is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coast?
fact: It is also the smallest country in Central America.

text: What is the southernmost point of mainland Africa?
fact: Its name is Portuguese for "Cape of Needles".

text: Which is the only country crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn?
fact: The Tropic of Capricorn crosses ten countries. The Equator misses the other nine.

text: The Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip of land reaching to China, belongs to which country?
fact: It was drawn in the 1890s to keep the Russian and British empires apart.

text: How many stars are on the Australian national flag?
fact: The large Commonwealth Star has seven points. The other five make up the Southern Cross.

text: How many countries make up the United Kingdom?
fact: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

text: How many provinces does Canada have, not counting its territories?
fact: Newfoundland became the tenth in 1949. There are also three territories.

text: How many emirates make up the United Arab Emirates?
fact: Abu Dhabi is the largest by area. The others include Dubai, Sharjah and Ajman.

text: How many other states and territories share a border with South Australia?
fact: It borders WA, the NT, Queensland, NSW and Victoria.

text: In what year did the Channel Tunnel between England and France open?
fact: It runs about 50 km from Folkestone to Coquelles, near Calais.

text: How many countries share a land border with China?
fact: That ties China with Russia for the most land neighbours of any country.

text: As of 2025, how many time zones does Russia use?
fact: They run from UTC+2 on the Baltic to UTC+12 in Kamchatka.

text: In what year did Timor-Leste become fully independent, after a period of UN administration?
fact: Independence came on 20 May 2002. Indonesia had invaded in 1975.

text: Put these oceans in order of area, largest first.
Put these cities in the order they reach midnight on New Year's Eve, first to last.
Put these South American capitals in order from north to south, northernmost first.
Put these islands in order of area, largest first.
Put these Pacific nations in order of independence, earliest first.
Which major gives its champion a green jacket?
What is the famous trophy awarded to the winner of The Open?

fact: Wan directed and Whannell wrote the script. The shoot took just 18 days.

text: In the Australian horror film Talk to Me, what do the teenagers hold to contact spirits?
fact: It is set in Adelaide, and a spirit must be let go within 90 seconds.

text: Which Australian plays Annie, the mother at the centre of Hereditary (2018)?
fact: Annie works as a miniature artist.

text: Psycho (1960) was shot in black and white. What stood in for blood in the shower scene?
fact: Body double Marli Renfro recalled a can of watered-down syrup on the set.

text: Bela Lugosi's Dracula (1931) was shot by day. What did Universal film on the same sets at night?
fact: Carlos Villarías played the Count. Lugosi had already played the part on Broadway.

text: In the first Jaws film, which character says 'You're gonna need a bigger boat'?
fact: Roy Scheider played Brody, the police chief.

text: In Shaun of the Dead, which pub do Shaun and his friends hole up in?
fact: Edgar Wright directed it, the first of his Three Flavours Cornetto films.

text: The real Wolfe Creek crater, which gave Wolf Creek its name, is in which state or territory?
fact: The film drops the 'e'. It was shot almost entirely in South Australia.

text: George A. Romero shot Night of the Living Dead (1968) in farm country outside which US city?
fact: Nobody in the film says 'zombie'. The creatures are called ghouls.

text: Which English actor played Rick Grimes in The Walking Dead?
fact: He also played Mark in Love Actually (2003).

text: Kathy Bates won the Best Actress Oscar as Annie Wilkes in which film?
fact: James Caan played the novelist she holds captive. Rob Reiner directed.

text: Netflix's The Haunting of Hill House (2018) is based on a novel by which author?
fact: The novel came out in 1959. Mike Flanagan directed the series.

text: In Friday the 13th Part III (1982), Jason takes his first hockey mask from which character?
fact: In Part 2 he wore a sack over his head. Part III was released in 3D.

text: What was the first Scream film called while it was being written and shot?
fact: The old title was reused for a spoof comedy in 2000.

text: Who played the Monster's mate in Bride of Frankenstein (1935)?
fact: She also plays the novel's author in the opening scene.

text: Which was the first novel Stephen King published under the name Richard Bachman?
fact: A Washington bookshop clerk uncovered the pen name in 1985.

text: The Blair Witch Project is set in the woods near which Maryland town?
fact: Daniel Myrick and Eduardo Sánchez directed it.

text: Which 1981 film won the first Oscar in the new Best Makeup category?
fact: Rick Baker won it. Heartbeeps was the only other nominee.

text: Who composed the all-strings score for Hitchcock's Psycho (1960)?
fact: Hitchcock first wanted the shower scene to play with no music at all.

text: In the Japanese film Ring (1998), what is the name of the ghost who became Samara in the US remake?
fact: Hideo Nakata directed it, from a 1991 novel by Koji Suzuki.

text: Who played the creature in Alien (1979), inside a suit designed by H. R. Giger?
fact: Badejo was a very tall Nigerian student, spotted in a London pub. Giger was Swiss.

text: Midsommar is set in Sweden. In which country was it mostly filmed?
fact: It was shot around Budapest, with Florence Pugh as Dani.

text: Who played the vampire Count Orlok in the silent film Nosferatu (1922)?
fact: His surname is close to the German for 'terror'. The film was an unlicensed take on Dracula.

text: In Mary Shelley's novel, Frankenstein is a student at which university when he makes his creature?
fact: His first name is Victor. The Boris Karloff film renamed him Henry.

text: The Invisible Man (2020) is set in San Francisco. In which city was it mostly filmed?
fact: Elisabeth Moss stars. Street scenes were shot around Martin Place.

text: In The Ring (2002), how many days after watching the cursed tape does the viewer die?
fact: Gore Verbinski directed this remake of a Japanese hit.

text: In the first Gremlins film, how many rules come with looking after a mogwai?
fact: No bright light, no water, and no food after midnight.

text: In It (2017), the creature wakes to feed on the town of Derry every how many years?
fact: Bill Skarsgård played its clown form, Pennywise.

text: In The Shining (1980), what is the number of the hotel room Danny is warned to stay out of?
fact: In Stephen King's novel it is Room 217.

text: How many seasons did the original The Walking Dead series run for?
fact: It ran for 177 episodes, from 2010 to 2022.

text: In Candyman (1992), how many times must his name be said into a mirror to summon him?
fact: Tony Todd played him. The story comes from Clive Barker's The Forbidden.

text: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974) opens by dating its story to 18 August of which year?
fact: Gunnar Hansen played Leatherface. It was sold as a true story but is largely fiction.

text: How many Oscar nominations did The Exorcist (1973) receive?
fact: It won two, for its adapted screenplay and its sound.

text: In how many Hammer films did Christopher Lee play Count Dracula?
fact: The first was Dracula (1958). The last was The Satanic Rites of Dracula (1973).

text: Put these films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these zombie films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these 2010s horror films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these Stephen King novels in order of publication, earliest first.
Put these classic Universal monster films in order of release, earliest first.
In January 2019, a photo of what beat Kylie Jenner's record for the most-liked Instagram post?
fact: The account that posted it was called world_record_egg.

text: If you have been 'rickrolled', which song have you been tricked into hearing?
fact: Rick Astley released it in 1987.

text: In real life, what colours was 'The Dress' that divided the internet in 2015?
The Ice Bucket Challenge raised money to fight which disease?
fact: In the United States it is usually called ALS.

text: Which company bought YouTube in 2006?
fact: Google paid US$1.65 billion in shares.

text: Which lip-sync app was merged into TikTok in August 2018?
Which prime minister went viral in 2015 for biting into a raw onion?
fact: He did it on a visit to a produce farm in northern Tasmania in March 2015.

text: Which newspaper bought the word game Wordle in January 2022?
fact: Wordle was created by Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.

text: More than two million people signed up to a joke Facebook event to storm what?
fact: The event was subtitled They Can't Stop All of Us.

text: In Me at the zoo, the first video uploaded to YouTube, which animals are in the background?
fact: It stars YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim and was shot at San Diego Zoo.

text: The 'Doge' meme features which breed of dog?
fact: The dog in the best-known photo was called Kabosu.

text: Nyan Cat flies through space with a body made of what?
The 2012 viral hit Dumb Ways to Die was a safety campaign for which organisation?
fact: The video went up on YouTube in November 2012.

text: Which word, first recorded on an Australian web forum in 2002, was Oxford's Word of the Year for 2013?
fact: The 2002 post was on Dr Karl's Self-Serve Science Forum.

text: Satirical news site The Betoota Advocate is named after a deserted town in which state or territory?
fact: The site was founded in 2014.

text: After the public voted for Boaty McBoatface in 2016, who was the polar ship really named after?
fact: The name Boaty McBoatface went to one of the ship's submersibles.

text: 'Left Shark' danced out of step behind which singer at the 2015 Super Bowl?
The 'One does not simply walk into Mordor' meme quotes which Lord of the Rings character?
fact: Sean Bean says the line in The Fellowship of the Ring (2001).

text: 'Stan', slang for an obsessive fan, comes from a 2000 song by which rapper?
Which company bought the streaming site Twitch in 2014?
fact: Twitch began in 2011 as a gaming spin-off of Justin.tv.

text: Which whaling song set off TikTok's sea shanty craze in early 2021?
fact: Scottish singer Nathan Evans posted the version that went viral.

text: In the 'Democracy Manifest' video, what does the arrested man say he was eating?
fact: It was filmed in Brisbane in 1991 and put online in 2009.

text: Which pop star, raised in Perth, first found fans by singing on YouTube from 2007?
Which YouTube comedy duo was started by Ian Hecox and Anthony Padilla?
What was Snapchat called when it first launched?
fact: It was relaunched as Snapchat two months later.

text: What was the real name of Grumpy Cat, the internet's most famous frowning pet?
fact: A photo posted to Reddit in September 2012 made her famous.

text: Which producer made the track behind the Harlem Shake videos?
Which song was the usual soundtrack to the Mannequin Challenge?
fact: The song is by Rae Sremmurd.

text: In 2009, which squeaky-voiced character had the first YouTube channel to reach a million subscribers?
fact: Fred was created and played by Lucas Cruikshank.

text: Natalie Tran was Australia's most-subscribed YouTuber around 2009 under which channel name?
YouTube's three founders had all worked together at which company?
fact: They were Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim.

text: The star of the five-second 'Dramatic Chipmunk' clip is really what animal?
What is the name of Reddit's alien mascot?
What does the M stand for in ASMR?
fact: In full it is autonomous sensory meridian response.

text: In 2017 a teenager's plea for free nuggets became the most retweeted tweet so far. Which chain did he ask?
fact: Wendy's told him he would need 18 million retweets.

text: BeReal, the app that had everyone posting at the same random moment in 2022, came from which country?
Vine was built on looping videos of at most how many seconds?
fact: Twitter shut the app down in January 2017.

text: How many characters could a tweet hold before the limit was doubled in 2017?
How many hours does a Snapchat Story stay up before it disappears?
In what year was Twitter rebranded as X?
fact: The change was made in July of that year.

text: How many subscribers does a YouTube channel need to earn the Gold Play Button?
fact: Silver is for 100,000 subscribers and Diamond for 10 million.

text: In what year did the dating app Tinder launch?
fact: It arrived on Apple's App Store in September 2012.

text: In what year was Charlie Bit My Finger uploaded to YouTube?
In January 2022, Baby Shark Dance became the first YouTube video to reach how many billion views?
fact: It was made by Pinkfong, a South Korean company.

text: In what year did Netflix launch in Australia?
fact: It went live here and in New Zealand on 24 March.

text: Put these apps in order of launch, earliest first.
Put these YouTube videos in order of upload, earliest first.
Hungarian journalist László Bíró gave his name to which everyday invention?
fact: He noticed that newspaper ink dried fast, and used a tiny rolling ball to lay it on paper.

text: Swiss engineer George de Mestral invented what after burrs stuck to his dog on a walk?
fact: Under a microscope he saw tiny hooks. The name blends the French words velours and crochet.

text: Raytheon engineer Percy Spencer noticed a snack melting in his pocket. Which invention followed?
fact: He was working on magnetrons for radar sets. Popcorn was among the first things he tested.

text: Alfred Nobel, who left his fortune to fund the Nobel Prizes, made much of it from which invention?
fact: He patented it in 1867. The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901.

text: Which Australian science agency earned hundreds of millions of dollars from its Wi-Fi patent?
fact: The idea grew out of radio astronomy. Royalties and settlements had passed $430 million by 2012.

text: Despite its name, what colour is an aircraft's "black box" flight recorder painted?
fact: The colour makes it easier to find among wreckage.

text: James Dyson made his name in the 1990s by removing what from the vacuum cleaner?
fact: He says he built 5,127 prototypes before his cyclone design worked.

text: Which American founding father is credited with inventing the lightning rod?
fact: He never patented his inventions, saying they should be shared freely.

text: Which office product grew out of a 3M glue that turned out too weak to hold anything for good?
fact: Art Fry of 3M wanted bookmarks that would stay put in his hymn book at choir practice.

text: Larry Page and Sergey Brin began which company as a Stanford research project called BackRub?
fact: BackRub judged how important a web page was by the links pointing to it.

text: Which Google product grew out of Where 2 Technologies, a Sydney start-up bought in 2004?
fact: Danish brothers Lars and Jens Rasmussen built it with Noel Gordon and Stephen Ma.

text: Which Hollywood star co-patented a "frequency hopping" radio system for guiding torpedoes in 1942?
fact: Her co-inventor was the composer George Antheil. The US Navy shelved the idea for years.

text: Chemist Stephanie Kwolek discovered which super-strong fibre at DuPont in 1965?
fact: Weight for weight, it is about five times stronger than steel.

text: The first SMS text message, sent in Britain in December 1992, said what?
fact: Engineer Neil Papworth typed it on a computer. Phones could not yet send texts.

text: Bluetooth wireless technology is named after what?
fact: Harald Bluetooth united Denmark and Norway. The logo joins the runes for his initials, H and B.
wrong: A blue chip in the prototype
A Swedish phrase for short link

text: Before they built aeroplanes, the Wright brothers ran what kind of business in Dayton, Ohio?
fact: Profits from the Wright Cycle Company helped pay for their flying experiments.

text: Josephine Cochrane patented the first commercially successful version of which appliance in 1886?
fact: Hotels and restaurants were her first customers, long before home kitchens.

text: Around 1980, Bruce Thompson of the Australian firm Caroma developed which water-saving device?
fact: A federal government grant in the late 1970s helped Caroma pay for the research.

text: A balloon built by which French brothers carried the first people in free flight, in 1783?
fact: Two passengers drifted over Paris for about 25 minutes on 21 November 1783.

text: In a famous 1968 demo in San Francisco, Douglas Engelbart first showed the public which computer device?
fact: His patent called it an "X-Y position indicator". Bill English built the first one in 1964.

text: Engineer Steven Sasson built the first handheld digital camera in 1975 at which company?
fact: It took 23 seconds to save a single 0.01-megapixel picture to a cassette tape.

text: Which Scottish inventor gave the first public demonstration of television, in London in 1926?
fact: Guests in his Soho laboratory watched the flickering face of a ventriloquist's dummy.

text: In which city did Lance Hill start making the Hills Hoist in his backyard in the 1940s?
fact: He built the first for his wife in 1945, at their home in the suburb of Glenunga.

text: Earle Dickson of Johnson & Johnson invented what for his wife, who kept cutting herself cooking?
fact: His ready-made strip let her dress small cuts without anyone's help.

text: In the "war of the currents", Edison's direct current lost out to the AC system of which businessman?
fact: He struck a deal for Nikola Tesla's AC motor patents in 1888.

text: On 14 February 1876, the same day as Bell, who lodged a rival telephone design at the US Patent Office?
fact: Gray filed a caveat, a notice of an invention in progress. Bell's patent was issued on 7 March.

text: Which English chemist made a working light bulb independently of Edison, then merged firms with him?
fact: Their joint British company, formed in 1883, was known as Ediswan.

text: Which Apple co-founder sold his 10% stake back for US$800 just 12 days after the company was formed?
fact: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak held 45% each. Wayne has said he does not regret it.

text: Registered on 15 March 1985, what was the first .com domain name?
fact: Symbolics made computers in Massachusetts. The next .com, bbn.com, came in April 1985.

text: Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes, often called the first computer program, were written for which machine?
fact: Charles Babbage designed it but never built it. Her program worked out Bernoulli numbers.

text: Microsoft built MS-DOS from 86-DOS, a system it bought in 1981 from which company?
fact: Tim Paterson wrote it in four months and nicknamed it QDOS: Quick and Dirty Operating System.

text: B.F. Goodrich coined the word "zipper" for which product fitted with the new fastener?
fact: The fastener itself was the work of Swedish-born engineer Gideon Sundback.

text: In 1974, what was the first product sold by scanning a UPC barcode, at a supermarket in Ohio?
fact: It was a ten-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit, rung up for 67 cents.

text: The oldest known wooden wheel, about 5,200 years old, was dug out of a marsh in which country?
fact: Found near Ljubljana in 2002, it was made of ash and still had its oak axle.

text: Whose 1712 "atmospheric engine" pumped water out of mines decades before James Watt improved on it?
fact: It went to work at a coal mine near Dudley Castle in the English Midlands.

text: In 1957, the inventors of Bubble Wrap were actually trying to make what?
fact: The wallpaper flopped. Its big break was protecting IBM computers in transit.

text: How many letters are on the top letter row of a standard QWERTY keyboard?
fact: They are Q, W, E, R, T, Y, U, I, O and P. The layout dates from the 1870s.

text: In what year did Sony's first Walkman go on sale?
fact: The TPS-L2 cassette player went on sale in Japan on 1 July.

text: In what year did Australia issue its first polymer banknote, a $10 note?
fact: It marked the bicentenary. A full series of polymer notes followed from 1992 to 1996.

text: A standard Australian patent lasts for up to how many years?
fact: Patents on pharmaceutical substances can run for up to 25 years.

text: In what year did Barclays unveil what is generally seen as the world's first cash machine, in London?
fact: It opened at the Enfield branch on 27 June. A Swedish rival followed nine days later.

text: How many US patents were granted to Thomas Edison?
In what year did Samuel Morse telegraph "What hath God wrought" from Washington to Baltimore?
fact: He sent it from the US Capitol on 24 May to his partner Alfred Vail.

text: In what year did Motorola's Martin Cooper make the first public call on a handheld mobile phone?
fact: Standing on a New York street, he rang Joel Engel, his rival at AT&T.

text: In what year did the Lumière brothers hold their first paying public film screening, in Paris?
fact: It was held on 28 December in the Salon Indien of the Grand Café.

text: Put these ways of listening to music in order of when they first appeared, earliest first.
Put these Australian inventions in order, earliest first.
Put these transport firsts in order, earliest first.
Put these computing milestones in order, earliest first.
Put these in order of when they were patented, earliest first.
In Round the Twist, what kind of building does the Twist family live in?
fact: The show is set in the fictional coastal town of Port Niranda.

text: Healthy Harold, who visited schools in the Life Education van, is what kind of animal?
What is the name of SpongeBob SquarePants's pet snail?
fact: Gary meows like a cat.

text: In Club Penguin, what were the little pets your penguin could adopt called?
fact: Disney bought Club Penguin in August 2007.

text: In High School Musical, what is East High's basketball team called?
fact: The film premiered on Disney Channel in January 2006.

text: In the English version of Beyblade, what do bladers shout as they launch?
fact: The first Beyblade tops went on sale in Japan in 1999.

text: In Despicable Me (2010), what does Gru set out to shrink and steal?
In Hannah Montana, what is the name of the schoolgirl who is secretly Hannah?
fact: Miley Stewart is the character. Miley Cyrus is the actor who plays her.

text: Tazos, the collectable discs of the schoolyard, came free inside packets of what?
fact: Australia's first Tazos set, in 1995, featured Looney Tunes characters.

text: In The Saddle Club, what is the name of the stables where the girls ride?
In Blue Water High, what is the name of the surf academy?
fact: The teenagers win a place in its 12-month surfing program.

text: Saturday Disney ran for more than 26 years on which Australian network?
fact: The first episode went to air on 27 January 1990.

text: Who took over from Greg Page as the Yellow Wiggle in 2006?
fact: Page retired because of ill health, and Moran had been his understudy.

text: In The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, the twins live in which Boston hotel?
In Kim Possible, what kind of animal is Ron Stoppable's pet, Rufus?
In the cartoon Arthur, what kind of animal is Arthur?
fact: Arthur Read lives in the fictional Elwood City.

text: Which George Miller film won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature at the 2007 ceremony?
fact: It beat Cars and Monster House.

text: In Toy Story 3, what does the villainous teddy bear Lotso smell of?
In Diary of a Wimpy Kid, who is Greg Heffley's best friend?
fact: Rodrick and Manny are Greg's brothers.

text: Which of these was NOT one of the five sports in the original Wii Sports?
fact: The five were tennis, baseball, bowling, golf and boxing.

text: On MSN Messenger, what did sending someone a 'nudge' do?
fact: Microsoft retired Messenger in 2013 in favour of Skype.
wrong: Rang them for a voice call

text: Sunnyboy ice blocks, sold until 2016, came in what shape?
fact: The maker stopped production in September 2016, blaming falling demand.

text: Which Japanese company makes Tamagotchi?
fact: The first Tamagotchi went on sale in Japan in November 1996.

text: In Tomorrow, When the War Began, what do the teenagers call their bush hideout?
fact: John Marsden's novel was published in 1993.

text: What flavour is a Rainbow Paddle Pop?
In Kung Fu Panda, what kind of bird is Po's adoptive father, Mr Ping?
fact: Mr Ping runs the most popular noodle shop in the Valley of Peace.

text: In Moshi Monsters, what was the name of the city your monster lived in?
fact: The original game closed in December 2019.

text: Who illustrates Andy Griffiths's Treehouse books?
fact: The first book, The 13-Storey Treehouse, came out in 2011.

text: Who wrote the Deltora Quest books?
fact: The Belt of Deltora holds seven gems.

text: Who hosted the Australian version of Prank Patrol on ABC3?
fact: It first aired in December 2009 on the then-new ABC3.

text: In Zoey 101, what is the name of Zoey's boarding school?
LazyTown, home of Sportacus and Stephanie, was made in which country?
fact: Sportacus calls fruit and vegetables 'sports candy'.

text: Which of these was NOT one of the four original Bratz dolls of 2001?
fact: Yasmin was the fourth. Meygan joined in 2002.

text: In Totally Spies!, what is the name of the agency Sam, Clover and Alex work for?
fact: It stands for the World Organization of Human Protection.

text: Crazy Frog went to No. 1 in Australia in 2005 with a version of which tune?
fact: Harold Faltermeyer wrote it for the 1984 film Beverly Hills Cop.

text: Mathletics, the online maths game played in classrooms, was created in which country?
fact: 3P Learning launched it for Australian schools in 2005.

text: In H2O: Just Add Water, how many seconds after touching water do the girls turn into mermaids?
fact: The girls get their powers on Mako Island.

text: In Finding Nemo, P. Sherman lives at what number Wallaby Way, Sydney?
In Phineas and Ferb, how many days of summer vacation do the boys have to fill?
In Lilo & Stitch, Stitch is also known as Experiment number what?
In the beep test, how many metres apart are the two lines you run between?
fact: A shorter 15-metre version of the test also exists.

text: In what year were the first NAPLAN tests held?
fact: Students sit the tests in Years 3, 5, 7 and 9.

text: In what year was the Nokia 3310 released?
fact: It came with four games: Snake II, Space Impact, Bantumi and Pairs II.

text: In what year did the original Club Penguin shut down?
fact: Its servers were switched off on 30 March 2017.

text: Apple's first iPod promised to put how many songs in your pocket?
Put these gadgets in order of first release, earliest first.
Put these DreamWorks films in order of release, earliest first.
Put these Disney Channel shows in order of their first episode, earliest first.

The Taj Mahal is in which Indian city?
fact: Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631.

text: Which architect designed Barcelona's Sagrada Família?
fact: Work began in 1882 under another architect. Gaudí took over the following year.

text: The Big Banana, one of Australia's first Big Things, stands in which NSW city?
What nickname do Sydneysiders give the Sydney Harbour Bridge?
The Inca citadel of Machu Picchu is in which country?
fact: It sits 2,430 m above sea level, where the Andes meet the Amazon basin.

text: Which prehistoric monument stands on Salisbury Plain in the south of England?
fact: It is about 13 km north of the city of Salisbury, in Wiltshire.

text: Which Gothic cathedral in Paris lost its roof and spire to a fire in April 2019?
fact: It reopened in December 2024 after five years of repairs.

text: In Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol, Tom Cruise climbs the outside of which skyscraper?
fact: Cruise did the climb himself, on the real tower in Dubai.

text: The Olympic stadium nicknamed the Bird's Nest is in which city?
fact: It hosted the ceremonies of both the 2008 Summer Games and the 2022 Winter Games.

text: The Alhambra, the hilltop palace of the Nasrid emirs, overlooks which Spanish city?
fact: Most of it dates from the 13th and 14th centuries.

text: What is the official name of the colour of the Golden Gate Bridge?
fact: Architect Irving Morrow chose it. The US Navy had wanted black and yellow stripes.

text: London's 30 St Mary Axe is better known by which nickname?
fact: Foster + Partners designed the 41-storey tower, which opened in 2004.

text: Whose engineering firm designed the iron skeleton inside the Statue of Liberty?
fact: He took over after the first engineer, Viollet-le-Duc, died in 1879.

text: Which architect designed New York's spiral Guggenheim Museum, opened in 1959?
fact: Wright died six months before it opened.

text: How was most of the Sydney Opera House's $102 million cost paid for?
fact: The Opera House Lottery ran from 1957 to 1986. The first estimate was $7 million.
wrong: A toll on the Harbour Bridge

text: How did Francis de Groot upstage Premier Jack Lang at the opening of the Sydney Harbour Bridge?
fact: He rode in on a borrowed horse and was fined £5. Lang then cut the ribbon as planned.
answer: Cut the ribbon with his sword
wrong: Flew a plane under the arch
Climbed the arch with a flag

text: Which reservoir was created by the building of Hoover Dam?
fact: The dam stands in Black Canyon, on the border of Nevada and Arizona.

text: Which country began digging the Panama Canal in 1881, only for its canal company to collapse within a decade?
fact: Ferdinand de Lesseps, builder of the Suez Canal, led the effort. The US took over in 1904.

text: Which of these was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007?
fact: The winners were announced in Lisbon on 7 July 2007. The Opera House was a losing finalist.

text: The word Brutalism is linked to the French phrase "béton brut". What does that phrase mean?
fact: The critic Reyner Banham made the term famous in Britain in the 1950s.

text: In 2004, who became the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, architecture's top honour?
fact: She was born in Baghdad and became a British citizen.

text: Which ancient city supplied the temple of the Holy Grail in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade?
fact: The facade is the Treasury, Al-Khazneh, reached through a narrow canyon called the Siq.

text: The MCG's Shane Warne Stand went by what name until 2022?
fact: The new name was unveiled at Warne's state memorial service on 30 March 2022.

text: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century as a temple to which Hindu god?
fact: King Suryavarman II built it. It later became a Buddhist temple.

text: Jørn Utzon solved the Opera House roof by cutting every shell from the surface of which shape?
fact: His team tried parabolas and ellipsoids before landing on the answer.

text: Which architect led the design of Parliament House in Canberra, opened in 1988?
fact: The winning design was picked in June 1980 from 329 entries.

text: At 11 am on 11 November, a ray of sunlight in Melbourne's Shrine of Remembrance lights up which word?
fact: It is part of "Greater love hath no man", carved on the Stone of Remembrance.

text: Who ran the building of the Brooklyn Bridge day to day after her husband, its chief engineer, fell ill?
fact: She was the first person to cross the finished bridge, riding in a carriage.

text: The Channel Tunnel is really how many tunnels running side by side?
fact: Two carry trains. A smaller service tunnel runs between them.

text: The Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, stood in which city?
fact: Ephesus is in western Turkey. A single column marks the temple's site today.

text: Copenhagen's Little Mermaid statue was paid for by the son of the founder of which brewery?
fact: Carl Jacobsen ordered it after seeing a ballet of the fairy tale. It was unveiled in 1913.

text: Which architect's master plan shaped Chandigarh, the capital built for Indian Punjab in the 1950s?
fact: His Capitol Complex there joined the World Heritage list in 2016.

text: Which Art Deco skyscraper won a 1929 race to be the world's tallest with a spire hidden inside it?
fact: It beat 40 Wall Street, then lost the title to the Empire State Building in 1931.

text: Work on which German cathedral began in 1248 and did not finish until 1880?
fact: Building stalled for centuries and only started again in the 1800s.

text: Nakatomi Plaza in Die Hard (1988) is really which Los Angeles tower?
fact: Ronald Reagan kept an office on its 34th floor after leaving the White House.

text: Japan's Himeji Castle is nicknamed after which white bird?
fact: Its nickname is Shirasagi-jo, the White Heron Castle. It joined the World Heritage list in 1993.

text: How many presidents' faces are carved into Mount Rushmore?
fact: Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln, each about 18 m tall.

text: In what year did the Sydney Opera House open?
fact: Queen Elizabeth II opened it on 20 October, 14 years after building began.

text: In what year did the Sydney Harbour Bridge open?
fact: Premier Jack Lang opened it on 19 March.

text: In what year was the climb on Uluru closed for good, as its Anangu owners had long asked?
fact: It closed on 26 October, the anniversary of the day the park was handed back to them.

text: How many passenger capsules does the London Eye have?
fact: They are numbered 1 to 33, because there is no capsule 13.

text: How many towers does the finished design of Barcelona's Sagrada Família call for?
fact: Twelve for the apostles, four for the evangelists, one for Mary and one for Jesus.

text: How many minarets does Istanbul's Blue Mosque have?
fact: Its official name is the Sultan Ahmed Mosque. Building began in 1609 under Sultan Ahmed I.

text: In what year did San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge open?
fact: Walkers crossed first, on 27 May. Cars followed the next day.

text: In what year did the original Wembley Stadium, with its twin towers, open?
fact: Its first event was the "White Horse" FA Cup final, won by Bolton Wanderers.

Arabic is written in which direction?
fact: Hebrew runs the same way.

text: 'Kia ora' is a greeting in which language?
fact: Literally it is a wish to 'be well' or 'have life'.

text: What is Auslan?
fact: It is closely related to British Sign Language and spells with a two-handed alphabet.
wrong: An Aboriginal language of the NT

text: Which of these words is a palindrome, reading the same backwards as forwards?
fact: The word comes from Greek roots meaning 'running back again'.

text: 'Kindergarten' is a German word that literally means what?
fact: Friedrich Fröbel coined it in 1840 for his institute for small children.

text: Newspeak is the official language of the state in which novel?
fact: George Orwell made it the language of Oceania, his totalitarian superstate.

text: Which language opens a question with an upside-down question mark?
fact: The Royal Spanish Academy recommended the mark in 1754.

text: Which of these is the Japanese word for 'cheers' when raising a glass?
fact: It is written with characters meaning 'dry cup'.

text: 'Hakuna matata', made famous by The Lion King, is a phrase in which language?
fact: It means 'no worries' or 'no trouble'.

text: English belongs to which branch of the Indo-European language family?
fact: Its closest relatives include Scots and Frisian.

text: By Ethnologue's count, which country has more living languages than any other?
fact: Ethnologue lists more than 800 there. Indonesia comes second with more than 700.

text: Which Japanese script is mainly used to write words borrowed from other languages?
fact: Hiragana handles word endings and grammar, and kanji most of the core vocabulary.

text: In Morse code, which letter is a single dot?
fact: E is the most common letter in English, so it was given the shortest code.

text: The word 'emoji' comes from two Japanese words meaning what?
fact: Any likeness to the English words 'emotion' and 'emoticon' is pure coincidence.

text: In Italian, what are 'peperoni'?
fact: It is the plural of peperone. A small hot chilli is a peperoncino.

text: The 'al' at the start of 'alcohol' and 'alchemy' is the Arabic word for what?
fact: Alcohol goes back to al-kuhl, a fine powder used to darken the eyelids: kohl.

text: Spanish 'embarazada' looks like 'embarrassed' to English speakers. What does it usually mean?
fact: Someone who is embarrassed is 'avergonzada' or 'avergonzado'.

text: The distress call 'Mayday' comes from a phrase in which language?
fact: It echoes 'm'aider', help me. A radio officer at Croydon Airport devised it in the 1920s.

text: 'Trivia' goes back to trivium, the Latin for a place where what meet?
fact: Trivium joins tri, three, and via, road.

text: 'Klutz', 'schmooze' and 'chutzpah' all came into English from which language?
fact: Klutz goes back to a word for a wooden beam, and schmooze to one meaning to chat.

text: The Aussie insult 'drongo' is thought to come from a 1920s what?
fact: Drongo had 37 starts without a win, though he ran second in a VRC Derby.
wrong: Boxer who never won a bout

text: 'Yakka', as in hard yakka, comes from an Aboriginal language of which area?
fact: It comes from yaga, meaning work, in the Yagara language.

text: Linguist Marc Okrand developed which language for the screen?
fact: He built it for Star Trek III and went on to write The Klingon Dictionary.

text: The joke spelling 'ghoti' mocks English spelling. Which word is it meant to spell?
fact: Gh as in tough, o as in women, ti as in nation. It dates back to at least 1855.

text: Which official language of the European Union is Semitic, descended from Arabic?
fact: It is also the only Semitic language officially written in the Latin alphabet.

text: Which king of Korea's Joseon dynasty is credited with creating the Hangul alphabet?
fact: Most scholars believe he was closely involved in the work himself.

text: On signs like 'Ye Olde Shoppe', the Y stands in for which lost English letter?
fact: Thorn made a 'th' sound, so 'Ye' was simply read as 'the'.

text: The Italian greeting 'ciao' comes from a Venetian phrase meaning what?
fact: It was a polite way of saying 'at your service'.

text: The 'honcho' in 'head honcho' reached English from which language?
fact: It comes from hanchō, meaning squad leader.

text: The 'amok' in 'run amok' is a word from which language?
fact: In Malay, amuk meant a furious attack.

text: The word 'bungalow' first meant a house in the style of which region?
fact: The Hindi word bangla means 'of Bengal'.

text: In the Noongar language of south-west WA, what is a 'kylie'?
fact: The Australian National Dictionary Centre says the girl's name may be based on it.

text: Tolkien modelled the sounds of Sindarin, one of his Elvish languages, on which real language?
fact: Finnish was an early inspiration for Quenya, his other main Elvish tongue.

text: American Sign Language is most closely related to the sign language of which country?
fact: About 58 per cent of its signs have been matched to that country's old sign language.

text: A word in the Latin Vulgate Bible led Michelangelo to carve which figure with horns?
fact: The Hebrew is now read as his face shining. The King James Bible gave him no horns.

text: Who is known as the reviver of Hebrew as an everyday spoken language?
fact: His son, raised only in Hebrew, became its first native speaker of modern times.

text: How many national languages does Switzerland have?
fact: The smallest is Romansh, spoken by about half a per cent of the population.

text: The French for this number is 'quatre-vingt-dix', literally 'four twenties ten'. What is it?
fact: Belgians and Swiss say 'nonante' instead.

text: How many letters are in the word 'antidisestablishmentarianism'?
fact: It means opposing the removal of a church's official status in the state.

text: In what year did Oxford Dictionaries name an emoji, Face with Tears of Joy, its Word of the Year?
fact: Oxford found it was the most used emoji in the world that year.

text: How many dot positions make up a single braille cell?
fact: Two columns of three dots give 64 possible patterns, counting the blank one.

text: In what year did Māori become an official language of New Zealand?
fact: The same Act set up a commission to promote the language.

text: In what year did Turkey pass the law replacing Arabic script with a Latin alphabet?
fact: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk drove the change. The new alphabet has 29 letters.

text: In what year was Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language published?
fact: He compiled its 42,773 entries almost single-handed.

text: In what year did Google Translate launch?
fact: It switched to neural machine translation in 2016.

Complicated and Sk8er Boi were hits for which singer?
fact: Both are on her debut album, Let Go, released in 2002.

text: Hey Ya! was a 2003 hit for which duo?
fact: André 3000 wrote and produced it. It was No. 1 in the US for nine weeks.

text: Boulevard of Broken Dreams and Holiday are on which Green Day album?
fact: The album came out in September 2004.

text: Who won the first season of Australian Idol?
fact: Shannon Noll was the runner-up.

text: Mr. Brightside was the debut single of which band?
fact: It first came out in the UK in September 2003 and is on the album Hot Fuss.

text: Which singer had a 2007 hit with Umbrella?
fact: It spent 10 weeks in a row at No. 1 in the UK.

text: Just Dance and Poker Face are on which Lady Gaga album?
fact: Paparazzi and LoveGame are on it too.

text: Which singer had a 2001 hit with Strawberry Kisses?
fact: It entered the ARIA singles chart at No. 2 that June.

text: Which duo had hits with 4ever and Untouched?
fact: Twins Lisa and Jessica Origliasso formed the duo in Brisbane in 2004.

text: Which rapper features on Beyoncé's hit Crazy in Love?
fact: It was the lead single from her first solo album, Dangerously in Love.

text: What is the title of Justin Timberlake's first solo album, released in 2002?
fact: The Neptunes produced most of it. It came out that November.

text: At the 2009 MTV VMAs, Kanye West interrupted Taylor Swift to praise which video?
fact: Swift had just won Best Female Video for You Belong with Me.

text: Which Jet song was used in a worldwide TV ad campaign for Apple's iPod?
fact: It also topped Triple J's Hottest 100 of 2003.
answer: Are You Gonna Be My Girl

text: Scar and The Special Two are on which Missy Higgins album?
fact: Her debut album, it came out in September 2004 and reached No. 1.

text: Which Powderfinger song topped Triple J's Hottest 100 of 2000?
fact: It also won Single of the Year at the 2001 ARIA Awards.

text: Last Nite and Someday are on which album by The Strokes?
fact: Their debut album, it was released first in Australia, on 30 July 2001.

text: Which member of Linkin Park rapped alongside singer Chester Bennington?
fact: Hahn was the band's DJ, Delson played lead guitar and Bourdon played drums.

text: Kanye West's 2007 hit Stronger is built on a sample of which French duo?
fact: The sample comes from Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger (2001).

text: Which producer made Get Ur Freak On and Work It with Missy Elliott?
fact: Get Ur Freak On came out in 2001 and Work It in 2002.

text: Britney Spears sang I'm a Slave 4 U at the MTV VMAs with what draped over her shoulders?
fact: It was a live albino Burmese python. A tiger was on stage too.

text: The 2001 hit version of Lady Marmalade came from the soundtrack of which film?
fact: Christina Aguilera, Lil' Kim, Mýa and Pink sang it. Missy Elliott co-produced it.

text: Which Radiohead album came out in 2007 as a download that fans could name their own price for?
fact: The download went up on 10 October 2007, and paying nothing was allowed.

text: In OK Go's 2006 video for Here It Goes Again, what does the band dance on?
fact: There are eight treadmills, and the video is one continuous take.

text: After Blink-182 went on hiatus in 2005, Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker formed which band?
fact: Tom DeLonge formed Angels & Airwaves the same year.

text: In September 2007, Kanye West's Graduation outsold which 50 Cent album released the same day?
fact: Graduation sold 957,000 copies in its first US week to Curtis's 691,000.

text: Before Empire of the Sun, Luke Steele fronted which Perth band?
fact: His partner in Empire of the Sun is Nick Littlemore of Pnau.

text: Which act's album Apocalypso won the ARIA for Album of the Year in 2008?
fact: The Presets and Gabriella Cilmi each won six ARIA Awards in 2008.

text: In April 2006, which song became the first UK No. 1 single on download sales alone?
fact: It sold more than 31,000 downloads that week and stayed at No. 1 for nine weeks.

text: Hearts a Mess is on which Gotye album, released in 2006?
fact: It was his second album, after Boardface (2003).

text: Kylie Minogue won her first Grammy, in 2004, for which song?
fact: It won Best Dance Recording. Love at First Sight and Slow were only nominated.
wrong: Can't Get You Out of My Head

text: Silverchair's Daniel Johns made a 2004 album with Paul Mac under which name?
fact: Their self-titled album reached No. 12 on the ARIA albums chart.

text: Gary Jules's Mad World, the UK Christmas No. 1 of 2003, kept which band's festive single at No. 2?
fact: Jules recorded the cover with Michael Andrews for the 2001 film Donnie Darko.

text: Sugar, We're Goin Down is on which Fall Out Boy album?
fact: Released in May 2005, it was the band's major label debut.

text: Mark Ronson's 2007 hit Valerie, sung by Amy Winehouse, was first recorded by which band?
fact: The Zutons released it in 2006. Ronson's version reached No. 2 in the UK.

text: Who was Pharrell Williams's partner in the production duo The Neptunes?
fact: Their hits as producers include Britney Spears's I'm a Slave 4 U.

text: Wolfmother won a Grammy in 2007 for which song?
fact: It won Best Hard Rock Performance.

text: In what year did Australian Idol first go to air?
fact: The first episode aired on Network Ten on 27 July.

text: How many members did the Black Eyed Peas have when Where Is the Love? came out in 2003?
fact: They were will.i.am, apl.de.ap, Taboo and Fergie, who had joined in 2002.

text: In what year did Eminem release The Marshall Mathers LP?
fact: It sold 1.76 million copies in its first week in the US.

text: In what year did Britney Spears and Justin Timberlake wear matching denim to the American Music Awards?
fact: The awards were held on 8 January. Spears later called the look tacky.

text: In what year did Arctic Monkeys release their debut album?
fact: It was then the fastest-selling debut album in British chart history.

text: In what year did Lady Gaga release her debut single, Just Dance?
fact: It came out in April and reached No. 1 in Australia that September.

text: For how many weeks in total was Delta Goodrem's Innocent Eyes No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart?
fact: It was also Australia's best-selling album of 2003.

text: How many Australian shows did Pink play on her Funhouse Tour in 2009?
fact: Seventeen of them were at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne.

text: In what year did Powderfinger and Silverchair tour together as Across the Great Divide?
fact: The tour backed Reconciliation Australia and ran from late August to late October.

Which dance move did Michael Jackson first perform on TV in 1983, while singing Billie Jean?
fact: It was on the special Motown 25, taped in March 1983 and shown that May.

text: Ray Parker Jr. sang the theme song of which 1984 film?
fact: The song spent three weeks at No. 1 in the US in 1984.

text: Who sang the 1988 duet Especially for You with Kylie Minogue?
fact: Stock Aitken Waterman wrote and produced it.

text: Which band released the 1987 album Appetite for Destruction?
fact: It includes Welcome to the Jungle, Sweet Child o' Mine and Paradise City.

text: Queen made the 1981 hit Under Pressure with which singer?
fact: It was recorded at Mountain Studios in Montreux, Switzerland.

text: Which rock band joined Run-DMC on their 1986 version of Walk This Way?
fact: Steven Tyler and Joe Perry took part. The version is on the album Raising Hell.

text: Which instrument plays the famous riff in Men at Work's Down Under?
fact: Greg Ham played it. In 2010 a court ruled it reproduced part of the song Kookaburra.

text: Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart had a 1983 hit with Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This) as which duo?
fact: Both had been in The Tourists, who split in 1980.

text: Need You Tonight and Never Tear Us Apart are on which INXS album?
fact: Need You Tonight is the band's only US No. 1 single.

text: What was Kylie Minogue's first single, released in 1987?
fact: It was No. 1 in Australia for seven weeks. Little Eva had the first hit with it in 1962.

text: Which was the first music video shown on MTV when the channel launched?
fact: It is by The Buggles: Trevor Horn and Geoff Downes.

text: Who played both Live Aid shows on the same day, flying from London to the US on Concorde?
fact: A helicopter flown by TV host Noel Edmonds took him from Wembley to Heathrow.

text: Which band recorded the 1985 James Bond theme A View to a Kill?
fact: The song reached No. 1 on the US Hot 100 in 1985.

text: Livin' on a Prayer and You Give Love a Bad Name are on which Bon Jovi album?
fact: Bruce Fairbairn produced it. It came out in August 1986.

text: Which band had a 1986 hit with Manic Monday, a song written by Prince?
fact: He was credited as 'Christopher'. It peaked at No. 2 in the US, behind his own Kiss.

text: Which Crowded House song reached No. 2 on the US Hot 100 in April 1987?
fact: Neil Finn has said it was pretty much written in a day.

text: Finish the title of Paul Kelly's 1985 song: From St Kilda to...
fact: He wrote it on Don Walker's piano while staying at Walker's flat.

text: Which catchphrase did Molly Meldrum use on Countdown when tipping an album?
fact: ABC rules stopped him telling viewers outright to buy a record.

text: Which future sitcom star is pulled on stage in Bruce Springsteen's Dancing in the Dark video?
fact: Brian De Palma directed the video in 1984, a decade before Friends began.

text: Which pop duo played concerts in Beijing and Guangzhou in April 1985?
fact: The ten-day visit was billed as the first to China by a Western pop group.

text: Which song opened Queen's set at Live Aid?
fact: They played six songs and closed with We Are the Champions.

text: Madonna's Into the Groove features in which 1985 film, in which she also starred?
fact: In 1985 the song became her first UK No. 1 single.

text: Which was the first AC/DC album to reach No. 1 on the US album chart?
fact: It came out in November 1981. Back in Black had peaked at No. 4 there.

text: Midnight Oil's The Dead Heart was written for the 1985 handback of which place to its traditional owners?
fact: The single came out in 1986, and the band toured remote communities with the Warumpi Band.

text: Jimmy Barnes's Working Class Man was written by Jonathan Cain, keyboard player of which US band?
fact: It played over the credits of the Ron Howard film Gung Ho.

text: Which Sydney band was called Flowers until 1981, then took the name of its own debut album?
fact: Singer Iva Davies took the name from a cold old flat he had lived in.

text: Which band smashed up the set while closing the TV Week/Countdown awards show in 1981?
fact: They played part of My Turn to Cry, then wrecked the set and walked off.

text: Which overseas star hosted the first ARIA Awards, held in Sydney in March 1987?
fact: John Farnham won six awards on the night.

text: Which novelty single, recorded in Melbourne, kept Ultravox's Vienna off No. 1 in the UK in 1981?
fact: Joe Dolce's song was UK No. 1 for three weeks from February 1981.

text: Which was the first video played on MTV Europe when it launched in August 1987?
fact: The Dire Straits song has Sting on guest vocals, and he shares the writing credit.

text: Tina Turner's 1989 hit The Best was first recorded a year earlier by which singer?
fact: Tyler's version is on her 1988 album Hide Your Heart.

text: Which song was the first a cappella single to top the US Hot 100?
fact: Bobby McFerrin's song held No. 1 for two weeks from 24 September 1988.

text: Which film director made the 18-minute video for Michael Jackson's Bad?
fact: It was shot in Brooklyn and features a young Wesley Snipes.

text: Def Jam Recordings, founded in 1984, was first run from a dorm room at which university?
fact: Rick Rubin ran it from his room in Weinstein Hall, and Russell Simmons soon joined him.

text: Which Depeche Mode founder quit in 1981 and went on to form Yazoo and Erasure?
fact: He formed Yazoo with Alison Moyet and Erasure with Andy Bell.

text: Which New Order single is often called the best-selling 12-inch single of all time?
fact: It came out on Factory Records in March 1983.

text: In what year was Band Aid's Do They Know It's Christmas? first released?
fact: Bob Geldof and Midge Ure wrote it. It was UK No. 1 for five weeks.

text: In what year did U2 release the album The Joshua Tree?
fact: It won the Grammy for Album of the Year at the 1988 ceremony.

text: In what year did MTV begin broadcasting in the United States?
fact: It went to air at 12:01 am on 1 August.

text: In what year did Prince release the album 1999?
fact: It was his fifth studio album, released that October.

text: How many members did INXS have throughout the 1980s?
fact: Three were brothers: Andrew, Jon and Tim Farriss.

text: In what year did Wham! play their farewell concert, The Final, at Wembley Stadium?
fact: About 72,000 people were there on 28 June.

text: Whitney Houston set a record with how many US No. 1 singles in a row, from 1985 to 1988?
fact: The run ended with Where Do Broken Hearts Go in April 1988.

text: How many Grammys did Michael Jackson win on a single night in February 1984?
fact: Seven were for Thriller and its songs. The eighth was for an E.T. storybook album.

text: For how many weeks in a row was Olivia Newton-John's Physical No. 1 on the US Hot 100, from November 1981?
fact: It held the top spot from 21 November 1981 to 23 January 1982.

fact: Noel Gallagher wrote it for the album (What's the Story) Morning Glory?

text: Which singer's debut single was ...Baby One More Time?
fact: It went to US radio in September 1998, when Spears was 16.

text: Smells Like Teen Spirit was the first single from which Nirvana album?
fact: It is also the album's opening track.

text: Which Celine Dion song was the theme of the 1997 film Titanic?
I Want It That Way was a 1999 hit for which boy band?
fact: It was the first single from their album Millennium.

text: Which Australian act had hits with Truly Madly Deeply and To the Moon and Back?
fact: Darren Hayes sang, and Daniel Jones played guitar and keyboards.

text: Which group had a worldwide hit in 1997 with Barbie Girl?
fact: Aqua are a Danish-Norwegian group.

text: Robbie Williams left which boy band in July 1995?
fact: The rest of the band announced their split in February 1996.

text: Ironic and You Oughta Know were hits for which Canadian singer?
fact: You Oughta Know was the first single from Jagged Little Pill.

text: Who is the lead singer of Pearl Jam?
fact: Pearl Jam formed in Seattle in 1990.

text: Which Britpop band released Common People in 1995?
fact: It was the first single from the album Different Class.

text: Which Spice Girl left the group in May 1998?
fact: Geri Halliwell announced her departure through her solicitor on 31 May 1998.

text: Kylie Minogue's 1995 duet Where the Wild Roses Grow was recorded with which singer?
fact: It came out in October 1995, credited to Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds and Kylie Minogue.

text: Powderfinger took their name from a song by which musician?
fact: Young's song Powderfinger is on his 1979 album Rust Never Sleeps.

text: Fake Plastic Trees and High and Dry are on which Radiohead album?
fact: The Bends, the band's second album, came out in March 1995.

text: What is the title of Dr. Dre's first solo album, released in December 1992?
Which record label did Sean "Puffy" Combs found in 1993?
fact: The label's first release was Craig Mack's Flava in Ya Ear, in 1994.

text: Which electronic act had a 1996 hit with Firestarter?
fact: The single was released in March 1996.

text: Underworld's Born Slippy .NUXX became a hit after it was used in which 1996 film?
fact: First a B-side in 1995, it reached No. 2 in the UK after the film.

text: Seal's Kiss from a Rose was re-released in 1995 on the soundtrack of which film?
fact: The song first appeared on Seal's second album in 1994.

text: Which blink-182 album includes All the Small Things and What's My Age Again?
fact: Released in June 1999, it was the band's first album with drummer Travis Barker.
wrong: Take Off Your Pants and Jacket

text: In which Verve video does Richard Ashcroft walk down a street bumping into passers-by?
fact: It was filmed in Hoxton, London, and directed by Walter Stern.

text: The Boy Is Mine was a 1998 duet between Brandy and which other singer?
Who is the lead singer of The Whitlams?
fact: The band formed in Sydney in late 1992.

text: Polyester Girl and Black Bugs are on which Regurgitator album?
fact: Unit came out in 1997, a year after the band's first album, Tu-Plang.

text: Natalie Imbruglia's Torn is the opening track of which debut album?
fact: Her second album, White Lilies Island, followed in 2001.

text: Chains was the first single from which Tina Arena album?
fact: Sorrento Moon (I Remember) and Heaven Help My Heart came from it too.

text: Which Blur video follows a walking milk carton as it searches for a missing band member?
fact: The carton, known as Milky, is looking for guitarist Graham Coxon.

text: Who directed the videos for the Beastie Boys' Sabotage and Weezer's Buddy Holly?
fact: Both videos were made in 1994.

text: The Wu-Tang Clan formed in which New York borough?
fact: The group formed in 1992 with nine original members.

text: Producer Butch Vig is the drummer of which band, formed in 1993?
fact: Garbage formed in Madison, Wisconsin, and are fronted by Scottish singer Shirley Manson.

text: Which Backstreet Boy is a first cousin of bandmate Brian Littrell?
Self Esteem and Come Out and Play are on which album by The Offspring?
fact: Smash came out in April 1994 on the independent label Epitaph.

text: Lisa Loeb's Stay (I Missed You) came from the soundtrack of which film?
fact: The 1994 single was credited to Lisa Loeb and Nine Stories.

text: Rhythm Is a Dancer was a 1992 hit for which German dance act?
fact: The single was released in March 1992.

text: Blackstreet's 1996 hit No Diggity features Dr. Dre and which other rapper?
fact: It knocked Macarena off No. 1 in the US in November 1996.

text: In what year was Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You first released?
How many brothers make up the band Hanson?
fact: Isaac, Taylor and Zac Hanson come from Tulsa, Oklahoma.

text: In what year did Alanis Morissette release the album Jagged Little Pill?
fact: It came out in June 1995 and won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 1996.

text: For what year was Triple J's Hottest 100 first a countdown of only that year's songs?
fact: The earlier polls were all-time lists. The Hottest 100 of 1993 was counted down in January 1994.

text: In what year did Radiohead first release their debut single, Creep?
fact: A reissue in 1993 took it to No. 7 in the UK.

text: In what year did Savage Garden release their self-titled debut album?
fact: Its first single, I Want You, had come out in May 1996.

text: For how many weeks in a row was One Sweet Day, by Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men, No. 1 in the US?
fact: Its run on the Hot 100 began in December 1995 and stood as the record for 23 years.

text: How many Grammys did Lauryn Hill win at the 1999 ceremony?
fact: She had 10 nominations that night, then a record for a woman.

text: How old was Daniel Johns when Silverchair's debut album Frogstomp came out in Australia?
fact: Johns was born on 22 April 1979; Frogstomp was released on 27 March 1995.

text: Put these 90s Triple J Hottest 100 winners in order of countdown year, earliest first.
Put these British albums in order of release, earliest first.
What do you call a triangle with all three sides the same length?
Pi Day is celebrated on which date each year?
fact: Written the American way, 3/14, the date matches the start of pi: 3.14.

text: What is 7.30 pm on a 24-hour clock?
What do you call a whole number greater than 1 that divides evenly only by 1 and itself?
fact: 2 is the only even one.

text: A jacket marked $80 is reduced by 25%. What is the sale price?
On a standard six-sided die, what do the numbers on opposite faces always add up to?
fact: So 1 sits opposite 6, 2 opposite 5 and 3 opposite 4.

text: The rule "a squared plus b squared equals c squared" is named after which ancient Greek?
fact: A triangle with sides of 3, 4 and 5 fits the rule: 9 + 16 = 25.

text: How many hearts are there in a standard 52-card deck?
fact: Each of the four suits has an ace, two to ten, a jack, a queen and a king.

text: Which of these fractions is the biggest?
fact: As decimals they are 0.75, about 0.67, 0.625 and 0.7.

text: Which of these is a prime number?
fact: 91 is 7 x 13, 87 is 3 x 29 and 93 is 3 x 31.

text: The mathematician Fibonacci is also known as Leonardo of which Italian city?
fact: His book Liber Abaci helped bring the digits 0 to 9 into everyday use in Europe.

text: 3 doors, 1 car. You pick one. The host knows where it is and always opens another to show a goat. Chance if you switch?
fact: The Monty Hall problem: your first pick is right 1 time in 3, and switching wins the rest.

text: In 1736 Euler proved that no walk could cross each of which city's seven bridges exactly once?
fact: His proof is seen as the start of graph theory. The city is now Kaliningrad, in Russia.

text: Which Greek mathematician wrote the Elements, the standard geometry textbook for some 2,000 years?
fact: It runs to 13 books and was written around 300 BC.

text: Ada Lovelace, often called the first computer programmer, was the daughter of which poet?
fact: She was his only legitimate child, born in 1815.

text: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing, asks whether a machine can do what?
fact: Turing called it the imitation game.
answer: Pass for a human in conversation

text: How many sides does an Australian 50 cent coin have?
fact: The first 50 cent coin, in 1966, was round and 80% silver. The 12-sided one came in 1969.

text: You roll two fair six-sided dice. What is the chance that they add up to 7?
fact: Six of the 36 possible rolls make 7, more than for any other total.

text: In two-up, two fair coins are tossed. What is the chance of "odds", one head and one tail?
fact: Head-tail and tail-head both count, so it is twice as likely as two heads.

text: English took the word "algebra" from which language?
fact: It comes from al-jabr, which first meant the setting of broken bones.

text: Which of these years was not a leap year?
fact: A century year is a leap year only if it divides by 400, as 2000 does.

text: What is the binary number 1011 in ordinary decimal numbers?
fact: From the left, its places are worth 8, 4, 2 and 1: 8 + 2 + 1 = 11.

text: Which Adelaide-born mathematician won the Fields Medal in 2006?
fact: Fields Medals go only to mathematicians under 40. He won at the 2006 congress in Madrid.

text: How many faces does an icosahedron have?
fact: On the regular kind every face is a triangle, like the 20-sided die of Dungeons & Dragons.

text: 6 is the smallest perfect number, the sum of its smaller divisors (1 + 2 + 3). What is the next one?
fact: 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28. The one after that is 496.

text: Ten people at a party each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes is that?
fact: Each of the 10 shakes 9 hands, but that counts every handshake twice: 90 / 2 = 45.

text: A leg of darts must finish on a double. What is the biggest finish possible with three darts?
fact: Treble 20, treble 20, then the bullseye, which counts as a double. It is called the Big Fish.

text: Emmy Noether's famous theorem says each conservation law in physics goes with a matching what?
fact: Energy is conserved because the laws of physics are the same from one moment to the next.

text: The word "calculus" comes from a Latin word meaning what?
fact: Romans did their sums by moving pebbles on a counting board.

text: Which German mathematician is known as the Prince of Mathematicians?
fact: A medal struck in his honour in 1856 was inscribed Mathematicorum Principi.

text: Grigori Perelman turned down a US$1 million prize in 2010 for proving which conjecture?
fact: He had already declined the Fields Medal.

text: 100 factorial is 1 x 2 x 3 and so on, all the way up to 100. How many zeros does it end in?
fact: Each zero needs a factor of 5: 20 multiples of 5, plus an extra from 25, 50, 75 and 100.

text: What do the six interior angles of a regular hexagon add up to, in degrees?
fact: Each of the six angles is 120 degrees.

text: Odds of 4 to 1 against mean what chance of the event happening?
fact: Four chances of losing to one of winning: one in five.

text: Which symbol did the Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde invent, in a book of 1557?
fact: He chose two parallel lines because, he wrote, no two things can be more equal.

text: Primes that are one less than a power of 2, such as 7 and 31, are named after which French friar?
fact: His own list of them came out in 1644. 7 is 8 - 1 and 31 is 32 - 1.

text: In the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, what number comes next?
fact: Each number is the sum of the two before it.

text: How many degrees do the three angles of a triangle add up to?
How many items are there in a gross?
fact: A gross is a dozen dozens. A great gross is a dozen of those: 1,728.

text: A googol is written as a 1 followed by how many zeros?
fact: The name was made up in 1920 by nine-year-old Milton Sirotta, a mathematician's nephew.

text: What is 2 to the power of 10?
fact: It is why a kilobyte was traditionally counted as 1,024 bytes.

text: What is the smallest whole number above zero that divides evenly by every number from 1 to 10?
fact: It is 5 x 7 x 8 x 9. Between them those four cover every number from 1 to 10.

text: With 365 equally likely birthdays, what is the smallest group in which a shared birthday is more likely than not?
fact: This is the birthday problem. With 23 people the chance is about 50.7%.

text: What do the numbers on a roulette wheel, 1 to 36, add up to?
fact: Eighteen pairs that each make 37: 1 + 36, 2 + 35 and so on. The zero adds nothing.

text: Counting squares of every size, from 1 by 1 up to 8 by 8, how many squares are there on a chessboard?
Put these shapes in order of how many sides they have, fewest first.
