What is the currency of Japan?
fact: The yen was adopted as Japan's modern currency in 1871.

text: Which bush poet, author of The Man from Snowy River, is on the Australian $10 note?
fact: The poet and campaigner Dame Mary Gilmore is on the other side.

text: On the share market, what is a long stretch of falling prices called?
fact: The usual yardstick is a fall of 20 per cent or more from a recent peak.

text: John D. Rockefeller built his vast fortune in which industry?
fact: With a few partners he set up Standard Oil in 1870.

text: Which currency did Italy use before it switched to the euro?
fact: The changeover rate was fixed at 1,936.27 lire to one euro.

text: Bitcoin's founding paper was published in 2008 under which name?
fact: The network's first block was mined on 3 January 2009.

text: On the classic London Monopoly board, which property costs the most?
fact: It costs £400. Old Kent Road and Whitechapel Road are the cheapest, at £60 each.

text: Which Australian actor played Naomi, Jordan Belfort's wife, in The Wolf of Wall Street?
fact: Martin Scorsese directed, with Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort.

text: What do economists call a general rise in prices across the economy?
fact: Deflation is the opposite: prices falling over time.

text: In June 1963 the government announced that Australia's new decimal currency would be called what?
fact: The name was so unpopular that by September it had been changed to the dollar.

text: The Royal Australian Mint, which makes Australia's circulating coins, is in which city?
fact: Prince Philip opened it in 1965, a year before decimal currency arrived.

text: In Australia, a 'franked' dividend comes with a credit for what?
fact: Shareholders can use franking credits to cut their own tax bill.

text: Which trading company's 1602 share sale is seen as the start of the world's first stock exchange?
fact: Its shares were traded in Amsterdam. In Dutch the company is known as the VOC.

text: CSL, which floated on the share market in 1994, began in 1916 as the Commonwealth what?
fact: The federal government set it up during the First World War, when imported vaccines ran short.

text: Which Wall Street bank filed in September 2008 for what was then the biggest bankruptcy in US history?
fact: It listed assets of about US$639 billion when it filed.

text: Top shares get their nickname from the most valuable chip in a traditional poker set. What colour was it?
fact: Hence 'blue chip': a big, established company whose shares are seen as dependable.

text: In the Wall Street Crash, 29 October went down in history as Black what?
fact: About 16 million shares were traded. Black Thursday, five days earlier, had begun the panic.

text: In 1971, which US president ended the dollar's convertibility into gold?
fact: He announced it on television on Sunday 15 August, while the markets were closed.

text: Which was the first multipurpose charge card, launched in New York in 1950?
fact: Co-founder Frank McNamara is said to have had the idea after forgetting his wallet at dinner.

text: In 2010, programmer Laszlo Hanyecz famously paid 10,000 bitcoins for what?
fact: Fans of the currency mark 22 May each year as Bitcoin Pizza Day.

text: Which big four bank began in 1817 as the Bank of New South Wales, Australia's first bank?
fact: It took the name Westpac in 1982, after merging with the Commercial Bank of Australia.

text: Which economist published The Wealth of Nations in 1776?
fact: The book contains his famous image of the market's 'invisible hand'.

text: The pound sign, £, is a stylised form of which letter?
fact: It stands for libra, the Roman pound.

text: 'Dollar' comes from 'thaler', short for Joachimsthaler. Joachimsthal is in which present-day country?
fact: The silver-mining town, now called Jáchymov, began striking the coins around 1520.

text: The first metal coins are generally credited to which ancient kingdom, in what is now Turkey?
fact: They date from around the 7th century BC and were struck from electrum, a gold and silver alloy.

text: In 1661, a bank in which country issued Europe's first banknotes?
fact: Stockholms Banco issued too many and soon failed. The Riksbank replaced it in 1668.

text: In 1901, Andrew Carnegie sold his steel company to a group led by which banker?
fact: Morgan folded it into U.S. Steel, often called the world's first billion-dollar company.

text: What did Berkshire Hathaway make before Warren Buffett turned it into an investment giant?
fact: Buffett took control of the struggling New England mill company in 1965.

text: On Black Wednesday in 1992, the pound was forced out of what?
fact: George Soros bet heavily against the pound and was dubbed 'the man who broke the Bank of England'.

text: Trader Nick Leeson's hidden losses in Singapore brought down which British bank in 1995?
fact: The Dutch group ING bought what was left of the bank for £1.

text: What do economists call a luxury good that people want more of as its price rises?
fact: It is named after Thorstein Veblen, who coined the phrase 'conspicuous consumption'.

text: 'Bad money drives out good' is a summary of whose law?
fact: Sir Thomas Gresham was a financial agent of Elizabeth I and founded London's Royal Exchange.

text: Which economist, nicknamed 'Nugget', was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia?
fact: The Reserve Bank came into being on 14 January 1960, when the Reserve Bank Act took effect.

text: The 'CH' in CHF, the code for the Swiss franc, comes from Switzerland's name in which language?
fact: Confoederatio Helvetica is the Latin name of the Swiss Confederation.

text: Which South American country scrapped its currency, the sucre, for the US dollar in 2000?
fact: The sucre had lost about two-thirds of its value during 1999.

text: In the comedy Trading Places, the Duke brothers try to corner the market in what?
fact: Eddie Murphy and Dan Aykroyd ruin them with a forged crop report.

text: In classic Monopoly, how much money does a player collect for passing Go?
fact: The rules call it a salary: $200 on American boards and £200 on the London one.

text: When Australia's GST began in 2000, what was its rate?
fact: It replaced the wholesale sales tax on 1 July 2000.

text: Since 1928, how many companies have made up the Dow Jones Industrial Average?
fact: It began in 1896 with 12 stocks.

text: In what year did euro notes and coins first go into circulation?
fact: Twelve countries switched on 1 January. The euro had existed for electronic payments since 1999.

text: In 1914, Henry Ford made headlines by lifting factory pay to how many dollars a day?
fact: It roughly doubled the old rate, and the working day was cut from nine hours to eight.

text: In what year did compulsory employer super, the Superannuation Guarantee, begin in Australia?
fact: It started on 1 July at 3 per cent of pay, or 4 per cent at bigger employers.

text: In what year was the Australian dollar floated?
fact: Treasurer Paul Keating announced the decision, and the float took effect on 12 December.

text: The New York Stock Exchange traces its origins to the Buttonwood Agreement, signed in what year?
fact: Twenty-four brokers signed it on 17 May, by legend under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street.

text: In what year was the Bank of England founded?
fact: It was founded on 27 July, mainly to pay for the war against France.

text: Put these booms and busts in order, earliest first.
Put these Australian coins in order of diameter, smallest first.

Put these Australian companies in order of founding, oldest first.
Put these companies in order of their stock market float, earliest first.
The trophy for winning the Bathurst 1000, first awarded in 2006, is named after which driver?
fact: Craig Lowndes and Jamie Whincup were the first to lift it.

text: Dick Johnson crashed out of the lead of the 1980 Bathurst 1000 after hitting what?
fact: TV viewers donated towards a new Falcon, and Ford matched them dollar for dollar.

text: Dick Johnson and his team are famous for which race number?
fact: His son Steven later raced under the famous number too.

text: Shane van Gisbergen, the Supercars champion who switched to NASCAR, is from which country?
fact: He was born in Auckland and is widely known by his initials, SVG.

text: When Holden bowed out of Supercars, which car took the Commodore's place on the grid?
fact: The Camaro arrived with the Gen3 rules, alongside a new Ford Mustang.

text: In what year did Holden race in the Supercars championship for the last time?
fact: Holden went out on top, winning that year's Bathurst 1000 and the championship.

text: The Chase was added in 1987 to break up which straight at Mount Panorama?
fact: Supercars get close to 300 km/h on the run down to The Chase.

text: Which Italian MotoGP great is nicknamed The Doctor?
fact: His race number, 46, was retired from MotoGP in 2022.

text: Phillip Island, long the home of the Australian Motorcycle Grand Prix, is in which state?
Speedway bikes race around dirt ovals with a single gear and without which of these?
fact: A heat is four riders over four laps, always anticlockwise.

text: What does the winner of the Indianapolis 500 traditionally drink in victory lane?
fact: It dates to 1936, when Louis Meyer drank buttermilk after his third win.

text: Put these drivers in order of their first win in Bathurst's Great Race, earliest first.
Peter Brock's famous race number, 05, was a nod to what?
fact: He carried it in support of a state campaign against drink-driving.

text: Shane van Gisbergen won on his NASCAR Cup debut in 2023 on the streets of which city?
fact: He was the first driver to win on Cup debut since Johnny Rutherford in 1963.

text: The Gold Coast's street race at Surfers Paradise began in 1991 as a round of which kind of racing?
fact: The American open-wheelers last raced there in 2008.

text: Ford legend Allan Moffat, a four-time winner of Bathurst's Great Race, was born in which country?
fact: He was born in Saskatoon and came to Australia as a teenager.

text: Who won the 2014 Bathurst 1000 after starting last and leading only the final lap?
fact: Jamie Whincup ran short of fuel on the last lap. Paul Morris shared the winning Falcon.

text: How many Supercars championships did Jamie Whincup win?
fact: He won them between 2008 and 2017, all with Triple Eight.

text: Marc Márquez ended a six-year title drought in 2025 riding for which make?
fact: All six of his earlier MotoGP titles came with Honda.

text: Who became Australia's first 500cc motorcycle world champion, in 1987?
fact: The Wollongong Whiz also won the first world championship Australian motorcycle GP, in 1989.

text: Which rider from Kurri Kurri won America's premier supercross title in 2004 and 2008?
fact: He was named the AMA's Athlete of the Year in 2009.

text: In the name of the Isle of Man TT, what does TT stand for?
fact: It is run as a time trial all the same: riders set off one by one, 10 seconds apart.

text: Sébastien Loeb won nine world rally titles in a row from 2004 with which make?
fact: Before rallying he was a gymnast, and a four-time champion of Alsace.

text: Colin McRae won the 1995 world rally title driving which car?
fact: At 27 he was the youngest world rally champion, a record that stood until 2022.

text: In Days of Thunder, what is the name of Tom Cruise's NASCAR driver?
fact: Nicole Kidman plays his doctor, Claire Lewicki.

text: In Ford v Ferrari, who plays the British racing driver Ken Miles?
fact: The film builds to the 1966 Le Mans 24 Hours. Some countries know it as Le Mans '66.

text: Top Fuel dragsters run mainly on which fuel?
fact: The rules allow up to 90 per cent nitromethane. Most of the rest is methanol.

text: How many 500cc world titles in a row did Mick Doohan win in the 1990s?
fact: He won every year from 1994 to 1998, all on Hondas.

text: The Indianapolis 500 is run over how many laps of the oval?
fact: Each lap is 2.5 miles, which makes the 500.

text: In what year did Toby Price become the first Australian to win the Dakar Rally?
fact: He won the bike class on a KTM, and did it again in 2019.

text: Put these famous races in order of when they were first held, earliest first.
Put these circuits in order of lap length, longest first.
The cars that finished first and second on the road at Bathurst in 1987 were later disqualified. What were they?
fact: The Swiss-run Texaco cars had illegally modified front wheel arches.

text: Which team won the 2017 Bathurst 1000 with David Reynolds and Luke Youlden?
Marcos Ambrose took both of his NASCAR Cup wins, in 2011 and 2012, at which road course?
fact: The Tasmanian was driving for Richard Petty Motorsports.

text: Which Le Mans legend shared Allan Moffat's winning Falcon in Ford's 1-2 at Bathurst in 1977?
fact: Colin Bond and Alan Hamilton drove the second Falcon in the famous formation finish.

text: Jack Miller took his first MotoGP win in the wet in 2016 at which circuit?
fact: He won a rain-interrupted Dutch TT on a Marc VDS Honda.

text: Superbike champion Troy Bayliss won a one-off MotoGP ride in 2006 at which circuit?
fact: A stand-in for the season finale, he qualified second and led all the way.

text: In 2024, who broke the long-standing record of 26 Isle of Man TT wins?
fact: The old record had belonged to his uncle, Joey Dunlop.

text: Which Australian won speedway's world title in 2004, 2006 and 2009?
fact: Born in Bristol, England, he is the son of Australian speedway champion Phil Crump.

text: Which Dane won the Le Mans 24 Hours nine times between 1997 and 2013?
fact: Six of the wins came in a row, from 2000 to 2005, earning him the name Mr Le Mans.

text: IndyCar great Scott Dixon races as a New Zealander but was born in which Australian city?
fact: He grew up in Auckland, and won the Indianapolis 500 in 2008.

text: Rally Australia joined the World Rally Championship in 1989. Until 2006 it was based in which city?
fact: It later moved to the New South Wales coast, last running as a WRC round in 2018.

text: In circuit racing, what does a black flag with an orange disc tell a driver?
answer: Pit now: your car has a problem

text: The 2023 film Gran Turismo is based on the story of which gamer turned racing driver?
fact: He won Nissan's GT Academy in 2011, and was his own character's stunt double in the film.

text: In what year was the race now known as the Bathurst 1000 first held at Mount Panorama?
fact: It began in 1960 as the Armstrong 500 at Phillip Island.

text: How many years in a row did Casey Stoner win his home MotoGP race at Phillip Island?
fact: He won every year from 2007 to 2012, then retired at the end of that season.

text: Jett Lawrence won every moto of the 2023 US 450 motocross season. How many motos was that?
fact: Before him, the last rider to go through a season unbeaten was James Stewart, in 2008.

text: Put these riders in order of their first 500cc world title, earliest first.
Each of these drivers won the V8 Supercars title exactly once. Put them in order, earliest first.
Who played Vito Corleone in The Godfather (1972)?
fact: The Godfather won three Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Brando.

text: Who played Holly Golightly in Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961)?
fact: The film's song Moon River won the Oscar for Best Song.

text: The boxer Rocky Balboa comes from which American city?
fact: The steps he runs up belong to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

text: In The Matrix (1999), which pill does Neo take?
fact: Most of the film was shot in Sydney, at Fox Studios and around the city.

text: Which 2008 film launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
fact: Iron Man had its premiere in Sydney on 14 April 2008.

text: In Jurassic Park (1993), where did the scientists find dinosaur DNA?
fact: Frog DNA was used to fill the gaps in the dinosaur genomes.

text: Which Stanley Kubrick film features the computer HAL 9000?
fact: HAL was voiced by Douglas Rain, chosen after Kubrick rejected Martin Balsam.

text: In King Kong (1933), which New York building does Kong climb?
What is Indiana Jones famously afraid of?
fact: In Raiders of the Lost Ark he faces thousands of them in the Well of Souls.

text: What did the crew of Jaws nickname the mechanical shark?
fact: It was named after Steven Spielberg's lawyer, Bruce Ramer.

text: In Casablanca, what is the name of Rick's nightclub?
In Citizen Kane, what does 'Rosebud' turn out to be?
fact: The sled is burned with Kane's junk, and no one in the story learns the truth.

text: As of 2026, who is the only man to win three Best Actor Oscars?
fact: He won for My Left Foot, There Will Be Blood and Lincoln.

text: Which film took the most money at the worldwide box office in 2023?
fact: Barbie made about US$1.45 billion, ahead of Mario's US$1.36 billion.

text: In January 2010, which film passed Titanic as the highest-grossing film ever?
fact: James Cameron directed both films.

text: Actor Heath Ledger was born in which Australian city?
fact: He won a posthumous Oscar for playing the Joker in The Dark Knight.

text: The 2000 comedy The Dish is set in which NSW town?
fact: The town's radio telescope relayed TV of the 1969 Moon landing.

text: Hattie McDaniel became the first Black actor to win an Oscar for which film?
fact: She won Best Supporting Actress for playing Mammy, at the 1940 ceremony.

text: In Some Like It Hot, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon go into hiding disguised as what?
fact: The band is called Sweet Sue and Her Society Syncopators.

text: At the 2017 Oscars, La La Land was wrongly announced as Best Picture. Which film had won?
fact: Warren Beatty had been handed the envelope for Best Actress.

text: Which Bond henchman kills with a steel-rimmed bowler hat?
fact: He appears in Goldfinger (1964), played by Harold Sakata.

text: Who was the first woman to win the Oscar for Best Director?
fact: She won at the 2010 ceremony for The Hurt Locker.

text: The climax of Hitchcock's North by Northwest takes place on which landmark?
fact: Cary Grant plays Roger Thornhill; James Mason plays the villain, Vandamm.

text: Who played Dumbledore in the first two Harry Potter films?
fact: Harris died in 2002; Gambon took over from Prisoner of Azkaban.

text: Who directed Lawrence of Arabia (1962)?
fact: It won seven Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Director.

text: In Muriel's Wedding, what is the name of Muriel's home town?
fact: Tweed Heads stood in for the town; the scene where they leave was shot in Coolangatta.

text: Which of Disney's Seven Dwarfs is the only one without a beard?
fact: He is also the only dwarf who never speaks.

text: As of 2026, who has hosted the Academy Awards more times than anyone else?
fact: Billy Crystal is next, with nine.

text: Which was the first film to win Oscars for picture, director, actor, actress and screenplay?
fact: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and The Silence of the Lambs later matched it.

text: Who wrote and directed the Australian horror film The Babadook (2014)?
fact: It was shot mostly in Adelaide, where the story is set.

text: In Alien (1979), what is the name of the Nostromo's cat?
fact: Ripley takes Jones with her in the shuttle before the Nostromo explodes.

text: Which actor was cast as Indiana Jones but had to pull out because of a TV contract?
fact: The show that kept him was Magnum, P.I.

text: Who won Best Actress at the 2025 Oscars for Anora?
fact: She beat Demi Moore, who had won the Golden Globe and the SAG Award.

text: Which film set a record with 16 nominations at the 2026 Oscars?
fact: The old record of 14 was shared by All About Eve, Titanic and La La Land.

text: Which Hollywood star was born Marion Morrison?
fact: He was born in Winterset, Iowa, in 1907.

text: The 1960 Western The Magnificent Seven is a remake of which Akira Kurosawa film?
fact: Seven Samurai was released in Japan in 1954.

text: How many films are in the main Harry Potter film series?
fact: They were released from 2001 to 2011.

text: In what year was Home Alone, starring Macaulay Culkin, released?
fact: It was the highest-grossing live-action comedy until The Hangover Part II in 2011.

text: In what year was The Wizard of Oz, starring Judy Garland, released?
fact: Buddy Ebsen was the first Tin Man but fell ill from the aluminium dust in his make-up.

text: How many Oscars did Oppenheimer win at the 2024 ceremony?
fact: It had 13 nominations.

text: How many James Bond films did Roger Moore star in?
fact: His last was A View to a Kill.

text: As of the 2026 ceremony, how many acting Oscar nominations has Meryl Streep received?
fact: She has won three, for Kramer vs. Kramer, Sophie's Choice and The Iron Lady.

text: How old was Tatum O'Neal when she won her Oscar for Paper Moon?
fact: She is still the youngest person to win a competitive Oscar.

text: How many Oscars did the Lord of the Rings film trilogy win in total?
fact: From 30 nominations across the three films.

text: How old was Jessica Tandy when she won Best Actress for Driving Miss Daisy?
fact: At 80 she became the oldest winner of the Best Actress Oscar.

text: Which Beatle took over on bass guitar after Stuart Sutcliffe left in 1961?
Which NSW city hosts Australia's best-known country music festival each January?
fact: The festival's Golden Guitar awards were first handed out in January 1973.

text: Which ABC music show ran from 1974 to 1987, with Molly Meldrum as its talent coordinator?
The 1969 Woodstock festival was held on a dairy farm in which US state?
fact: It was held on Max Yasgur's farm near the town of Bethel.

text: Which Spice Girl was known as Posh Spice?
fact: She was still Victoria Adams when the group took off.

text: Dave Grohl was the drummer in which band before he formed Foo Fighters?
The Stratocaster electric guitar is made by which company?
fact: Fender has made the Stratocaster since 1954.

text: Beyoncé first found fame in which group?
fact: The group formed in Houston, Texas, in 1990.

text: Oasis formed in 1991 in which English city?
Bohemian Rhapsody first appeared on which Queen album?
fact: The album came out in November 1975, a few weeks after the single.

text: Which Australian band won the Grammy for Best New Artist in February 1983?
fact: Their album Business as Usual spent 15 weeks at No. 1 in the US.

text: Perth's Tame Impala is in the studio essentially the work of which musician?
fact: Parker writes, records, plays and produces the studio albums himself.

text: Who was the lead singer of The Seekers?
fact: I'll Never Find Another You reached No. 1 in the UK in February 1965.

text: Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb of the Bee Gees were born where, before moving to Queensland?
fact: The family settled in Redcliffe, north-east of Brisbane, in 1958.

text: Hip hop group Hilltop Hoods come from which city?
fact: The Hard Road (2006) was the first Australian hip hop album to top the ARIA chart.

text: Which act topped Triple J's Hottest 100 of 2021 with a cover of Tame Impala's Elephant?
fact: It was recorded for Triple J's Like a Version segment.

text: Who wrote I Will Always Love You, a huge 1992 hit for Whitney Houston?
fact: Parton recorded it first, in 1973.

text: Which Adele album won Album of the Year at the Grammys in February 2012?
fact: Her debut album, 19, was named after her age when she wrote it.

text: Which Australian sang with Justin Bieber on Stay, a US No. 1 in 2021?
fact: Stay also spent 17 weeks at No. 1 on the ARIA singles chart.

text: Which singer's 1998 hit Believe made Auto-Tune famous as an obvious vocal effect?
fact: The warbling sound became known as the 'Cher effect'.

text: In 2019, which song set a record of 19 straight weeks at No. 1 on the US Hot 100?
fact: Choosin' Texas passed its total in 2026, but its weeks at No. 1 were not in a row.

text: In 2018, which rapper became the first artist outside classical and jazz to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music?
fact: He won it for his 2017 album Damn.

text: Silverchair formed in 1992, as Innocent Criminals, in which NSW city?
Which song topped Triple J's first Hottest 100, an all-time poll held in 1989?
fact: The Joy Division song won the 1990 poll as well.

text: Which musician was named Australian of the Year for 1992?
fact: He fronted Yothu Yindi, whose hit Treaty came out in 1991.

text: Before The Wiggles, Anthony Field and Jeff Fatt played in which Sydney band?
Which Powderfinger album won the ARIA for Album of the Year in 1999?
fact: It also won Best Rock Album and Best Cover Art that night.

text: In August 1995, Blur's Country House beat which Oasis single to No. 1 in the UK?
fact: Country House sold about 274,000 copies that week to 216,000.

text: In January 1992, Nirvana's Nevermind knocked which album off No. 1 in the US?
fact: Dangerous was Michael Jackson's first album after Bad.

text: Ronnie Wood joined the Rolling Stones in 1975 as the replacement for which guitarist?
The Beatles' last public performance, in January 1969, was on a rooftop in which London street?
fact: The roof belonged to their company Apple Corps, at 3 Savile Row.

text: Glastonbury Festival is held on which farm in Somerset?
fact: Michael Eavis held the first festival there. Tickets cost £1.

text: The Saints, whose 1976 single (I'm) Stranded was an early punk landmark, formed in which city?
The Big Day Out festival began in January 1992 as a one-city show in which city?
fact: Nirvana played the first one, at the Hordern Pavilion.

text: Which company made the TR-808 drum machine, first sold in 1980?
Which two Easybeats wrote their 1966 hit Friday on My Mind?
fact: Wright and Young had written most of the band's earlier hits.

text: How many members are in the K-pop group BTS?
In what year did Elvis Presley die?
fact: He died at Graceland, his home in Memphis, aged 42.

text: In what year was Bob Dylan awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature?
In what year did Kurt Cobain die?
In what year were the Live Aid concerts held in London and Philadelphia?
fact: Wembley Stadium and JFK Stadium hosted the shows on 13 July.

text: In what year did the Spice Girls release their debut single, Wannabe?
For how many weeks in total did Tones and I's Dance Monkey top the ARIA singles chart?
fact: It broke the record of 15 weeks set by Ed Sheeran's Shape of You.

text: For how many straight weeks was Bryan Adams's (Everything I Do) I Do It for You No. 1 in the UK in 1991?
fact: It was the theme from Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves.

text: How many No. 1 singles did the Beatles have on the US Billboard Hot 100?
fact: The first was I Want to Hold Your Hand, in 1964.

Ariana Grande plays which character in the Wicked films?
fact: Cynthia Erivo plays Elphaba. Wicked came out in 2024 and Wicked: For Good in 2025.

text: In Grease, which high school do Danny and Sandy go to?
fact: The stage show's writers named the school after the teen idol Bobby Rydell.

text: Mamma Mia! is set on an island in which country?
fact: The island, Kalokairi, is made up. The film was shot mainly on Skopelos.

text: In Hamilton, who shoots Alexander Hamilton in a duel?
fact: The real duel was fought at Weehawken, New Jersey, on 11 July 1804.

text: In The Wizard of Oz, what does the Scarecrow want from the Wizard?
fact: The Tin Man wants a heart and the Cowardly Lion wants courage.

text: Who played Maria in the 1965 film The Sound of Music?
fact: Christopher Plummer played Captain von Trapp.

text: Which Australian plays Fat Amy in the Pitch Perfect films?
fact: Fat Amy sings with the Barden Bellas, an all-female a cappella group.

text: Who plays Mia, the aspiring actress, in La La Land?
fact: Ryan Gosling plays Sebastian, a jazz pianist. Damien Chazelle wrote and directed.

text: Who played Troy Bolton in High School Musical?
fact: Vanessa Hudgens played Gabriella Montez.

text: Which musical with songs by Tim Minchin won a then-record seven Olivier Awards in 2012?
fact: Minchin's next show, Groundhog Day, won the 2017 Olivier for Best New Musical.

text: Hugh Jackman won a 2004 Tony for playing which Australian in The Boy from Oz?
fact: Todd McKenney played the part in the original Australian production in 1998.

text: In Les Misérables, which character sings On My Own?
Who wrote the music and lyrics for Wicked?
fact: His earlier shows include Godspell and Pippin.

text: The musical Hairspray is set in 1962 in which American city?
fact: It is based on John Waters's 1988 film and won the 2003 Tony for Best Musical.

text: Come From Away is set in which Canadian town, where 38 planes landed on 11 September 2001?
fact: Gander, in Newfoundland, took in more than 6,500 passengers and crew.

text: The musical Six was first staged in 2017 by Cambridge students at which festival?
fact: Toby Marlow and Lucy Moss wrote it.

text: Singin' in the Rain is set as Hollywood switches to what?
fact: The story begins in 1927. Gene Kelly directed the film with Stanley Donen.

text: Rent is a rock musical retelling of which opera?
fact: Jonathan Larson moved Puccini's story to New York's East Village.

text: & Juliet is built on the pop hits of which Swedish songwriter?
fact: In the show, Shakespeare's wife Anne Hathaway rewrites the ending so that Juliet lives.

text: Who wrote the lyrics for Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita?
fact: Andrew Lloyd Webber wrote the music for both.

text: Before Hamilton, Lin-Manuel Miranda won a Tony for the songs of which musical?
fact: It won four Tonys in 2008, including Best Musical and Best Original Score.

text: Which was the first Broadway musical by the team of Rodgers and Hammerstein?
fact: It opened in 1943. Before that, Rodgers wrote with Lorenz Hart and Hammerstein with Jerome Kern.

text: In Cabaret, the Kit Kat Klub is in which city?
fact: John Kander and Fred Ebb wrote the songs, as they did for Chicago.

text: Which duo wrote the songs for Dear Evan Hansen and The Greatest Showman?
fact: Benj Pasek and Justin Paul also won an Oscar for the lyrics of City of Stars.

text: Wicked lost the 2004 Tony for Best Musical to which show?
fact: Wicked won three Tonys that night, including Best Actress for Idina Menzel.

text: As of 2026, which musical holds the record for Tony wins by one show, with 12?
fact: Mel Brooks's show won all 12 in 2001.

text: The 'Tony' of the Tony Awards is short for which name?
fact: Antoinette Perry was an actress and director who led the American Theatre Wing in wartime.

text: Who was the first to play Eva Perón on stage, in the original London Evita?
fact: Julie Covington sang the part on the 1976 album. Patti LuPone played it on Broadway.

text: In the original stage show of Grease, what was the T-Birds gang called?
fact: The film renamed them the T-Birds, and some later stage revivals followed suit.

text: Stephen Sondheim wrote the lyrics, but not the music, for which of these shows?
fact: Jule Styne wrote the music. Sondheim also wrote only the lyrics for West Side Story.

text: In 2019, the West End home of Les Misérables was renamed after which composer?
fact: It had been the Queen's Theatre. Les Mis has run in London since 1985.

text: Which Melbourne theatre is said to be haunted by Federici, a singer who died there in 1888?
fact: Frederick Federici was playing Mephistopheles in the opera Faust that night.

text: Who played Bernadette when the stage musical Priscilla opened in Sydney, London and on Broadway?
fact: He reached 2,000 performances in the part in 2018 and was nominated for a Tony in 2011.

text: Jimmy Chi, who wrote Bran Nue Dae (1990), called the first Aboriginal musical, came from which WA town?
fact: He wrote it with his band Kuckles, and it opened at the Festival of Perth.

text: Who played the Phantom when The Phantom of the Opera opened in Melbourne in 1990?
fact: Marina Prior played Christine. Warlow returned to the role in 2007.

text: Which Moulin Rouge! star won a Tony as the only nominee in his category?
fact: He won Best Actor in a Musical for playing Christian, at the ceremony held in 2021.

text: How many von Trapp children are there in The Sound of Music?
fact: From oldest to youngest: Liesl, Friedrich, Louisa, Kurt, Brigitta, Marta and Gretl.

text: In what year was the film Grease, with John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John, released?
fact: It was the highest-grossing film of 1978 in the United States.

text: In what year did The Lion King open on Broadway?
fact: Julie Taymor became the first woman to win the Tony for directing a musical.

text: In what year did Mamma Mia! first open on stage, in London?
fact: It opened at the Prince Edward Theatre and reached Broadway in 2001.

text: In what year was the film Cabaret, starring Liza Minnelli, released?
fact: It won eight Oscars, including Best Actress for Minnelli.

text: Hamilton set a record in 2016 with how many Tony nominations?
fact: Its 16 nominations came in 13 categories, as some of its actors were up against each other.

text: How many Oscars did the 1961 film West Side Story win?
fact: It was nominated for 11 and lost only the screenplay award.

text: In what year did The Rocky Horror Show first open on stage, in London?
fact: Richard O'Brien wrote it. The film, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, followed in 1975.

text: In what year did the long-running Broadway revival of Chicago open?
fact: In 2014 it passed Cats to become the second-longest-running show in Broadway history.

Which Roman god is the equal of the Greek sea god Poseidon?
fact: Both are shown holding a trident, a three-pronged fishing spear.

text: In Greek myth, what happens to anyone who looks straight at Medusa?
fact: Perseus beat her by looking only at her reflection in his polished shield.

text: In the best-known version of the Greek myth, where is the one place Achilles can be wounded?
fact: His mother, Thetis, held him by the heel when she dipped him in the River Styx.

text: In Norse myth, which god is the trickster and shape-shifter who keeps causing trouble?
fact: He is the son of a giant but is counted among the gods of Asgard.

text: In Arthurian legend, what is the name of King Arthur's sword?
fact: Durendal was the sword of Roland and Joyeuse the sword of Charlemagne.

text: Which bird of legend burns up and rises again, young, from its own ashes?
fact: Ancient writers said only one phoenix lived at a time, for 500 years or more.

text: The sportswear brand Nike is named after the Greek goddess of what?
fact: Before it took her name, the company was called Blue Ribbon Sports.

text: In Greek myth, which monster, half man and half bull, lives in the Labyrinth on Crete?
fact: The inventor Daedalus built the Labyrinth for King Minos to hold it.

text: In ancient Egyptian belief, Ra was the god of what?
fact: From the 4th dynasty on, Egypt's kings took the title "Son of Ra".

text: In Greek myth, who is the ferryman who rows the dead across to the underworld?
fact: The dead were often buried with a coin to pay his fare.

text: In the Odyssey, how does Penelope hold off the suitors who want to marry her?
fact: She says she must first finish a burial shroud for Odysseus's father, Laertes.
wrong: Hiding in a temple of Athena

text: Which Roman god of doorways and beginnings is shown with two faces?
fact: The month of January is named after him.

text: Which king in Greek myth is punished by standing in water he can never drink?
fact: Fruit hangs just out of his reach too. His name gave English the word "tantalise".

text: Which planet is the only one named after a Greek god instead of a Roman one?
fact: William Herschel, who found it in 1781, wanted to name it after King George III.

text: Which Italian fashion house uses the head of Medusa as its logo?
In Norse myth, the god Baldr can be harmed by only one thing. What is it?
fact: His mother, Frigg, had made everything else in the world swear not to hurt him.

text: In Egyptian myth, which god is killed by his brother Set and becomes ruler of the dead?
fact: His son, Horus, later defeats Set and becomes king of Egypt.

text: In Arthurian legend, which knight's love for Queen Guinevere helps to bring down Camelot?
fact: Chrétien de Troyes made him the queen's lover in a French poem of the late 12th century.

text: In the Ramayana, which ten-headed king of Lanka carries off Sita, the wife of Rama?
fact: Kumbhakarna is his brother and Indrajit is his son.

text: In Japanese folklore, which animal is a kitsune, a spirit that can take human shape?
fact: Kitsune are linked with Inari, the Shinto deity of rice.

text: In Māori tradition, who fished up the North Island of New Zealand?
fact: The island's Māori name, Te Ika-a-Māui, means "the fish of Māui".

text: The kraken, a giant sea monster, comes from the folklore of which country?
fact: Bishop Erik Pontoppidan made it famous in a natural history of Norway in the 1750s.

text: For the Wurundjeri and other Kulin peoples of Victoria, the creator spirit Bunjil is which bird?
fact: Bunjilaka, the cultural centre at Melbourne Museum, means "the place of Bunjil".

text: In Greek myth, which hero rides the winged horse Pegasus to kill the Chimera?
fact: He tamed Pegasus with a bridle given to him by the goddess Athena.

text: In Greek myth, what flows in the veins of the gods in place of blood?
In Greek myth, which of the Muses looks after history?
fact: Calliope has epic poetry, Thalia has comedy and Urania has astronomy.

text: In Greek myth, Zeus carries off the princess Europa while in the form of what?
fact: He comes to Leda as a swan and to Danaë as a shower of gold.

text: In Norse myth, what are the names of Odin's two ravens?
fact: Geri and Freki are his two wolves.

text: In Norse myth, which two humans live through Ragnarök and repopulate the world?
fact: They shelter in a wood called Hoddmímis holt and live on the morning dew.

text: In Egyptian myth, which giant serpent must Ra fight off every night in the underworld?
fact: He is also known as Apep, and stood for chaos and darkness.

text: In Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur, which knight throws the dying Arthur's sword into the lake?
fact: In the older French romances the task falls to a knight called Griflet.

text: In Irish legend, which hero defends Ulster single-handed in the Cattle Raid of Cooley?
fact: He is 17 at the time. A curse has left the other warriors of Ulster unable to fight.

text: In the Mahabharata, who drives Arjuna's chariot at the battle of Kurukshetra?
fact: Their conversation before the battle forms the Bhagavad Gita.

text: In Japanese myth, which storm god, brother of the sun goddess Amaterasu, kills an eight-headed serpent?
fact: The serpent is called Yamata no Orochi.

text: In the best-known Māori telling, which god pushes apart the sky father and the earth mother?
fact: Ranginui and Papatūānuku were locked together. Tāne lay on his back and pushed them apart.

text: In Chinese legend, who swallows an elixir of immortality and rises to live on the Moon?
fact: Her story is told at the Mid-Autumn Festival. Her husband is the archer Hou Yi.

text: In Greek myth, how many heads does Cerberus, the guard dog of the underworld, usually have?
fact: The poet Hesiod gave him fifty.

text: How many animals are there in the Chinese zodiac?
fact: The cycle starts with the Rat and ends with the Pig.

text: In Greek myth, how many Muses are there in the usual telling?
fact: They are the daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne, the goddess of memory.

text: In Norse myth, how many legs does Odin's horse Sleipnir have?
In Greek legend, for how many years did the Greeks besiege Troy?
fact: Odysseus then took another ten years to get home.

text: In what year was Bram Stoker's novel Dracula first published?
fact: It came out in London in May, bound in yellow cloth.

text: In Homer's Odyssey, how many years does Odysseus spend on the island of the nymph Calypso?
fact: Her island is called Ogygia.

text: In the Ramayana, for how many years is Prince Rama exiled to the forest?
fact: The exile is demanded by his stepmother, Kaikeyi.

text: In what year did William Caxton first print Thomas Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur?
fact: Malory had finished writing it about 15 years earlier.

fact: The first restaurant was in Rosettenville, Johannesburg.

The oat milk brand Oatly was founded in which country?
Bubble tea was invented in the 1980s in which place?
fact: The chewy pearls are made from tapioca starch.

text: Halloumi, the squeaky brunch cheese, comes originally from which island?
The hangover "cure" known as hair of the dog means having what?
fact: It may dull things briefly but can drag the hangover out. Only time cures one.

text: The Espresso Martini is credited to bartender Dick Bradsell, in the 1980s, in which city?
Which spirit is the base of a Caipirinha?
fact: The Caipirinha is cachaça, sugar and lime.

text: Prosecco is made mainly from which grape?
fact: The grape itself was called Prosecco until Italy renamed it in 2009.

text: Little Creatures brewery was founded in 2000 in which port city?
Australia's first Hungry Jack's opened in 1971 in which city?
fact: It was in the suburb of Innaloo.

text: The burrito chain Zambrero was founded in 2005 in which city?
fact: Founder Sam Prince was a medical student at the time.

text: Chicken salt was invented in the 1970s in which state?
fact: Peter Brinkworth of Gawler made it to season rotisserie chickens.

text: Which chef's Sydney cafe is often credited as the first to put avocado toast on its menu, in 1993?
fact: The cafe was Bills, in Darlinghurst.

text: In which city does a "pint" of beer traditionally mean a 425 ml glass?
fact: That is the size other states call a schooner.

text: The Chiko Roll was first sold in 1951 at the agricultural show in which town?
fact: Inventor Frank McEncroe was a boilermaker from Bendigo.

text: Pimm's No. 1 Cup is based on which spirit?
Sriracha sauce is named after a town in which country?
fact: The town is Si Racha.

text: The Australian dim sim, or "dimmy", was popularised in the 1940s from which city's Chinatown?
fact: William Chen Wing Young began making them commercially there in about 1945.

text: How many beers are in a standard Australian slab?
In darts, what is the highest score possible with three darts?
fact: It takes three treble 20s.

text: How many millilitres are in a standard Australian nip, or single shot, of spirits?
Counting the cue ball, how many balls are on the table at the start of a game of eight-ball pool?
In what year was Boost Juice founded?
fact: Janine Allis opened the first store in Adelaide.

text: McDonald's says its Chicken McNuggets come in how many shapes?
fact: They are the bell, the bone, the ball and the boot.

text: Jägermeister is made with how many herbs and spices?
In what year did the first Guzman y Gomez open, in Newtown, Sydney?
fact: Its founders, Steven Marks and Robert Hazan, were both from New York.

Which Queensland State of Origin great was nicknamed "The King"?
fact: He won eight State of Origin man of the match awards.

text: Which club plays its home games at Brookvale Oval?
fact: The ground has carried the sponsored name 4 Pines Park since 2021.

text: Which club joined Western Suburbs to form Wests Tigers, who first played in 2000?
fact: Wests Tigers won the premiership in 2005, their sixth season.

text: Which actor became a co-owner of South Sydney in 2006?
fact: He took over the club with businessman Peter Holmes à Court.

text: Which club's home crowd performs the "Viking Clap" before kick-off?
fact: Raiders fans took it up in 2016, the year Iceland's supporters made it famous.

text: Who coached the Brisbane Broncos for their first 21 seasons?
fact: He later won a premiership with St George Illawarra, in 2010.

text: What is the Australian women's rugby league team called?
fact: A jillaroo is a female jackaroo. The team took the name around 2000.

text: Which Australian singer joined Tina Turner on the NSWRL's 1992 advertising campaign song?
fact: Turner fronted the league's advertising from 1989 to 1995.

text: Who won the Clive Churchill Medal in 2025?
Who kicked the golden point field goal that won North Queensland the 2015 grand final?
fact: It was the first grand final decided in golden point, and the Cowboys' first premiership.

text: Who coached Canberra to its premierships in 1989, 1990 and 1994?
fact: He won a fourth premiership as coach of Wests Tigers.

text: Which club did Brisbane beat in the first NRL grand final, in 1998?
fact: Brisbane won 38-12 at the Sydney Football Stadium.

text: South Sydney captain John Sattler played most of the 1970 grand final with a broken what?
fact: Souths beat Manly 23-12, and he went to hospital only after accepting the trophy.

text: Which club went into a joint venture with Manly for the 2000 season?
fact: They played as the Northern Eagles for three seasons. Manly returned as itself in 2003.

text: Which club was nicknamed the "Chocolate Soldiers" in its early years, for its brown and white jerseys?
fact: Penrith joined the premiership in 1967 wearing brown with a white V.

text: Who coached Queensland through its record run of State of Origin series wins from 2006?
fact: He coached the Maroons for ten series, from 2006 to 2015, and lost only one.

text: Who captained Queensland in the very first State of Origin match?
fact: Beetson was 35 and had long played for New South Wales under the old residency rules.

text: Which nation beat Australia in the 2008 Rugby League World Cup final?
fact: The Kiwis won 34-20 at Lang Park in Brisbane, their first World Cup title.

text: Which fullback won the Dally M Medal in both 2019 and 2025?
fact: In 2025 he polled 67 points to win by 22 from Nathan Cleary.

text: Which coach, nicknamed "Supercoach", won five premierships with Easts and Parramatta?
fact: He won two with Easts and then three in a row with Parramatta.

text: In 2021 the NRL made a field goal worth two points if kicked from beyond how many metres out?
fact: Adam Reynolds kicked the first under the new rule, from 43 metres, in April 2021.

text: Which prop, who won premierships with three clubs, was nicknamed "The Brick with Eyes"?
fact: He won two with Canberra, two with Brisbane and one with Melbourne.

text: Which club won back-to-back NRLW premierships in the 2022 and 2023 seasons?
fact: They beat Parramatta in the 2022 grand final and Gold Coast in 2023.

text: As of the end of 2025, who had played the most Tests for the Kangaroos?
fact: Lockyer played 59 Tests, three more than Cameron Smith.

text: Which of these players was one of the four original Immortals named in 1981?
fact: The other three were Clive Churchill, Reg Gasnier and Johnny Raper.

text: Which club did South Sydney beat in the first premiership final, in 1908?
fact: Souths won 14-12 at the Royal Agricultural Society Showground.

text: Who scored the try in the final seconds that won Newcastle the 1997 ARL grand final?
fact: Andrew Johns set it up with a run down the blind side. Newcastle beat Manly 22-16.

text: In the 2003 grand final, Penrith's Scott Sattler ran down which Roosters winger?
fact: Penrith won 18-6. Scott is the son of Souths great John Sattler.

text: In 1987 a State of Origin exhibition match was played in which American city?
fact: New South Wales won 30-18 at Veterans Memorial Stadium in California.

text: What nickname was given to the 1986 Kangaroo touring side?
fact: The Invincibles were the 1982 tourists. The 1986 side also won every match of its tour.

text: Who scored a record eight tries in one premiership match, in 1920?
fact: Burge was a forward. Nobody had matched his eight by the end of the 2025 season.

text: Which radio caller was known for "It's long enough, it's high enough and it's straight between the posts"?
fact: Hyde called matches on Sydney radio station 2SM.

text: Which foundation club played its last premiership season in 1929?
fact: It finished runner-up four times but never won a premiership.

text: Who was the first winner of the Clive Churchill Medal, in 1986?
fact: Parramatta beat Canterbury 4-2 that day without a try being scored.

text: Which club lost the only Super League grand final, in 1997?
fact: Brisbane won 26-8 at home in front of 58,912.

text: Who scored Queensland's last-minute "miracle" try to win the first State of Origin game of 1994?
fact: Ray Warren's call was "That's not a try, that's a miracle!"

text: In the NRL, how many minutes does a player sent to the sin bin spend off the field?
fact: The sin bin came into the premiership in 1981.

text: In what year did Cronulla win its first premiership?
fact: The Sharks beat Melbourne 14-12. They had joined the premiership in 1967.

text: How many premierships in a row did St George win, starting in 1956?
fact: The run lasted until 1966 and was still the record at the end of the 2025 season.

text: In what year did the Brisbane Broncos play their first premiership season?
fact: Newcastle and the Gold Coast-Tweed Giants joined in the same year.

text: How many clubs played in the 1995 ARL premiership, after four new clubs joined?
fact: The newcomers were Auckland, North Queensland, South Queensland and the Western Reds.

text: In what year was the last grand final played at the Sydney Cricket Ground?
fact: Manly beat Canberra 18-8 in front of 50,201.

text: How many premiership tries did Ken Irvine score, the record until Alex Johnston passed it in 2026?
fact: He scored 171 for North Sydney and 41 for Manly, from 1958 to 1973.

text: In 1935 St George ran up a record score against Canterbury. How many points did St George score?
fact: St George won 91-6, still the highest score and biggest margin at the end of 2025.

text: How many NRL games did Cameron Smith play, all of them for Melbourne Storm?
fact: In 2019 he became the first player to reach 400.

text: Put these clubs in order of when they joined the premiership, earliest first.
Put these clubs in order of their first premiership win, earliest first.
Put these changes to the Australian game in order, earliest first.
Put these goal-kickers in order of career premiership points, most first.
Put these players in order of State of Origin games played, most first.
Which of these is not one of the five ring colours on the Olympic flag?
fact: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red.

text: Who lit the cauldron at the opening ceremony of the Sydney 2000 Olympics?
fact: Debbie Flintoff-King handed her the torch for the final steps.

text: Which sprinter won both the 100 m and 200 m at three Olympics in a row, from 2008 to 2016?
Rachael "Raygun" Gunn competed for Australia at Paris 2024 in which sport?
fact: Paris 2024 was the sport's Olympic debut, and it is not on the programme for 2028.

text: Each medal at Paris 2024 held a piece of iron taken from which landmark?
fact: A hexagon of iron from the tower was set into every medal.

text: In a film made for the London 2012 opening ceremony, who escorted the Queen to the stadium?
fact: Daniel Craig played Bond, and a stuntman dressed as the Queen made the parachute jump.

text: Kaylee McKeown won the 100 m and 200 m of which stroke at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024?
Which country traditionally enters the stadium first in the opening ceremony's parade of nations?
fact: The host nation's team comes in last.

text: Dawn Fraser won which event at three Olympics in a row, in 1956, 1960 and 1964?
Which Australian won three golds, a silver and a bronze in the pool at Munich 1972, aged 15?
fact: Her golds came in the 200 m and 400 m freestyle and the 200 m individual medley.

text: Which Australian shared the podium with Tommie Smith and John Carlos during their 1968 protest?
fact: He won silver in the 200 m and wore a human rights badge in support.

text: Which aerial skier won Australia's second Winter Olympic gold, two days after Steven Bradbury's?
Jessica Fox won two golds at Paris 2024. In which event did her sister Noemie also win gold?
fact: Noemie was the event's first Olympic champion. Jessica went out in the heats.

text: Who became Australia's youngest ever Olympic gold medallist at Paris 2024?
fact: She was 14 when she won the women's park skateboarding.

text: Which 14-year-old gymnast was awarded seven perfect 10s at the Montreal 1976 Olympics?
fact: The scoreboard could not show 10.00, so her first one came up as 1.00.

text: In ice hockey's "Miracle on Ice" at the 1980 Winter Olympics, which team did the USA upset?
fact: The USA won 4-3, then had to beat Finland two days later to take the gold.

text: Which sport returned to the Olympics at Rio 2016 after 112 years away?
Which sport made its Olympic debut at Tokyo 2020 but was left out of Paris 2024?
Where is the Olympic flame lit before each Games?
fact: The sun's rays are focused by a curved mirror to light it.

text: After Ben Johnson was disqualified at Seoul 1988, who was awarded the men's 100 m gold?
fact: Christie moved up to silver and Smith to bronze.

text: Under which three letters did Russian athletes compete at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics?
fact: It stood for Russian Olympic Committee. They were OAR at the 2018 Winter Games.

text: Eric "the Eel" Moussambani, cheered home in a 100 m freestyle heat at Sydney 2000, swam for whom?
fact: He swam alone after both rivals false-started, and finished in 1:52.72.

text: Sydney 2000 had three official mascots: Syd, Olly and Millie. Which animal was Millie?
fact: Syd was a platypus and Olly a kookaburra. The wombat, Fatso, was unofficial.

text: Edwin Flack, Australia's first Olympic champion, won which two races at the 1896 Games?
fact: He led the marathon too, but collapsed before the finish.

text: Which runner, later a multiple world record holder, lit the cauldron at Melbourne 1956 aged 19?
fact: He burned his arm as the cauldron caught.

text: Which American said his team would "smash them like guitars" before Australia won a relay in 2000?
fact: It was the USA's first Olympic loss in the event, after seven wins from seven.

text: Who won the 5000 m, 10,000 m and marathon at the same Games, Helsinki 1952?
fact: It was the first marathon he had ever run.

text: Which 30-year-old mother of two won four athletics golds at London 1948?
fact: The Dutch sprinter was nicknamed "the Flying Housewife".

text: Whose record of 18 Olympic medals stood from 1964 until Michael Phelps passed it in 2012?
fact: The Soviet gymnast won nine gold, five silver and four bronze.

text: American Eddie Eagan won gold at both the Summer and Winter Olympics. In which two sports?
fact: He won as a light heavyweight in 1920 and in Billy Fiske's bob crew in 1932.

text: At which Olympic Games was the five-ring Olympic flag first flown?
From 1912 to 1948 the Olympics gave medals for the arts. Which of these was a medal event?
fact: It joined in 1928, alongside architecture, literature, music, painting and sculpture.

text: Over 20 African nations boycotted the 1976 Games after which rugby team toured South Africa?
fact: The IOC had refused to ban New Zealand from the Games.

text: The Paralympics grew out of 1948 games for injured war veterans at which English hospital?
fact: Dr Ludwig Guttmann held them on the day the London Olympics opened.

text: Sydney won the right to host the 2000 Games by two votes in the final round. Which city lost?
fact: The final vote in Monte Carlo in 1993 was 45 to 43.

text: At which Winter Games did Torvill and Dean skate to Boléro and earn twelve perfect 6.0s?
fact: The British ice dancers came back ten years later and won bronze.

text: How long is an Olympic swimming pool?
How many gold medals did Michael Phelps win at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
fact: That beat Mark Spitz's seven at a single Games.

text: In what year were the first Winter Olympics held?
fact: They were held in Chamonix, France.

text: How many Olympic gold medals did Ian Thorpe win in his career?
fact: Three came at Sydney 2000 and two at Athens 2004.

text: How many medals did Emma McKeon win at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics?
fact: Four gold and three bronze, equalling the most by a woman at one Games.

text: In what year was the Olympic torch relay first run?
fact: It was introduced for the Berlin Games, with over 3,000 runners carrying the flame.

text: As of Paris 2024, cricket had been played at only one Olympics. In what year?
fact: Great Britain beat France in the only match.

text: In what year were solid gold medals last awarded at the Olympics?
fact: A gold medal today is at least 92.5% silver, plated with at least six grams of gold.

text: In what year were the first Paralympic Games held?
fact: Rome hosted them in September 1960, days after its Olympics closed.

text: Put these cities in order of when they first hosted the Summer Olympics, earliest first.
Which band sang Come On Eileen?
fact: The record is credited to Dexys Midnight Runners and the Emerald Express.

text: Which group had a hit in 2000 with Who Let the Dogs Out?
fact: Trinidad's Anslem Douglas first released it in 1998, under the title Doggie.

text: Which country star joined Lil Nas X on the hit remix of Old Town Road?
fact: The remix came out in April 2019, four months after the original.

text: I'll Be There for You by The Rembrandts is the theme song of which sitcom?
fact: The TV theme runs under a minute. The duo stretched it into a full single in 1995.

text: Which singer had a 1999 hit with Mambo No. 5 (A Little Bit of...)?
fact: Born in Munich, he built it on an instrumental by the Cuban bandleader Pérez Prado.

text: Teenage Dirtbag was a hit in 2000 for which American band?
fact: It missed the US Hot 100 altogether but spent four weeks at No. 1 in Australia.

text: Terry Crews sings along to Vanessa Carlton's A Thousand Miles in which 2004 comedy?
fact: Crews plays the basketball star Latrell Spencer.

text: Vanilla Ice's Ice Ice Baby takes its bass line from which song?
fact: Its writers got no credit on Ice Ice Baby until after it had become a hit.

text: Macarena was a worldwide hit for which Spanish duo?
fact: The Bayside Boys remix spent 14 weeks at No. 1 in the US in 1996.

text: Rednex, the group behind the hoedown dance hit Cotton Eye Joe, came from which country?
fact: Their producers reworked an old American folk song, Cotton-Eyed Joe, as a techno track.

text: Which model plays the title role in the video for Fountains of Wayne's Stacy's Mom?
fact: The band took its name from a lawn ornament shop in Wayne, New Jersey.

text: In 2006, Daniel Powter's Bad Day played as contestants were voted off which TV show?
fact: It ended 2006 as Billboard's No. 1 song of the year on the Hot 100.
wrong: So You Think You Can Dance

text: Which superstar sings the chorus of Rockwell's 1984 hit Somebody's Watching Me?
fact: Rockwell is a son of Berry Gordy, the founder of Motown.

text: Which band, known for Walking on Sunshine, won Eurovision for the UK in 1997?
fact: They won with Love Shine a Light, 12 years after their big hit.

text: Linda Perry, who wrote Pink's Get the Party Started, sang which 1993 hit with her own band?
fact: The band was 4 Non Blondes. Perry also wrote Christina Aguilera's Beautiful.

text: Which Melbourne band took a rock cover of Funky Town to No. 1 in Australia?
fact: It stayed on top for seven weeks. Lipps Inc. had the original disco hit in 1980.

text: What About Me, a No. 1 for Shannon Noll in 2004, was first a No. 1 for which Australian band?
fact: The original spent six weeks at No. 1 in 1982.

text: Brisbane-born Gina G sang Ooh Aah... Just a Little Bit for which country at Eurovision 1996?
fact: She finished eighth, but the song went to No. 1 on the UK singles chart.

text: Haddaway's What Is Love is the head-bobbing anthem of which Will Ferrell comedy?
fact: The 1998 film grew out of a Saturday Night Live sketch with Ferrell and Chris Kattan.

text: Joe Dolce, who had a huge hit with Shaddap You Face, was born in which country?
fact: He was born in Painesville, Ohio, and settled in Melbourne in the late 1970s.

text: Little Eva, who had the first hit with The Loco-Motion, had been working for its writers as what?
fact: The writers were the husband-and-wife team of Carole King and Gerry Goffin.

text: Taylor Swift's Look What You Made Me Do gives a writing credit to the men behind which hit?
fact: Her chorus follows the rhythm of Right Said Fred's song.

text: Which 1996 film, written and directed by Tom Hanks, follows a 1960s band with a single hit?
fact: The band is the Wonders. Adam Schlesinger of Fountains of Wayne wrote the title song.

text: Soft Cell's Tainted Love was first recorded in the 1960s by which American singer?
fact: Jones recorded it in 1964 and later played keyboards in T. Rex.

text: Which German-language song reached No. 1 on the US Hot 100 in March 1986?
fact: It was by Falco, from Vienna. Nena's 99 Luftballons had stalled at No. 2 two years earlier.

text: Bananarama's 1986 hit Venus was first a US No. 1 in 1970 for which Dutch band?
fact: Bananarama's version also went to No. 1 in the US.

text: The nonsense chorus of The Ketchup Song is a garbled take on which hip hop classic?
fact: In the song, Diego hears his favourite record in a club and sings along as best he can.

text: O-Zone, the boy band behind the 'Numa Numa' song Dragostea Din Tei, formed in which country?
fact: The title is Romanian for "the love from the linden tree".

text: Mr. Oizo's 1999 hit Flat Beat, with its yellow puppet Flat Eric, came out of TV ads for which brand?
fact: Flat Eric was built by Jim Henson's Creature Shop. The single was a UK No. 1.

text: Gotye built Somebody That I Used to Know on a guitar sample from which Brazilian musician?
fact: The sample comes from Seville, a 1967 instrumental. Bonfá shares the writing credit.

text: Counting the Beat, a No. 1 in Australia in 1981, was by which New Zealand band?
fact: Their frontman, Phil Judd, had been a founding member of Split Enz.

text: DJ Casper first wrote the Cha Cha Slide as what?
fact: It was for his nephew, a fitness trainer at a Bally Total Fitness gym in Chicago.

text: Which Australian act went to No. 1 in the UK in 2010 with We No Speak Americano?
fact: It samples Tu vuò fà l'americano, a 1956 song by Italy's Renato Carosone.

text: Which other comedian has a writing credit on Austen Tayshus's pun-filled No. 1, Australiana?
fact: Birmingham went on to send up cricket commentators as The Twelfth Man.

text: After Video Killed the Radio Star, both members of The Buggles joined which prog rock band?
fact: Trevor Horn and Geoff Downes joined for the 1980 album Drama.

text: Even When I'm Sleeping, APRA's Song of the Year for 1998, was by which Sydney band?
fact: Abby Dobson sang it. It beat Paul Kelly's How to Make Gravy to the award.

text: In I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles), how many miles in total do The Proclaimers say they would walk?
fact: The Scottish twins' song was No. 1 in Australia for five weeks in 1989.

text: The Italian group behind Blue (Da Ba Dee) is called Eiffel what?
fact: The band say the 65 came from a phone number scribbled on a label copy by mistake.

text: In what year did Chumbawamba release Tubthumping?
fact: The band had formed in Burnley, Lancashire, back in 1982.

text: In what year was the line-dancing hit Achy Breaky Heart released?
fact: It was No. 1 in Australia for seven weeks.

text: In what year did Owl City's Fireflies reach No. 1 on the US Hot 100?
fact: Owl City is Adam Young, who began recording in his parents' basement in Minnesota.

text: In what year did Zager and Evans top the US chart with In the Year 2525?
fact: It was No. 1 for six weeks, including the week of the first Moon landing.

text: By 2003, Spirit in the Sky had been a UK No. 1 single for how many different acts?
fact: Norman Greenbaum (1970), Doctor and the Medics (1986) and Gareth Gates (2003).

text: In what year did The Knack release My Sharona?
fact: It spent six weeks at No. 1 in the US. Sharona Alperin, who inspired it, is on the sleeve.

text: In what year did Carl Douglas release Kung Fu Fighting?
fact: Recorded in a hurry as a B-side, it went to No. 1 in both the UK and the US.

What breed of dog is Snoopy, from the Peanuts comic strip?
fact: He first appeared on 4 October 1950, two days after the strip began.

text: A cavoodle is a poodle crossed with which other breed?
fact: Overseas the same cross is usually called a cavapoo.

text: How do dogs get rid of most of their excess body heat?
fact: Dogs do have sweat glands in their paw pads, but these play only a small part.

text: Where on a dog or cat is an identity microchip normally implanted?
fact: It sits just under the skin between the shoulder blades and is about the size of a grain of rice.

text: Which food does the cartoon cat Garfield love above all others?
fact: His owner is Jon Arbuckle, and the day of the week he hates is Monday.

text: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, what is the last part of the Cheshire Cat to disappear?
fact: Alice thinks she has often seen a cat without a grin, but never a grin without a cat.

text: Which breed of cat is best known for having no tail?
fact: It comes from the Isle of Man, where a cat with no tail at all is called a rumpy.

text: Why is a saucer of milk a poor treat for many adult cats?
fact: Cornell's vet school says dairy can give lactose-intolerant cats an upset stomach.

text: The budgie is a small parrot native to which country?
fact: Wild budgies are green and yellow. They have been bred in captivity since the 1850s.

text: Wally Conron bred his first labradoodles in 1989 while working for which kind of organisation?
fact: He wanted a guide dog for a blind woman whose husband was allergic to dog hair.

text: Despite its name, the Australian shepherd was developed as a breed in which country?
fact: It took shape on ranches in the western United States in the late 1800s.

text: The kelpie is named after a shape-shifting water spirit from the folklore of which country?
fact: The first Kelpie was a black and tan pup from Victoria. Jack Gleeson swapped a horse for her.

text: In Hairy Maclary from Donaldson's Dairy, which tomcat sends all the dogs running home?
fact: New Zealander Lynley Dodd's book first came out in 1983.

text: In the American Kennel Club's 2022 rankings, which breed ended the Labrador's 31 years at number one?
fact: It was the first time the breed had topped the list.

text: What is the name for the extra claw set higher up on the inside of a dog's leg?
fact: Almost all dogs have them on the front legs. Only some have them on the back legs too.

text: Dogs are not fully colour-blind. Which two colours can their eyes pick out?
fact: Dogs have two types of colour-sensing cone in their eyes. People have three.

text: What is the mottled coat pattern, often seen with blue eyes, that is common in Australian shepherds?
fact: In dachshunds the same pattern is known as dapple.

text: Nearly all tortoiseshell and calico cats have what in common?
fact: The orange gene sits on the X chromosome. Only about 1 in 3,000 tortoiseshells is male.

text: Which of these is a collective noun for a group of cats?
fact: A skulk is of foxes, a sleuth is of bears and a bask is of crocodiles.

text: What was the name of the ship's cat who sailed with the navigator Matthew Flinders?
fact: A bronze Trim sits on a window ledge of Sydney's Mitchell Library, behind a statue of Flinders.

text: Which popular cut flower is so toxic to cats that even its pollen or vase water is dangerous?
fact: Every part of the plant is a risk to a cat's kidneys, so vets say keep lilies out of the house.

text: Which taste can cats not detect, because of a broken gene?
fact: Cats lack a working copy of Tas1r2, a gene needed to build the sweet receptor.

text: Guinea pigs are neither pigs nor from Guinea. Which continent do they come from?
fact: They were first domesticated in the Andes.

text: The original statue of Red Dog, the wandering Pilbara kelpie cross, stands in which WA town?
fact: A second statue went up in 2023 in Paraburdoo, where he is believed to have been born.

text: Balto ran the last leg of the 1925 serum run into which Alaskan town, now the Iditarod's finish?
fact: The relay carried diphtheria antitoxin. Togo's team ran the farthest of all.

text: As of the 2026 show, which breed has won Best in Show at Westminster the most times?
fact: It has won 15 times, most recently in 2019. The Scottish terrier is next with eight.

text: By the usual account, the Australian silky terrier came from crossing the Australian terrier with which breed?
fact: For decades it was called the Sydney silky. Its early history is poorly documented.

text: In a 2007 Italian study, pet dogs' tails wagged with a bias to their left at the sight of what?
fact: For their owner, a stranger or a cat, the wag leaned to the dog's right.

text: Which NSW pastoralist crossed dingoes with imported British dogs to create the first "Heelers"?
fact: Hall's Heelers, bred at Dartbrook from 1840, were the forerunners of the Australian cattle dog.

text: At Dogs Australia shows, which group does the Great Dane compete in?
fact: The poodle, the Dalmatian and the chow chow are in the same group.

text: A Siamese cat's dark face, ears, paws and tail come from a pigment enzyme that is sensitive to what?
fact: The enzyme only works in the cooler parts of the body. Kittens are born cream or white.

text: What is the reflective layer behind a cat's retina, which makes its eyes shine in the dark, called?
fact: Dogs have one too. People do not.

text: The Bengal cat breed was created by crossing domestic cats with which wild species?
fact: American breeder Jean Mill made the cross that began the breed in 1963.

text: In Tom and Jerry's first cartoon, Puss Gets the Boot, what was the cat called?
fact: The mouse was not named on screen at all. Hanna and Barbera directed it for MGM.

text: Which of the four main tabby patterns has thin, vertical stripes running down the cat's sides?
fact: Whatever the pattern, a tabby almost always has an M-shaped mark on its forehead.

text: What is a group of ferrets called?
fact: A male ferret is a hob, a female is a jill and the young are kits.

text: In the English saying, how many lives does a cat have?
fact: In Italy, Germany, Greece and Brazil the saying gives cats only seven.

text: By the old rule of thumb, one year of a dog's life equals how many human years?
fact: Vets say it is not that simple: a dog's first year is closer to 15 human years.

text: In what year did Larry the cat move into 10 Downing Street as Chief Mouser?
fact: He came from Battersea Dogs & Cats Home that February, when David Cameron was prime minister.

text: RSPCA Australia says a puppy should be at least how many weeks old before leaving its mother?
fact: It should also be fully weaned by then.

text: About how many days does a dog's pregnancy last on average?
fact: That is nine weeks. Anything from 57 to 65 days is normal.

text: How many toes does a cat normally have in total?
fact: Five on each front paw and four on each back paw.

text: For how many years is Greyfriars Bobby said to have guarded his master's grave in Edinburgh?
fact: His owner, John Gray, was a night watchman for the Edinburgh police.

text: In what year was The Seeing Eye, the oldest guide dog school in the United States, founded?
fact: Dorothy Harrison Eustis and Morris Frank set it up in Nashville, Tennessee.

text: In what year was the first bronze statue of Hachiko unveiled at Shibuya station in Tokyo?
fact: Hachiko, an Akita, was still alive. The statue was melted down in 1945 and replaced in 1948.

On Lego Masters Australia, judge Ryan McNaught is better known by which nickname?
fact: Hamish Blake was the host when the show began on Nine.

text: At a MAFS commitment ceremony, each partner writes down one of which two words?
fact: Under the rules, a couple only goes home if both of them write "leave".

text: On My Kitchen Rules, what are the dinners that teams cook and host in their own homes called?
Who joined Julia Morris as co-host of I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! in 2024?
fact: He took over from Dr Chris Brown, her co-host since the show began in 2015.

text: Who took over as host of The Block when the show returned in 2010?
fact: He won the Gold Logie in 2014.

text: Which long-serving MasterChef Australia judge was known for his cravats?
fact: A 2009 collection of his food writing was titled Cravat-A-Licious.

text: On Survivor, what does the host say as he snuffs out a voted-off player's torch?
On Love Island, what do Islanders shout when a message from the producers arrives?
Which singer was crowned the very first American Idol?
fact: She beat Justin Guarini in a live final at the Kodak Theatre in Hollywood.

text: The original Big Brother Australia house stood at which Gold Coast theme park?
fact: After a spell in Sydney under Seven, the show went back there for Ten's 2025 series.

text: Which Australian Idol judge turned the "touchdown" into a trademark way of praising a performance?
fact: The first one went to Cosima De Vito in season one.

text: Which MasterChef Australia judge won the show as a contestant in 2012?
fact: He joined the judging panel in 2020.

text: In 2010 a federal election leaders' debate was moved so it would not clash with which show's finale?
fact: The Gillard v Abbott debate was moved to 6.30 pm and cut from 90 minutes to an hour.

text: Who hosted Australian Survivor on Ten from 2016 to 2025?
fact: His last season was Australia V The World. David Genat took over in 2026.

text: Which former NRL player became host of The Amazing Race Australia when Ten revived it in 2019?
fact: Grant Bowler hosted the earlier version on Seven.

text: Which cricketer was the first King of the Jungle on Australia's I'm a Celebrity, in 2015?
fact: He entered the South African camp as an intruder and beat Barry Hall in the final.

text: Which Hollywood actor sat on the guessing panel for The Masked Singer Australia's first season in 2019?
fact: She sat beside Dannii Minogue, Dave Hughes and Jackie O.

text: Which singer, later known for Brother and Resolution, was runner-up on Australian Idol in 2007?
fact: Natalie Gauci won that season. Brother won the ARIA for Song of the Year in 2012.

text: From season 33 in 2016 to season 50 in 2026, every American Survivor was filmed in which country?
fact: The show's home there is the Mamanuca Islands.

text: In 2011, which act became the first group to win The X Factor in the UK?
fact: Earlier in the series they were called Rhythmix.

text: Selling Sunset follows the agents of which Los Angeles real estate brokerage?
fact: Twin brothers Jason and Brett Oppenheim both appear on the show.

text: On Netflix's Queer Eye, which member of the Fab Five is the food and wine expert?
fact: The Netflix series ran for ten seasons, from 2018 to 2026.

text: On RuPaul's Drag Race, what does RuPaul tell the queen who loses the lip sync and goes home?
fact: "Sashay" and "shantay" are both in RuPaul's 1992 single Supermodel (You Better Work).

text: MasterChef Australia had a host in 2009, before the judges took over the job. Who was it?
fact: She presented the first season only.

text: Which network aired the first Australian Survivor, back in 2002?
fact: It was filmed on South Australia's Eyre Peninsula and hosted by Lincoln Howes.

text: Australian Survivor: Brains V Brawn (2021) was filmed near which outback Queensland town?
fact: It was the first season of the Ten era to be filmed in Australia.

text: The British I'm a Celebrity is usually filmed in bushland near which NSW town?
fact: Its 2020 and 2021 series were made at Gwrych Castle in Wales instead.

text: The lifeguards on Bondi Rescue work for which local council?
fact: The show first aired on Ten in 2006.

text: Which Home and Away star won the first season of Dancing with the Stars in 2004?
fact: Her dance partner was Michael Miziner. Daryl Somers and Sonia Kruger hosted.

text: Who won Big Brother Australia in 2003 and then won it again in 2022?
fact: She was the first housemate to win the Australian show twice.

text: The first season of Below Deck Down Under (2022) was set in which part of Queensland?
fact: Captain Jason Chambers and chief stew Aesha Scott led the crew of the yacht Thalassa.

text: Survivor grew out of Expedition Robinson, which first went to air in 1997 in which country?
fact: The format itself was devised by British producer Charlie Parsons.

text: The first four British and American seasons of The Traitors were all filmed at which Scottish castle?
fact: The 19th-century castle stands north of Inverness, in the Highlands.

text: On The Amazing Race, what is the name for a task that only one member of a team may perform?
fact: A Detour is a choice between two tasks, and both team members take it on.

text: In which country were the first two seasons of Netflix's Squid Game: The Challenge filmed?
fact: Season one's opening game was shot at Cardington Studios in Bedford.

text: Courtney Act, once an Australian Idol contestant, won which British reality show in 2018?
fact: Courtney was also a runner-up on season 6 of RuPaul's Drag Race.

text: How many coaches sat in the red chairs on the first season of The Voice Australia?
fact: They were Delta Goodrem, Joel Madden, Seal and Keith Urban.

text: How many daughters does Kris Jenner, the "momager" of Keeping Up with the Kardashians, have?
fact: Kourtney, Kim, Khloé, Kendall and Kylie. She also has a son, Rob.

text: The Block first went to air on Nine in which year?
fact: The first Block was an apartment building in Bondi, Sydney.

text: In what year did The Great British Bake Off first air?
fact: Edd Kimber won the first series, which had only ten bakers.

text: In what year did Gogglebox Australia first air?
fact: It was the first show commissioned jointly by Foxtel and a free-to-air network.

text: How old was Casey Donovan when she won Australian Idol in 2004?
fact: She beat Anthony Callea in the final.

text: How many days did Gina Chick last in the Tasmanian wilderness to win the first Alone Australia?
fact: Her prize was $250,000.

text: How many days did the first season of the American Survivor last?
fact: Sixteen castaways started the game.

text: In what year did Border Security: Australia's Front Line first air?
fact: In the UK and Ireland it is shown as Nothing to Declare.

text: Put these Australian shows in order of their debut, earliest first.
Put these overseas shows in order of their first broadcast, earliest first.
Put these Big Brother Australia hosts in order of their first season in the job, earliest first.
