Put these stars of The Bachelorette Australia in order of their season, earliest first.
The deepest known point in the ocean, Challenger Deep, lies in which trench?
fact: It is nearly 11 km down. Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2 km of water above it.

text: What is the largest living reptile, with big males weighing more than a tonne?
fact: Big males can reach 6 m long. Its range takes in northern Australia.

text: Which cartoon is the longest-running scripted primetime TV series in American history?
fact: It is also America's longest-running sitcom and its longest-running animated series.

text: Which drinks brand paid for Felix Baumgartner's record skydive from the edge of space in 2012?
fact: The project was called Red Bull Stratos. He stepped off a capsule about 39 km up.

text: Which double-decker jet is the largest passenger airliner ever built?
fact: It first carried passengers in 2007, with Singapore Airlines. Production ended in 2021.

text: The world's longest fence runs more than 5,500 km across Australia. Which animals does it keep away from sheep?
fact: Guinness describes it as enclosing the main sheep areas of Australia.

text: The Guinness Book of Records was first published by a company that made what?
fact: The brewery's boss wanted a book that could settle arguments in pubs.

text: In 2024, which tour became the first in history to take more than US$2 billion at the box office?
fact: It began in Glendale, Arizona, in March 2023 and ended in Vancouver in December 2024.

text: Who wrote The Mousetrap, the world's longest-running play, which opened in London in 1952?
fact: The pandemic halted it in March 2020. It reopened 14 months later, in May 2021.

text: Which show, first aired in 1963, is the world's longest-running science fiction TV series?
fact: The first episode went out on the BBC on 23 November 1963.

text: Which diamond, found in South Africa in 1905, was still the largest gem-quality rough diamond on record in 2025?
fact: It weighed 3,106 carats, about 621 grams, and was named after the mine's owner.

text: The Welcome Stranger, the biggest alluvial gold nugget ever found, was dug up in 1869 in which colony?
fact: Two Cornish miners, John Deason and Richard Oates, found it at Moliagul, near Dunolly.

text: General Sherman, the largest living single-stem tree by volume as of 2025, is what kind of tree?
fact: It stands in Sequoia National Park in California.

text: The strongest earthquake recorded up to 2025, of about magnitude 9.5, struck which country in 1960?
fact: It struck on 22 May 1960. Valdivia was the worst-hit city.

text: As of 2025, the biggest wave ever officially surfed, 26.21 m high, was ridden at which spot?
fact: German surfer Sebastian Steudtner rode it in October 2020.

text: As of 2025, which is the longest railway tunnel in the world, at 57 km?
fact: It opened under the Swiss Alps in 2016 and is also the world's deepest traffic tunnel.

text: In 2015 a maglev train with 49 staff on board hit 603 km/h, faster than any train before it. In which country?
fact: It was a seven-car L0 Series train on JR Central's test track in Yamanashi.

text: As of 2025, which show has had the longest run in Broadway history?
fact: It closed in April 2023 after 13,981 performances.

text: As of 2025, who has won the most Academy Awards, with 22 competitive Oscars?
fact: He was nominated 59 times, also a record, and was given four honorary awards as well.

text: The shortest war on record, over in under an hour in 1896, was between Britain and which sultanate?
fact: It lasted between 38 and 45 minutes on 27 August 1896.

text: Guinness's longest-running laboratory experiment began in Brisbane in 1927. What does it watch drip?
fact: Only nine drops had fallen at the University of Queensland by 2025, the ninth in April 2014.

text: As of 2025, which city has the largest working tram network in the world?
fact: The network has about 250 km of double track.

text: In 1996 Concorde set the record for a passenger flight from New York to London. How long did it take?
fact: The exact time was 2 hours 52 minutes 59 seconds, on 7 February 1996.

text: Since 1997, Guinness World Records has refused to monitor which record, saying it is too dangerous?
fact: The last holder it listed, Robert McDonald, stayed awake for nearly 19 days in 1986.

text: Which is the largest fruit that grows on a tree, with some weighing more than 40 kg?
fact: The heaviest on Guinness's books, found in Florida in August 2024, weighed 54.43 kg.

text: Which twin brothers compiled the first Guinness Book of Records?
fact: The twins ran a London agency that supplied facts and figures to newspapers.

text: The Guinness book grew out of a 1951 shooting party in Ireland. Which bird had Sir Hugh Beaver just missed?
fact: The argument was over Europe's fastest game bird, and no reference book could settle it.

text: In 2014, who broke Felix Baumgartner's record for the highest skydive, jumping from over 41 km?
fact: He was a senior Google executive, and his record still stood in 2025.

text: In 1960, which vessel carried two men to the deepest point of the ocean for the first time?
fact: Its crew were Swiss oceanographer Jacques Piccard and US Navy lieutenant Don Walsh.

text: The Hoba meteorite, the largest single meteorite known on Earth, still lies where it fell in which country?
fact: It weighs more than 60 tonnes and has never been moved.

text: As of 2025 the lowest air temperature measured on the ground, -89.2 °C in 1983, was at which Antarctic base?
fact: Vostok is a Russian base about 3,500 m up on the East Antarctic ice sheet.

text: Ken Warby's 1978 water speed record still stood in 2025. On which NSW dam did he set it?
fact: His jet-powered boat was called Spirit of Australia.

text: As of 2025, the world's oldest roller coaster in continuous operation, opened in 1912, is at which park?
fact: It is the Great Scenic Railway, which opened with the park on 13 December 1912.

text: As of 2025, the world's shortest scheduled passenger flight, about 2.7 km, links two islands in which group?
fact: Loganair's hop from Westray to Papa Westray has been flown in as little as 53 seconds.

text: As of 2025 the world's largest working cattle station is Anna Creek. Which state or territory is it in?
fact: It is more than seven times the size of King Ranch, the biggest ranch in the United States.

text: As of 2025, the oldest world record in Olympic track and field dates from 1983. Which women's event is it?
fact: Jarmila Kratochvílová of Czechoslovakia ran 1:53.28 in Munich.

text: As of 2025, Jeanne Calment is the oldest person ever verified. How old was she when she died in 1997?
fact: She was born in Arles, France, in February 1875 and lived for 122 years and 164 days.

text: Guinness lists US park ranger Roy Sullivan as hit by lightning more times than anyone on record. How many?
fact: The strikes came between 1942 and 1977. He worked in Shenandoah National Park, Virginia.

text: In what year was the first Guinness Book of Records published?
fact: It was bound on 27 August 1955 and topped Britain's bestseller list by Christmas.

text: Robert Wadlow is the tallest person ever reliably measured. How tall was he, in centimetres?
fact: The American, from Alton, Illinois, died in 1940 aged 22.

text: American Charles Osborne had the longest attack of hiccups on record. How many years did it last?
fact: It began in 1922 and stopped in 1990.

text: As of 2025, what is the lowest temperature ever recorded in Australia, at Charlotte Pass, NSW, in 1994?
fact: Charlotte Pass is a ski village in the Snowy Mountains.

text: The world's longest dead-straight stretch of railway crosses the Nullarbor. How long is it, in km?
fact: It is part of the Trans-Australian Railway between Port Augusta and Kalgoorlie.

text: Mike Powell's long jump world record of 8.95 m still stood in 2025. In what year did he set it?
fact: He jumped it at the world championships in Tokyo, beating Carl Lewis on the night.

text: The Antonov An-225 Mriya, destroyed in 2022, was the heaviest aircraft ever built. How many engines did it have?
fact: Only one was ever finished. It was designed to carry the Soviet Buran space shuttle.

text: Which Beatles album cover shows the four of them walking across a zebra crossing?
fact: The photo was taken on 8 August 1969, outside the studios where they recorded.

text: Thunderstruck and T.N.T. are songs by which Australian band?
fact: T.N.T. was recorded in 1975. Thunderstruck came out in 1990, on The Razors Edge.

text: Jim Morrison was the lead singer of which 1960s band?
fact: They formed in Los Angeles in 1965, with Ray Manzarek on keyboards.

text: Stairway to Heaven is a 1971 song by which band?
fact: Jimmy Page wrote the music and Robert Plant the words. It is on their untitled fourth album.

text: Enter Sandman was a 1991 hit for which band?
fact: It opens their self-titled fifth album, often called the Black Album.

text: Which Guns N' Roses guitarist made a top hat his trademark on stage?
fact: He was born Saul Hudson in London in 1965.

text: Hound Dog and Jailhouse Rock were 1950s hits for which singer?
fact: Hound Dog came out in 1956 and Jailhouse Rock in 1957.

text: Which Australian rock singer was a federal government minister from 2007 to 2013?
fact: The Midnight Oil frontman was the member for Kingsford Smith from 2004 to 2013.

text: Ozzy Osbourne first found fame as the singer of which band?
fact: His first solo album, Blizzard of Ozz, came out in 1980.

text: Which punk band released the double album London Calling in 1979?
fact: The cover shows bassist Paul Simonon smashing his bass on stage in New York.

text: What is the name of Bruce Springsteen's long-time backing band?
fact: It first toured with him in 1972 and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014.

text: Iron Maiden's mascot has been on their album covers since their 1980 debut. What is he called?
fact: The wrong answers are the mascots of Megadeth, Motörhead and Dio.

text: Black Sabbath and Judas Priest both formed in which English city?
fact: Sabbath formed there in 1968 and Priest a year later.

text: Which band completes thrash metal's 'Big Four' with Metallica, Slayer and Megadeth?
fact: Anthrax formed in New York City in 1981.

text: Who played guitar in Rage Against the Machine?
fact: He later formed Audioslave with singer Chris Cornell.

text: The four members of System of a Down who recorded Toxicity all share which heritage?
fact: The band formed in Glendale, California, in 1994.

text: Which Australian band broke through with the double A-side Second Solution / Prisoner of Society?
fact: It won the 1998 ARIA for Highest Selling Single. Scott Owen played double bass, not bass guitar.

text: Metalcore band Parkway Drive formed in 2003 in which NSW town?
fact: They took their name from the street where they rehearsed.

text: Which solid-body electric guitar did Gibson first sell in 1952?
fact: The Flying V and Explorer arrived in 1958 and the SG in 1961.

text: Which member of Queen wrote Another One Bites the Dust?
fact: Deacon was the band's bassist. The song is on the album The Game.

text: In Kiss's original line-up, which member wore the Catman make-up?
fact: Criss was the drummer. The others were the Spaceman, the Demon and the Starchild.

text: Jimi Hendrix set his guitar on fire at the end of Wild Thing at which festival?
fact: He poured lighter fluid on the guitar, set it alight, then smashed it on the stage.

text: Which Chuck Berry song was sent into space on the Voyager Golden Record?
fact: A copy of the record was fixed to each of the two Voyager spacecraft.

text: The Rolling Stones' tongue and lips logo made its debut with which album?
fact: John Pasche designed the logo in 1970. The album followed in April 1971.

text: Which guitarist founded Fleetwood Mac in London in 1967?
fact: He named the band after drummer Mick Fleetwood and bassist John McVie.

text: Low and Heroes are two parts of David Bowie's Berlin Trilogy. Which album is the third?
fact: Low and Heroes both came out in 1977, and Lodger in 1979.

text: Who was the Sex Pistols' original bassist, replaced by Sid Vicious?
The Ramones formed in 1974 in which New York City borough?
fact: They came from the Forest Hills neighbourhood, and each took the surname Ramone.

text: Who produced Slayer's 1986 album Reign in Blood?
fact: It came out on Def Jam, a label far better known for hip hop.

text: Which Pantera album debuted at No. 1 on the US chart in 1994?
fact: It reached No. 1 in Australia as well.

text: In 2019 Tool released their first album in 13 years. What is it called?
fact: It followed 10,000 Days, from 2006.

text: Before Queens of the Stone Age, Josh Homme played guitar in which stoner rock band?
fact: Kyuss formed in Palm Desert, California, in 1987.

text: Deep Purple's Smoke on the Water describes a fire that broke out during whose concert?
fact: It was at the Montreux Casino in December 1971. The song blames someone with a flare gun.

text: Who was AC/DC's first lead singer, before Bon Scott joined in 1974?
fact: He sang on the band's first single, Can I Sit Next to You Girl, in 1974.

text: Jim Marshall, the founder of Marshall amplifiers, played and taught which instrument?
fact: He ran a music shop in Hanwell, west London, and was nicknamed the Father of Loud.

text: Soundwave grew out of a 2004 action sports event in which Australian city?
fact: It began as Gravity Soundwave, the music side of the Gravity Games.

text: How many strings does a standard electric guitar have?
fact: Standard tuning, from the lowest string, is E, A, D, G, B, E.

text: How many members did Slipknot have when their debut album came out in 1999?
fact: The members were also known by the numbers 0 to 8.

text: In what year did Pink Floyd release The Dark Side of the Moon?
fact: Its cover shows a prism splitting a beam of white light into colours.

text: The Big Day Out ran every year from 1992 to 2014 except one. In which year was there no festival?
fact: The organisers took a year off, and the festival was back in 1999.

text: How many studio albums did Nirvana release?
fact: The first was Bleach, in 1989, and the last was In Utero, in 1993.

text: In what year did the Sex Pistols release Never Mind the Bollocks, their only studio album?
fact: It came out on Virgin Records on 28 October.

text: In what year did Elvis make his first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show?
fact: Actor Charles Laughton filled in as host, and Elvis sang from a studio in Hollywood.

text: In what year did the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induct its first members?
fact: The museum itself opened in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1995.

text: How many studio albums did King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard release in 2017?
fact: The last of them, Gumboot Soup, came out on 31 December.

text: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 of which breed of dog during her reign?
fact: Many were descended from Susan, an 18th birthday present in 1944.

text: Denmark's Queen Mary, formerly Mary Donaldson, was born in which Australian city?
fact: She was born in 1972 and married Crown Prince Frederik in Copenhagen in 2004.

text: Which French king was known as the Sun King?
fact: He moved his court to the Palace of Versailles in 1682.

text: Prince William and Catherine Middleton met as students at which university?
fact: They met there in 2001.

text: Which king gave up the throne in 1936 to marry the American Wallis Simpson?
fact: After abdicating he was made Duke of Windsor.

text: Where are the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom kept on public display?
fact: The collection holds about 140 objects set with more than 23,000 gemstones.

text: Which title did Queen Elizabeth II give Prince Harry on his wedding day?
fact: The title had not been held by anyone since 1843.

text: From 1992, Queen Elizabeth II's portrait appeared on which Australian banknote?
fact: The portrait was drawn from photographs the Reserve Bank commissioned in 1984.

text: In which building did Prince Charles marry Lady Diana Spencer?
fact: About 750 million people around the world watched on television.

text: At which royal residence did Queen Elizabeth II die in September 2022?
fact: She was 96. Two days earlier she had appointed Liz Truss prime minister there.

text: Which flag flies over Buckingham Palace only when the monarch is in residence?
fact: It never flies at half-mast, because there is always a sovereign on the throne.

text: Which English king's remains were found under a Leicester car park in 2012?
fact: He was reburied in Leicester Cathedral in 2015.

text: Which wife of Henry VIII had her marriage annulled after about six months?
fact: She stayed in England as "the King's Beloved Sister" and outlived his other wives.

text: Who took the English throne when Elizabeth I died without children?
fact: He was the son of Mary, Queen of Scots, and ruled England as James I.

text: Queen Victoria's first prime minister gave his name to which Australian city?
fact: William Lamb, Lord Melbourne, was in office when the settlement was named in 1837.

text: Queen Victoria's 1840 wedding is widely credited with making what fashionable for brides?
fact: She married Prince Albert at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace.

text: Australian speech therapist Lionel Logue helped which king manage his stammer?
fact: Geoffrey Rush played Logue in the 2010 film The King's Speech.

text: Who was Britain's king when the First Fleet arrived in New South Wales in 1788?
fact: He reigned for 59 years, from 1760 to 1820.

text: Who in 2008 became the first woman to serve as Governor-General of Australia?
fact: She had been Governor of Queensland, and was Governor-General until 2014.

text: Which family captured the Rock of Monaco in 1297 and still rules the principality today?
fact: Legend says Francesco Grimaldi took the fortress disguised as a friar.

text: Which era began in Japan when Emperor Naruhito took the throne?
fact: Japan's foreign ministry explains the name as "beautiful harmony".

text: Who was the last emperor of China, removed from the throne as a child in 1912?
fact: He had become emperor in 1908, aged two.

text: Cleopatra's eldest son, Ptolemy XV, was said to be the child of which Roman?
fact: He is better known as Caesarion, a nickname meaning "little Caesar".

text: Queen Liliuokalani, overthrown in 1893, was the last monarch of which kingdom?
fact: She also wrote the song Aloha Oe.

text: At which home on the Isle of Wight did Queen Victoria die in 1901?
fact: It was built between 1845 and 1851 as a summer home for Victoria and Albert.

text: Adelaide is named after the queen consort of which British king?
fact: Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen married him in 1818. The city was named in 1836.

text: Who was the last monarch of the House of Stuart?
fact: In her reign the 1707 Acts of Union joined England and Scotland as Great Britain.

text: Who was the last British monarch to lead troops in battle?
fact: He led the allied army at Dettingen, in Bavaria, in 1743.

text: Until George V renamed it Windsor in 1917, what was the British royal house called?
fact: The change came amid strong anti-German feeling during the First World War.

text: Which crown was placed on Charles III's head at the moment of his crowning in 2023?
fact: Made for Charles II, it was swapped for the lighter Imperial State Crown before he left.

text: Sweden's royal house was founded by one of Napoleon's marshals. Which one?
fact: He was elected heir to the Swedish throne in 1810 and reigned as Charles XIV John.

text: In 1905 Norway left its union with Sweden and made a Danish prince king. What name did he take?
fact: Born Prince Carl of Denmark, he reigned until his death in 1957.

text: King Bhumibol of Thailand reigned for 70 years. In which country was he born?
fact: He was born in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1927 and spent his early life in Switzerland.

text: Mary Donaldson met Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik in 2000 at which Sydney pub?
fact: They met while the Sydney Olympics were on.

text: Catherine the Great took the Russian throne in 1762 by overthrowing which tsar?
fact: He was her husband. She went on to rule for more than 34 years.

text: Who was the last king to reign in France, forced out by the 1848 revolution?
fact: Styled "King of the French", he spent the rest of his life in exile in England.

text: How many wives did Henry VIII have?
fact: His first marriage, to Catherine of Aragon, lasted almost 24 years.

text: How many years on the throne did Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee mark?
fact: She was the first British monarch to reach a Platinum Jubilee.

text: In what year did Elizabeth II become queen?
fact: She was in Kenya when her father died. Her coronation followed in June 1953.

text: In what year did Australians vote No in a referendum on becoming a republic?
fact: About 55% voted No, and no state returned a Yes majority.

text: How many children did Queen Victoria and Prince Albert have?
fact: Their marriages into other royal families earned her the name "grandmother of Europe".

text: How old was Charles III when he became king in September 2022?
fact: No one older has ever come to the British throne.

text: How many British prime ministers served during Elizabeth II's reign?
fact: Winston Churchill was the first and Liz Truss the last.

text: For how many years did Louis XIV reign over France?
fact: He became king in 1643, aged four, and died in 1715.

text: In what year was the monarchy restored in England under Charles II?
fact: He rode into London on 29 May, his 30th birthday.

What is the trophy awarded to the winners of the men's Rugby World Cup called?
fact: It is named after the Rugby School pupil said to have first picked up the ball and run.

text: How many points is a try worth in rugby union today?
fact: Penalty goals and drop goals are worth three points each.

text: Which city is home to the Brumbies Super Rugby team?
fact: They won the Super 12 title in 2001 and 2004.

text: Which Wallabies winger of the 1980s and 90s was famous for his goose-step?
fact: He was named player of the tournament at the 1991 World Cup.

text: Which country won the first Rugby World Cup, in 1987?
fact: The All Blacks beat France 29-9 in the final at Eden Park, Auckland.

text: Which country joined the Tri Nations in 2012, turning it into the Rugby Championship?
fact: The Tri Nations had run since 1996.

text: Which country joined the Five Nations in 2000 to make it the Six Nations?
fact: The championship began in 1883 with only the four Home Nations.

text: Who captained South Africa to World Cup wins in 2019 and 2023?
fact: In 2018 he became the Springboks' first black Test captain.

text: As of the end of 2025, who had captained the Wallabies in the most Tests?
fact: The flanker led them 69 times between 2014 and 2023.

text: Whose long drop goal in extra time broke a 21-all deadlock in the Wallabies' 1999 World Cup semi-final?
fact: Most reports put it at 48 metres. Australia beat the Springboks 27-21 at Twickenham.

text: Which Wallaby taunted the All Blacks with "Four more years, boys" at the 2003 World Cup?
fact: It was the semi-final, which Australia won 22-10.

text: Which Wallabies great was nicknamed "Nobody", because nobody's perfect?
fact: The lock won two World Cups and was captain for the second, in 1999.

text: As of the end of 2025, who had played the most Tests for the Wallabies?
fact: The prop made his Test debut in 2010 and took the record in 2024.

text: Which team beat South Africa 34-32 at the 2015 World Cup, in the "Brighton Miracle"?
fact: Karne Hesketh scored the winning try in added time, after the 80 minutes were up.

text: Which of these nations took no part in the first two Rugby World Cups, in 1987 and 1991?
fact: The Springboks were shut out over apartheid, then won at their first attempt in 1995.

text: Which Springbok captain was handed the 1995 World Cup by Nelson Mandela?
fact: Mandela wore a Springbok jersey with Pienaar's number 6 on it.

text: Who was tour captain of the British and Irish Lions in Australia in 2025?
fact: The Lions won the series 2-1, losing only the last Test, 22-12 in Sydney.

text: Sydney's first-grade club rugby premiership is played for which trophy?
fact: It is named after Robert Shute and has been awarded since 1923.

text: Which Australian team won its first Super Rugby title in 2014, beating the Crusaders 33-32?
fact: Bernard Foley kicked the winning penalty in the 79th minute at Stadium Australia.

text: Which haka did the All Blacks first perform in 2005, as an alternative to Ka Mate?
fact: It was unveiled before a Test against the Springboks in Dunedin.

text: Which team did Australia beat in the final to win women's sevens gold at the 2016 Olympics?
fact: Australia won 24-17 in Rio, the first Olympic rugby gold awarded since 1924.

text: How many points is a penalty try worth in rugby union today?
fact: Since 2017 it has been an automatic seven, with no conversion attempt.

text: As of the end of 2025, what was the Wallaroos' best finish at a Women's Rugby World Cup?
fact: They beat France 22-8 in the third-place play-off in 2010.

text: What is it called when one Home Nation beats the other three in a Six Nations season?
fact: Beating all five opponents is a Grand Slam.

text: The 1905 "Original" All Blacks lost only one match on their tour of the British Isles. Who beat them?
fact: It finished 3-0 in Cardiff. New Zealanders long argued that Bob Deans had scored a try.

text: Which fourth-choice fly-half kicked the winning penalty in the 2011 World Cup final?
fact: He was whitebaiting on the Waikato River when the All Blacks called him up.

text: Who scored the last-minute try that beat the All Blacks in John Eales's final Test, in 2001?
fact: Australia won 29-26 in Sydney to keep the Tri Nations title.

text: Which prop scored the only try of the 1991 World Cup final?
fact: Michael Lynagh kicked the other eight points in the 12-6 win over England.

text: As of the end of 2025, which player held the men's Test try record, with 69?
fact: He scored them between 1996 and 2006. Bryan Habana finished two short.

text: The touring Wallabies won rugby gold at the 1908 London Olympics by beating which English county side?
fact: Cornwall, the county champions, stood in for Great Britain. Australia, as Australasia, won 32-3.

text: At which Sydney ground did the Wallabies lose their 1987 World Cup semi-final to France?
fact: France won 30-24, with Serge Blanco scoring the deciding try.

text: Mark, Glen and Gary Ella all went to which Sydney high school?
fact: All three were in the unbeaten Australian Schools side that toured Britain in 1977-78.

text: Rugby sevens was first played in 1883 in which Scottish Borders town?
fact: Local butcher Ned Haig came up with it as a fundraiser for his club.

text: Which country won the first Women's Rugby World Cup, in 1991?
fact: They beat England 19-6 in the final at Cardiff Arms Park.

text: Which country's national rugby team is nicknamed the Lelos?
fact: The name comes from lelo burti, an old folk ball game. Lelo is also their word for a try.

text: A Wallabies v Lions series trophy was named after which man, who played Tests for both sides?
fact: He played for Australia from 1908 and toured with the British side in 1910.

text: What number does the scrum-half traditionally wear?
fact: The fly-half, the other half of the pairing, wears 10.

text: How many players from each team normally pack down in a rugby union scrum?
fact: Two props, a hooker, two locks and three back-rowers. A sevens scrum has just three a side.

text: In what year did rugby union officially turn professional?
fact: The first Super 12 and Tri Nations seasons followed a year later.

text: In what year did the Wallabies come from 1-0 down to win a Test series against the Lions 2-1?
fact: It was Australia's first series win over the Lions.

text: According to legend, in what year did a Rugby School pupil first pick up the ball and run with it?
fact: Historians doubt the story, which first appeared in print in 1876.

text: How many points did the Wallabies score against Namibia at the 2003 World Cup, without conceding any?
fact: As of 2025 it was the biggest winning margin at a men's World Cup. Australia scored 22 tries.

text: In what year was the value of a try in rugby union last raised?
fact: The rise before that came in 1971.

text: How many people watched the Wallabies host the All Blacks at Stadium Australia in July 2000?
fact: It was a world record crowd for rugby union. A late Jonah Lomu try won it 39-35.

text: In what year was the first rugby international played, between Scotland and England?
fact: Scotland won at Raeburn Place in Edinburgh.

text: Put these nations in order of men's Rugby World Cup wins as of the end of 2025, most first.

Put these Wallabies in order of their Test debut, earliest first.

Put these Wallabies in order of Test tries scored, most first.
What is the largest organ of the human body?
fact: An adult's skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres.

text: Which planet is home to a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
fact: The Great Red Spot is wider than Earth, though it has been slowly shrinking.

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
fact: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and the third pumps it around the body.

text: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red cells?
fact: O negative red cells can be given to almost anyone, so hospitals keep them for emergencies.

text: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
fact: The femur is about a quarter of a person's height.

text: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air. Oxygen is about 21%.

text: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
fact: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish he had left out while on holiday.

text: Which part of the eye controls how much light gets in?
fact: The iris widens and narrows the pupil to control how much light reaches the retina.

text: Which vitamin does your skin make when exposed to sunlight?
fact: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones.

text: Which mineral sits at 10, the top of the Mohs hardness scale?
fact: German geologist Friedrich Mohs introduced his scratch-hardness scale in 1812.

text: Dry ice is the solid form of which substance?
fact: It's called dry ice because it never melts into a puddle. It turns straight into gas.

text: Botanically speaking, bamboo is a type of what?
fact: Some bamboo species can grow almost a metre in a single day.

text: What connects a muscle to a bone?
fact: Ligaments connect bone to bone. The Achilles is the body's thickest tendon.

text: What is a shark's skeleton made of?
fact: Shark cartilage is about half as dense as bone, which keeps the skeleton light.

text: Which planet is tipped over so far that it spins on its side?
fact: Uranus is tilted about 98 degrees, possibly after a huge collision long ago.

text: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
fact: The stapes, in the middle ear, is only about 2 to 3 mm long.

text: Which element has the chemical symbol K?
fact: K comes from kalium, the New Latin name for potassium.

text: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
fact: About three-quarters of all normal matter in the universe, by mass, is hydrogen.

text: Which of these metals is a liquid at 20°C?
fact: Gallium is close behind. It melts at about 30°C, so it can melt in your hand.

text: Which organ makes insulin?
fact: Insulin was first used to treat a diabetic patient in 1922, in Toronto.

text: Which is the fastest animal on Earth when diving?
fact: Peregrines hit their top speed in a hunting dive called a stoop.

text: Which gland in the neck makes hormones that control your metabolism?
fact: The butterfly-shaped thyroid sits at the front of the neck, just below the Adam's apple.

text: Which is the closest star to Earth after the Sun?
fact: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light years away, too faint to see without a telescope.

text: Marie Curie named which element after her home country?

text: In 1796, who used cowpox to protect a boy from smallpox?

text: Which part of the brain mainly controls balance and coordination?
fact: The cerebellum is about 10% of the brain's volume but has more neurons than the rest combined.

text: What is the largest moon in the Solar System?
fact: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is wider than the planet Mercury.

text: Which planet has the fastest winds in the Solar System?
fact: Winds on Neptune reach about 2,000 km/h.

text: Which land animal has the longest pregnancy?
fact: An elephant pregnancy lasts about 22 months.

text: What will the Sun eventually become after its red giant phase?
fact: The Sun is too small to become a black hole or neutron star.

text: Aspirin was developed from a compound found in the bark of which tree?

text: The tallest known living tree belongs to which species?
fact: A coast redwood in California named Hyperion is about 116 m tall.

text: Which planet is less dense than water?
fact: Saturn is the only planet in the Solar System whose average density is less than water's.

text: What chemical makes chilli peppers taste hot?

text: Barry Marshall drank a culture of which bacterium to prove it causes stomach ulcers?

text: Which human cells have no nucleus when mature?

text: What was the first animal to orbit Earth?

text: What is the point in a planet's orbit closest to the Sun called?
fact: Earth reaches perihelion in early January, during the Australian summer.

text: Sound travels fastest through which of these?
fact: Sound moves through steel at about 5,900 m/s, roughly 17 times faster than in air.

text: Which element was discovered in the Sun before it was found on Earth?
fact: Helium is named after Helios, the Greek sun god.

text: What did Wilhelm Röntgen discover in 1895?

text: Which part of a plant cell carries out photosynthesis?

text: Which SI unit is named after a Scottish inventor famous for steam engines?

text: What is the scientific study of fungi called?

text: Which plant produces the largest single flower in the world?

text: Four chemical elements are named after which Swedish village?
fact: Yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium all take their names from Ytterby and its mine.

text: What does a dendrochronologist use to date events?
fact: Tree-ring records in some places reach back more than 10,000 years.

text: What is the lightest metal?

text: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?

text: What is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?

text: Which scientist discovered the electron in 1897?

text: Which metal has the highest melting point?
fact: Tungsten melts at about 3,400°C, which is why it was used in light bulb filaments.

text: Which chicken-sized bird lays an egg about six times the size of a hen's egg?
fact: A brown kiwi's egg can weigh as much as 450 g.

text: Which planet takes longer to spin once on its axis than to orbit the Sun?
fact: Venus spins once every 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in 225.

text: Andre Agassi completed his career Grand Slam at the 1999 French Open by beating whom?
fact: Agassi came back from two sets down.

text: From 1975 to 1977, the US Open at Forest Hills was played on what surface?
fact: It was green Har-Tru clay; the event moved to hard courts at Flushing Meadows in 1978.

text: Serena Williams' outburst in her 2009 US Open semi-final followed a call for what?
fact: The penalty point came on match point, handing Kim Clijsters the win.

text: Tennis returned as a full Olympic medal sport at which Games, after 64 years away?
fact: It had been a demonstration sport in 1968 and 1984.

text: Who beat Carlos Alcaraz in the men's singles final at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
fact: It was Djokovic's first Olympic gold.

text: Which unseeded 20-year-old won the 2017 French Open women's singles?
fact: It was her first title on the WTA Tour.

text: How many French Open singles titles did Rafael Nadal win?
fact: He won on his debut in 2005.

text: In a standard tiebreak, what is the fewest points a player needs to win it?
How long is a tennis court from baseline to baseline, in feet?
fact: That is 23.77 metres.

text: Isner beat Mahut in the longest match ever, at Wimbledon in 2010. The final set ended 70 games to how many?
fact: The match lasted 11 hours and 5 minutes over three days.

text: In the 1980 Wimbledon final, John McEnroe won the famous fourth-set tiebreak 18 points to how many?
fact: Björn Borg still won the match in five sets.

text: The 2012 Australian Open final, still the longest Slam final, lasted 5 hours and how many minutes?
fact: Novak Djokovic beat Rafael Nadal in five sets.

text: Australia beat Spain on grass at Rod Laver Arena to win the Davis Cup in which year?
How many Wimbledon men's doubles titles did "the Woodies", Woodbridge and Woodforde, win together?
How many times did Chris Evert and Martina Navratilova play each other?
fact: Navratilova led their head-to-head 43–37.

text: Put these women in order of Grand Slam singles titles, most first.
What is the name of the language that Furby toys speak?
fact: The first Furbies knew about 200 words, half of them in English.

text: What is the name of the giraffe mascot of Toys "R" Us?
fact: In 1950s adverts for the chain's forerunner he was called Dr. G. Raffe.

text: What paperwork came with every Cabbage Patch Kid?
fact: Each doll had a birth certificate too. Xavier Roberts first sold them as Little People.

text: What set Heelys apart from ordinary sneakers?
fact: Roger Adams filed his first patent for them in 1999.

text: In the first Transformers toy line, what does Optimus Prime turn into?
fact: Bumblebee began as a Volkswagen Beetle.

text: In the backyard game Totem Tennis, what is the ball attached to?
fact: Two players hit it in opposite directions around the pole. It is also called swingball.

text: Barbie and Hot Wheels were both launched by which toy company?
fact: Matchbox, once the great rival of Hot Wheels, joined the same stable in 1997.

text: Zhu Zhu Pets were robotic toy versions of which animal?
fact: The first ones included Chunk, PipSqueak, Mr. Squiggles and Num Nums.

text: The Frisbee's name is traced to the Frisbie company of Connecticut. What did that company make?
fact: Students tossed its empty tins. Wham-O first sold its disc as the Pluto Platter.

text: What was Play-Doh first sold as, before it became a toy?
fact: It lifted coal soot off walls. A nursery teacher, Kay Zufall, saw it could be a toy.

text: Mr. Potato Head is credited as the first toy ever to do what?
fact: The first kits were for sticking faces on real potatoes. A plastic body came in 1964.

text: Why did Jack Odell make the first Matchbox toy small enough to fit in a matchbox?
fact: Her school only allowed toys that fitted in a matchbox, so he shrank a road roller.

text: Lonnie Johnson, who invented the Super Soaker, was an engineer at which organisation?
fact: He worked on the Galileo mission to Jupiter. His water gun was first sold as the Power Drencher.

text: The Care Bears began in 1981 as characters on what?
fact: Elena Kucharik drew them for American Greetings. Kenner's plush toys came later.

text: 'Tamagotchi' blends two Japanese words. One is the word for 'watch'. What does the other mean?
fact: Tamago is egg and uotchi is watch.

text: A 1938 US law keeps the classic Kinder Surprise off American shelves. What does it ban?
fact: The Italian company Ferrero has made Kinder Surprise since 1974.

text: Which humble plaything joined the US National Toy Hall of Fame in 2008?
fact: The cardboard box was inducted in 2005 and the blanket in 2011.

text: Hasbro coined the term 'action figure' so that boys would not be sold a 'doll'. For which toy?
fact: The first G.I. Joes stood about 30 cm tall. A 1982 relaunch shrank them to under 10 cm.

text: Which of these was NOT a command on the original Bop It?
fact: Spin it and Flick it arrived later, with Bop It Extreme.

text: Barbie and Ken took their names from which real pair?
fact: Ruth Handler's daughter was Barbara and her son was Kenneth.

text: Pogs took their name from POG, a Hawaiian brand of what?
fact: POG stands for passionfruit, orange and guava. Maui's Haleakala Dairy made it from 1971.

text: Shopkins, the tiny supermarket-themed collectables, were created by Moose Toys in which city?
fact: They went on sale in 2014. Moose Toys has been making toys since 1985.

text: The prototype for Polly Pocket was a tiny doll's house built inside what?
fact: Bluebird Toys of Swindon, England, made the first sets. The dolls were under an inch tall.

text: Which Australian toy company was selling plastic hoops before Wham-O's Hula Hoop swept America?
fact: Alex Tolmer made them in 1957, when Coles could not get enough bamboo hoops.

text: Which best-selling Australian novelist helped create Cadbury's Yowie?
fact: He developed it with Geoff Pike. Each chocolate held a native animal toy to build.

text: The first Transformers were reworked from Diaclone and Micro Change, toy lines by which Japanese firm?
fact: Hasbro bought the rights and had Marvel Comics write the robots a backstory.

text: Which company first sold the Nerf ball, long before Hasbro owned the brand?
fact: The first Nerf was a four-inch foam ball, sold as safe to throw indoors.

text: What fine powder coats the inside of an Etch A Sketch screen?
fact: French inventor André Cassagnes first called it L'Écran Magique, the magic screen.

text: In the US and Canada, Sylvanian Families are sold under what name?
fact: The Japanese company Epoch created the range in 1985.

text: Cheong Choon Ng invented the Rainbow Loom while working as what?
fact: He worked for Nissan and first called his loom Twistz Bandz.

text: What is the stretchy 1970s strongman Stretch Armstrong filled with?
fact: Kenner sold him from 1976. He stretches from 38 cm to well over a metre.

text: Which US agency made headlines in 1999 by banning Furbies from its Maryland headquarters?
fact: It feared the toys would repeat secrets. Staff who found one were to call security.

text: Which Australian animal was one of the nine original Beanie Babies?
fact: Patti the Platypus joined a frog, pig, dog, dolphin, whale, moose, bear and lobster.

text: Which model does its maker name as the very first Hot Wheels car?
fact: It was one of 16 cars in the first range, known to collectors as the Sweet 16.

text: Which company first published the Pokémon Trading Card Game in English?
fact: Its Base Set began the schoolyard craze. Wizards lost the licence in 2003.

text: Which maker's name was printed on the Coca-Cola yo-yos of Australian schoolyards?
fact: They were stamped 'Genuine Russell Yo-Yo'. Russell ran contests in Australian schools.

text: How many studs are on top of a standard 2x4 LEGO brick?
fact: Six of these bricks can be combined in 915,103,765 ways.

text: In what year did fidget spinners become a worldwide craze?
fact: Each one spins on a ball bearing. Some schools banned them for disrupting lessons.

text: In what year did the Ken doll first go on sale as Barbie's boyfriend?
fact: His full name is Kenneth Sean Carson. Barbie's is Barbara Millicent Roberts.

text: How many small coloured squares cover the outside of a standard 3x3 Rubik's Cube?
fact: Nine on each of six faces. The cube has about 43 quintillion possible arrangements.

text: How many buttons does a classic Tamagotchi have?
fact: Its two creators shared an Ig Nobel Prize for economics.

text: In what year did Hot Wheels cars first go on sale?
fact: Elliot Handler wanted a flashier rival to England's Matchbox cars.

text: In what year did the first modern LEGO minifigures appear?
fact: Jens Nygaard Knudsen designed them. A minifigure stands 4 cm tall.

text: How many different answers can a Magic 8 Ball give?
fact: Ten are positive, five negative and five vague, on a 20-sided die floating in blue liquid.

text: How many teeth does a Labubu show in its grin?
fact: Hong Kong-born artist Kasing Lung created Labubu. Pop Mart has sold the toys since 2019.

text: Put these toys in order of when they first went on sale, earliest first.
Put these crazes in order of when they swept the world, earliest first.
Put these Christmas must-have toys in order of their big year, earliest first.
Put these in order of their first year in toy shops, earliest first.
Put these LEGO themes in order of launch, earliest first.
Which three-letter airport code is printed on a luggage tag for a flight to Bali?
fact: It stands for Denpasar, the island's capital. The airport is named after I Gusti Ngurah Rai.

text: In which city do you tap on to trains and buses with an Oyster card?
fact: The blue smartcard was first issued in 2003.

text: Which greeting will you hear all day long on a holiday in Fiji?
fact: It means hello, and its literal meaning is life.

text: In the film Rain Man, which is the only airline Raymond is willing to fly?
fact: At least 15 airlines cut the scene from the version of the film they showed on board.

text: On a cruise ship, which side is "port" when you are facing the front?
fact: The right side is starboard.

text: The ski resorts Thredbo and Perisher are in which state?
fact: Both lie inside Kosciuszko National Park.

text: Cable Beach, known for camel rides at sunset, is in which Western Australian town?
fact: It is named after the telegraph cable laid from there to Java in 1889.

text: In which of these countries is tipping in restaurants not the custom, so staff may even hand it back?
fact: Saying "gochisosama deshita", thank you for the meal, is the polite way to show thanks.

text: The Kangaroo Route is the name for flights between Australia and which country?
fact: Qantas opened the route in 1947, flying Constellations all the way from Sydney to London.

text: Thailand's original Full Moon Party is held each month on Haad Rin beach, on which island?
fact: The island has no airport, so partygoers arrive by ferry or speedboat.

text: Which of these neighbouring countries drives on the left, as Australia does?
fact: Most of its land borders are with countries that drive on the right.

text: The backpacker circuit nicknamed the Banana Pancake Trail runs through which part of the world?
fact: The name is said to come from the breakfasts guesthouses cooked for Western travellers.

text: What is the traditional symbol of the Camino de Santiago, seen on waymarkers all along the walk?
fact: Yellow arrows point the way too, an idea credited to the village priest Elías Valiña.

text: Which Vietnamese town is famous for tailors who make clothes to measure in a day or two?
Niseko, loved by Australian skiers for its powder snow, is on which Japanese island?
fact: Skiers call its light powder champagne snow.

text: Maya Bay, where the 2000 film The Beach was shot, is in which Thai island group?
fact: The bay was shut to visitors from 2018 until early 2022.

text: What name did Qantas give its project for non-stop flights from Sydney to London and New York?
fact: It is named after wartime flights across the Indian Ocean that saw the sun rise twice.

text: In Venice, what is a vaporetto?
fact: A traghetto is the cheap gondola ferry that crosses the Grand Canal.

text: The Interislander ferry sails from Wellington to which South Island port?
fact: The ferry reaches Picton through Tory Channel and Queen Charlotte Sound.

text: A riad, a house built around a courtyard garden and now often a guesthouse, is typical of which country?
fact: The word comes from the Arabic for garden.

text: The running of the bulls in Pamplona is part of which festival?
fact: The festival runs from 6 to 14 July, with a bull run at 8 am each day from the 7th.

text: A classic Route 66 road trip starts in Chicago and ends in which Californian city?
fact: The road was commissioned in 1926 and crossed eight states.

text: Wineglass Bay is the best-known sight of which Tasmanian national park?
fact: The park was reserved in 1916, making it one of the first two in Tasmania.

text: Europe's passport-free Schengen Area is named after a village in which country?
fact: The agreement was signed in 1985 aboard a riverboat on the Moselle.

text: La Tomatina, the giant tomato fight, is held in which Spanish town?
fact: Since 2013 it has been a ticketed event.

text: Which London district was nicknamed Kangaroo Valley for the young Australians living there?
fact: Barry Humphries gave his comic-strip hero Barry McKenzie a flat there.

text: What was the title of Lonely Planet's first guidebook, published in 1973?
fact: Tony and Maureen Wheeler wrote it in Sydney after their own overland trip.

text: Contiki began in the early 1960s when John Anderson filled a minibus in London. Where was he from?
fact: Short of money and not keen to travel alone, he toured Europe with 11 strangers.

text: The world's first permanent youth hostel was set up by a schoolteacher in a castle in which country?
fact: Richard Schirrmann's hostel was in Altena Castle. Its first rooms are now a museum.

text: The world's first capsule hotel opened in 1979 in which city?
fact: It was designed by Kisho Kurokawa, the architect of Tokyo's Nakagin Capsule Tower.

text: Bangkok's Thai name, Krung Thep, is usually translated as what?
fact: The city's full ceremonial name runs to 168 letters.

text: In Lost in Translation, Bob and Charlotte meet while staying at which real Tokyo hotel?
fact: The hotel fills the top floors, 39 to 52, of the Shinjuku Park Tower.

text: The airport code YYZ belongs to the main airport of which Canadian city?
fact: Most of the airport lies in the neighbouring city of Mississauga.

text: A parador is a state-run hotel, often in an old castle or monastery, in which country?
fact: The first one opened in 1928, in the Gredos mountains.

text: On a restaurant bill in Italy, what is the "coperto"?
fact: It pays for the table setting and often the bread, and it is not a tip.

text: Which of these countries uses the same slanted-pin power plug as Australia?
fact: China and Fiji use it too.

text: For how many years is a standard adult Australian passport valid?
fact: Travellers aged 75 and over can choose a five-year passport instead.

text: On standard time, how many hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time is Sydney?
fact: Perth is two hours behind Sydney, at eight hours ahead.

text: In what year did Qantas begin flying non-stop between Perth and London?
fact: The flights began that March, using Boeing 787s.

text: As of 2026, a short stay in Europe's Schengen Area is limited to how many days in any 180-day period?
fact: In 2026 the area was made up of 29 countries, 25 of them EU members.

text: In what year did Japan's first Shinkansen bullet train line open?
fact: It opened nine days before the Tokyo Olympics began.

text: In what year did The Ghan first carry passengers all the way from Adelaide to Darwin?
fact: Until then the train stopped at Alice Springs. The full trip is 2,979 km.

text: In what year did the Interrail pass for train travel around Europe first go on sale?
fact: It began as a pass for travellers aged 21 and under.

text: In what year was the first Oktoberfest held?
fact: It marked the wedding of Bavaria's Crown Prince Ludwig and Princess Therese.

text: In what year did the world's first commercial bungy site open, at Kawarau Bridge near Queenstown?
fact: AJ Hackett and Henry van Asch were the pair behind it.

text: Put these east coast holiday towns in order from north to south, northernmost first.
Put these festivals in the order they fall in the calendar year, earliest first.
Put these Disney parks in order of opening, earliest first.
Put these famous journeys in order of length, shortest first.
It is midday in Sydney. Put these holiday spots in order of their local time, earliest first.
What does Darth Vader actually say to Luke in The Empire Strikes Back?
fact: Luke has just accused Vader of killing his father. The "No" is Vader's answer.

text: What do the letters of the distress call SOS stand for?
fact: It was agreed as the world standard in 1906: three dots, three dashes, three dots in Morse.

text: What did China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, say in 2003 about seeing the Great Wall from orbit?
fact: The wall is much the same colour as the land around it, so it barely stands out.
wrong: He saw it only at night

text: Myth or fact: chocolate can poison a dog?
fact: Dogs clear theobromine far more slowly than people. Darker chocolate is the bigger risk.
wrong: Myth: only the sugar is bad

text: What makes a bull charge at a matador's cape?
fact: Cattle are red-green colour blind. Bulls charge a moving cape of any colour.

text: Which of these is true of bats?
fact: Many bats also steer by echolocation, which is probably where the "blind" myth began.

text: Which mountain's summit is the highest above sea level?
fact: Mauna Kea is taller from base to peak, and Chimborazo's top is farthest from Earth's centre.

text: What really causes warts?
fact: The human papillomavirus is to blame. A toad's bumps are glands, and they are not catching.

text: What usually happens to a honey bee after it stings a person?
fact: Its barbed sting lodges in skin and tears away. Most other bee species can sting again.
wrong: It can sting again at once

text: Which famous "quote" is never actually said in the film Casablanca?
fact: The real line is Ilsa's: "Play it, Sam. Play As Time Goes By."

text: Which part of the tongue can taste sweetness?
fact: The school "tongue map" grew from a misreading of a German paper from 1901.

text: What have controlled trials found about sugar and children's behaviour?
fact: A 1995 review in the medical journal JAMA pooled the trials and found no effect.

text: What mainly decides which way water swirls down a household sink or toilet?
fact: The Coriolis effect is real and steers cyclones, but it is far too weak to rule a sink.
answer: The bowl's shape and water flow

text: Daddy-long-legs spiders are said to have the deadliest venom of all. What does the evidence say?
fact: The Australian Museum says the venom is not very potent, even for insects.
answer: No evidence; the venom is weak
wrong: True, but fangs are too short
True, but they have no fangs

text: Compared with the average Frenchman of his day, how tall was Napoleon?
fact: His "5 foot 2" was in French units, about 1.68 m. British cartoonists drew him tiny.
answer: About average or a bit taller

text: In WWII, Britain said carrots gave its night-fighter pilots sharp eyes. What was it hiding?
fact: Ace pilot John Cunningham was nicknamed "Cat's Eyes" as part of the cover story.
wrong: A network of spies in France

text: "Lightning never strikes twice." About how often does it hit the Empire State Building each year?
fact: The US National Weather Service puts the average at 23 strikes a year.

text: What rank did James Cook hold when he charted Australia's east coast in the Endeavour in 1770?
fact: He was made a commander in 1771, and a post-captain in 1775 after his second voyage.

text: How does Sydney's average yearly rainfall compare with London's?
fact: Sydney's Observatory Hill averages about 1,200 mm a year. Heathrow gets about 615 mm.
answer: Sydney gets about twice as much
wrong: Sydney gets about half as much
Sydney gets a quarter as much

text: Where does the story of Isaac Newton and the falling apple come from?
fact: He told it to his friend William Stukeley in 1726. The apple hitting his head is a later touch.
wrong: A poem written after he died

text: Which of these is true of Albert Einstein's school days?
fact: He said he had mastered calculus before 15. At 16 he failed an entry exam, but not its maths.

text: Which of these popular beliefs about the body is true?
fact: Seeing, hearing or even reading about a yawn can set one off.
wrong: Reading in dim light ruins eyes
The head loses most body heat

text: Horned Viking helmets were made famous by 1870s stage costumes for whose operas?
fact: Carl Emil Doepler designed them for the Ring cycle in 1876. Viking-age texts mention no horns.

text: Which writer told the "Let them eat cake" story in a book written when Marie Antoinette was a child?
fact: His Confessions credits it to "a great princess". It was pinned on her decades after she died.

text: What did the scholars who doubted Columbus's plan get right?
fact: Educated Europeans knew the Earth was round. Columbus had badly underestimated its size.
answer: Asia was much too far away
wrong: The seas boiled at the equator

text: Toast knocked off a table is said to land butter side down. What did physicist Robert Matthews show in 1995?
fact: A table is too low for the toast to finish a full turn. He won a 1996 Ig Nobel Prize for it.
answer: It is true at table height
wrong: It is false: the odds are 50-50
Butter side up is more likely

text: Which Disney nature documentary staged the scene that spread the myth of lemmings' mass suicide?
fact: The 1958 scene was staged with a few dozen lemmings, far from the sea in Alberta.

text: Who wrote "I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it"?
fact: She wrote it in a book about Voltaire to sum up his attitude. Readers took it for his words.

text: According to the Australian National Dictionary Centre, where does "pom" for a Briton come from?
fact: "Pomegranate" played on "Jimmy Grant", slang for an immigrant. No evidence backs the acronym.

text: A 2003 study followed 130 confirmed white-tailed spider bites. How many caused skin ulcers?
fact: The Medical Journal of Australia study found most bites caused only pain and a red mark.

text: Thomas Crapper did not invent the flush toilet. Who described one in 1596 and built one for Elizabeth I?
fact: Harington was the Queen's godson. Crapper was a real plumber, but centuries later.

text: Why are the panes in very old windows often thicker at the bottom?
fact: Glass does not visibly sag at room temperature. Glaziers often set the thick edge down.
wrong: Rain has worn the tops thin

text: Which of these is the biggest number?
fact: A 2015 count found about 3 trillion trees. The Milky Way has 100 to 400 billion stars.
wrong: Nerve cells in a human brain

text: Sherlock Holmes's deerstalker hat is never named in the stories. Who gave it to him?
fact: The line "Elementary, my dear Watson" is not in Conan Doyle's stories either.

text: How strong is Earth's gravity at the height of the International Space Station?
fact: Astronauts float because the station is in constant free fall around the Earth.

text: Counting islands, how far apart are Russia and the United States at their closest?
fact: Russia's Big Diomede and Alaska's Little Diomede sit either side of the date line.

text: How many months of the year have at least 28 days?
fact: All of them. February is just the only one that can stop there.

text: The "10 per cent" line is a myth. What percentage of the brain does a healthy person use?
fact: Scans show activity right across the brain over a day, even during sleep.

text: Owls cannot turn their heads in a full circle. How many degrees can they turn them each way?
fact: Johns Hopkins researchers found the neck arteries have extra room, so the twist is safe.

text: In what year did Orson Welles's radio play The War of the Worlds go to air?
fact: The famous "mass panic" was mostly a newspaper story. Few people were even tuned in.

text: Until what year did Australia's federal Parliament sit in Melbourne rather than Canberra?
fact: It met in Victoria's Parliament House from 1901 and opened in Canberra on 9 May 1927.

text: In what year did Swiss women win the right to vote in national elections?
fact: Men approved it in a referendum. One canton held out on local votes until 1990.

text: How many soldiers did the Australian army send to fight the 1932 "Emu War"?
fact: Major Meredith, a sergeant and a gunner took two Lewis guns and 10,000 rounds.

text: In what year was "OMG" first written down, in a letter from an admiral to Winston Churchill?
fact: Lord Fisher wrote "O.M.G. (Oh! My God!)". It is the Oxford English Dictionary's earliest record.

text: Coca-Cola did not put Santa in red, but in what year did its famous Sundblom Santa ads begin?
fact: Santa was already wearing red on magazine covers in the early 1900s, long before the ads.

text: Greenland looks huge on most maps. Put these in order of real land area, smallest first.
fact: The Mercator projection stretches land near the poles. Africa is 14 times Greenland's size.

text: Put these moments in order, earliest first. One is older than you might think.
fact: Scottish clockmaker Alexander Bain patented his fax idea 33 years before Bell's telephone.

text: Put these in order of when they began, earliest first.
fact: Oxford has no founding date, but teaching was under way there by 1096.

text: Put these in order of how wide they are, narrowest first.
fact: Australia is wider than the Moon and Pluto, though far smaller in surface area.

text: Put these in order of when they first appeared on Earth, earliest first.
fact: Shark-like scales turn up in rocks about 450 million years old, long before the first trees.

text: In The Office (US), what is the name of the paper company?
fact: The show follows its branch in Scranton, Pennsylvania.

text: In Friends, what is the name of the coffee house where the gang hangs out?
Who plays Detective Jake Peralta in Brooklyn Nine-Nine?
What is the first of the six deadly games in season 1 of Squid Game?
In Stranger Things, which food is Eleven famously obsessed with?
In Game of Thrones, what are the words of House Stark?
In Bluey, what is the name of Bluey's little sister?
fact: Muffin and Socks are her cousins; Coco is a pink poodle from school.

text: In Summer Heights High, what subject does Mr G teach?
fact: He gives himself the title Director of Performing Arts.

text: Married at First Sight Australia airs on which network?
In Breaking Bad, what is the name of Gus Fring's fried chicken chain?
In Succession, what is the name of the Roy family's media company?
The Bear is set in the kitchen of a restaurant in which city?
Zendaya won two Emmys for playing which Euphoria character?
fact: She won Lead Actress in a Drama in 2020 and again in 2022.

text: What is the name of the school in Netflix's Heartbreak High?
Who has hosted the American version of Survivor since it began in 2000?
Who hosted the first season of Love Island Australia?
fact: The first season was filmed in Mallorca, Spain.

text: Who won the first season of MasterChef Australia?
fact: Poh Ling Yeow was the runner-up.

text: In The Office (US), what does Dwight Schrute's family farm grow?
In Brooklyn Nine-Nine, what is the name of Captain Holt's corgi?
When Game of Thrones begins, who is king of the Seven Kingdoms?
In season 4 of Stranger Things, which Kate Bush song helps Max escape Vecna?
In Friends, what is the name of Ross's pet monkey?
Game of Thrones, Succession and Euphoria were all made by which American network?
In Kath & Kim, what do Kim and Brett name their baby daughter?
Who was Australia's first Bachelor, in the show's first season on Ten?
The Red Wedding takes place in which episode of Game of Thrones?
fact: It is the ninth episode of season 3.

text: In The Office (US), what is the title of the action film Michael Scott wrote and stars in?
fact: He plays Agent Michael Scarn; Jim plays the villain, Goldenface.

text: In Friends, which character does Joey play on the soap Days of Our Lives?
Who plays Logan Roy in Succession?
In Squid Game's honeycomb challenge, which shape does Gi-hun have to cut out?
fact: He gets through by licking the back of the honeycomb.

text: In season 3 of Stranger Things, what is the name of the ice cream shop where Steve works?
fact: It is in the Starcourt Mall.

text: Ja'mie King of Summer Heights High first appeared in which earlier series?
Married at First Sight is based on a show that began in which country?
fact: The Danish original is called Gift ved første blik.

text: In The Bear, what is the family sandwich shop called before it becomes The Bear?
The American series Euphoria is based on a series of the same name from which country?
Heartstopper is based on graphic novels by which author?
How many seasons of Game of Thrones were made?
How many players start the games in season 1 of Squid Game?
fact: The prize is 45.6 billion won: 100 million for every player.

text: In what year did the final episode of Friends air?
fact: The last episode went to air in the US on 6 May.

text: How many seasons of The Office (US) were made?
In what year did Euphoria, starring Zendaya, first air?
How many episodes of Breaking Bad were made?
In what year did the original Heartbreak High first air on Australian TV?
fact: It began on Network Ten; the Netflix reboot arrived in 2022.

text: The Bluey special The Sign is the show's longest episode. How many minutes does it run?
How many episodes of Friends were made?

fact: The RSPCA awarded his donkey its Purple Cross in 1997.

fact: Australian airmen of No. 3 Squadron buried him with full military honours.

text: What name was given to the ground between the opposing front-line trenches of the First World War?

fact: Its working name, 'landship', was thought to give too much away.

fact: British codebreakers read it. The prize on offer was Texas, New Mexico and Arizona.

fact: It grows wild on the Gallipoli peninsula.

text: 'They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old' is from For the Fallen. Who wrote it?
fact: It was first published in The Times in September 1914.

fact: Petra was carved into pink sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago.

text: Australia's first ever World Cup point came from a 0-0 draw with which country?
Which Italian fell over Lucas Neill to win the last-gasp penalty that knocked Australia out in 2006?
fact: Francesco Totti scored from the spot in the 95th minute.

text: Tofiq Bahramov, the linesman behind England's disputed third goal in 1966, came from which present-day country?
fact: English fans wrongly called him the Russian linesman. Baku's national stadium bears his name.

text: Who scored five goals for Russia against Cameroon in 1994, a men's World Cup record as of 2026?
fact: Russia won 6-1, and he shared that year's Golden Boot.

text: Who scored after about 11 seconds for Turkey in 2002, the fastest men's World Cup goal as of 2026?
fact: It came in the third-place play-off against South Korea.

text: As of the 2026 World Cup, who is the oldest goalscorer in men's World Cup history, at 42?
fact: He was 42 years and 39 days old.

text: The 1982 "Disgrace of Gijón" between West Germany and Austria sent which team home?
fact: A goal after ten minutes gave both sides the result they needed.

text: Who won the Golden Boot at the 2023 Women's World Cup with five goals?
Who scored the goal that beat Norway in 2023, New Zealand's first win at a men's or women's World Cup?
fact: It came in the tournament's opening match at Eden Park.

text: Which Brazilian played at a record seven Women's World Cups, from 1995 to 2019?
fact: She also played at seven Olympic Games.

text: Which team knocked Italy out of the 1966 World Cup with a 1-0 win in Middlesbrough?
fact: Pak Doo-ik scored. They then led Portugal 3-0 in the quarter-final but lost 5-3.

text: How many teams played at the 2026 World Cup, the biggest yet?
fact: They played 104 matches in all.

text: How many World Cups did Pelé win as a player?
fact: As of the 2026 World Cup, no other player has won more than two.

text: In what year did the Socceroos first play at a World Cup?
fact: They drew one game and lost two, without scoring a goal.

text: In what year was the first FIFA Women's World Cup held?
fact: China hosted it, and Norway lost the final 2-1.

text: How many Women's World Cup goals did Marta score, the record as of the 2023 tournament?
fact: She scored them across five tournaments, from 2003 to 2019.

text: In what year did France win the men's World Cup for the first time?
fact: They won it at home, with Zinedine Zidane heading two goals in the final.

text: How many goals did Just Fontaine score at the 1958 World Cup, a single-tournament record as of 2026?
fact: He needed only six matches, and it was the only World Cup he played in.

text: In what year was a match at the men's World Cup finals first decided by a penalty shoot-out?
fact: It settled a semi-final in Seville that had finished 3-3 after extra time.

text: How many men's World Cup goals had Kylian Mbappé scored in total as of the 2026 tournament, a record?
fact: He scored 10 of them in 2026. The record before that tournament was Miroslav Klose's 16.

Which of these four things happened first?
fact: Squid Game arrived in September 2021. Musk bought Twitter in 2022. The other two came in 2023.

text: Which of these happened in 2021?
fact: The Games kept the name Tokyo 2020 but ran from 23 July to 8 August 2021.
wrong: The first photo of a black hole

text: In which year did Britain vote for Brexit, Donald Trump first win a US election and DiCaprio win his Oscar?
fact: Leonardo DiCaprio won Best Actor for The Revenant at the ceremony on 28 February.

text: In which year did ChatGPT first open to the public?
fact: OpenAI released the first version in November 2022.

text: In which year did Australians vote Yes to same-sex marriage in a national postal survey?
fact: The result, 61.6 per cent Yes, was announced on 15 November.

text: Which of these four films reached cinemas first?
fact: Top Gun came out in 1986. Its sequel, Top Gun: Maverick, followed 36 years later.

text: Which of these social networks launched first?
fact: Tumblr followed in 2007, Pinterest in 2010 and TikTok's international app in 2017.

text: In which year did Tiger King arrive on Netflix?
fact: It was released on 20 March 2020, just as the first COVID lockdowns began.

text: In which year did Princess Diana die, Hong Kong return to China and Mike Tyson bite Evander Holyfield's ear?
fact: Tyson bit Holyfield on 28 June, Hong Kong changed hands on 1 July and Diana died on 31 August.

text: In which year did Steve Irwin die and Melbourne host the Commonwealth Games?
fact: Melbourne's Games ran from 15 to 26 March 2006. Irwin died on 4 September.

text: In which year did Game of Thrones end, Avengers: Endgame open and Scott Morrison win his "miracle" election?
fact: Australia voted on 18 May 2019. The Game of Thrones finale went to air in the US the next day.

text: Which of these children's TV shows first went to air in 1969?
fact: Sesame Street began on American public television on 10 November 1969.

text: Which of these happened in 2018?
fact: She played on 14 and 21 April 2018. The shows became the Netflix film Homecoming.
wrong: Lady Gaga wore a meat dress

text: Which James Bond film came out in the same year as the London Olympics?
fact: London hosted the Games in 2012. Skyfall opened in Britain that October.

text: In which year did Star Wars return to cinemas with The Force Awakens?
fact: It opened in December 2015, ten years after Revenge of the Sith.

text: The seventh and last Harry Potter novel, The Deathly Hallows, was published in which year?
fact: It went on sale on 21 July 2007. The last of the films came out four years later.

text: In which year did Prince Charles marry Camilla Parker Bowles?
fact: They married in a civil ceremony at the Windsor Guildhall on 9 April 2005.

text: Which of these happened in 1998?
fact: eBay dates from 1995, Wikipedia from 2001 and Skype from 2003.

text: In which year did Barack Obama win his first presidential election?
fact: He beat John McCain on 4 November 2008 and took office the following January.

text: In which year were twelve boys and their football coach rescued from a flooded cave in Thailand?
fact: They went into Tham Luang cave on 23 June. The last of them came out on 10 July.

text: Which of these cartoons first went to air in 1999?
fact: SpongeBob had a sneak preview on 1 May 1999 and began its regular run that July.

text: In which year did Nelson Mandela walk free from prison and East and West Germany reunite?
fact: Mandela was released on 11 February. Germany became one country again on 3 October.

text: In which year did Pope Francis take office, Black Caviar retire unbeaten and William and Kate have Prince George?
fact: Francis was elected on 13 March, Black Caviar retired on 17 April and George was born on 22 July.

text: In which year did Medicare begin, the $1 coin arrive and Advance Australia Fair become the anthem?
fact: Medicare began on 1 February, the anthem was proclaimed on 19 April and the coin came on 14 May.

text: Which games console first went on sale in the same year as the Sydney Olympics?
fact: The PlayStation 2 launched in Japan in March 2000 and reached Australia that November.

text: Which of these famous names is the oldest?
fact: Barbie made her debut at a New York toy fair on 9 March 1959.

text: In which year did Margaret Thatcher become Britain's first female prime minister?
fact: She had led the Conservative Party since 1975 and stayed in office until 1990.

text: In which year did Concorde carry its last paying passengers?
fact: Air France stopped its flights that May and British Airways on 24 October.

text: In which year was Sydney's first Gay Mardi Gras held?
fact: It was held on 24 June 1978. Those who took part are known as the 78ers.

text: In which year did French agents sink the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour?
fact: Two bombs sank the ship at its berth on 10 July 1985.

text: In which year did the Falklands War break out, E.T. reach cinemas and Brisbane host the Commonwealth Games?
fact: Brisbane's Games ran from 30 September to 9 October.

text: Which of these Apple products went on sale first?
fact: The Watch went on sale in April 2015. AirPods followed in December 2016.

text: Which of these toy crazes came first?
fact: Bandai released the first Tamagotchi in Japan on 23 November 1996.

text: Which of these happened in 1991?
fact: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as Soviet president on 25 December 1991.

text: In which year did Michelle Payne become the first woman to ride a Melbourne Cup winner?
fact: She won on Prince of Penzance, a 100-1 outsider, on 3 November 2015.

text: Which of these screen and comic-book landmarks is the oldest?
fact: The Jazz Singer had its premiere on 6 October 1927.
answer: The Jazz Singer, an early talkie
wrong: Gone with the Wind, the film

text: In what year did the Berlin Wall come down?
fact: The border was thrown open on the night of 9 November.

text: In what year did the September 11 attacks on the United States take place?
In what year did Michael Jackson die?
fact: He died in Los Angeles on 25 June, aged 50.

text: In what year did Oprah Winfrey tape her talk show at the Sydney Opera House?
fact: She taped two shows there on 14 December, in front of about 6,000 fans.

text: In what year was US President John F. Kennedy shot dead in Dallas?
fact: He was killed on 22 November while riding in a motorcade through the city.

text: In what year were 33 miners in Chile winched to safety after 69 days underground?
fact: The last man reached the surface on 13 October.

text: In what year did the German airship Hindenburg burst into flames while landing in New Jersey?
fact: It caught fire on 6 May, at the end of a flight across the Atlantic.

text: In what year did Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne found Apple?
fact: The partnership was formed on 1 April to sell Wozniak's Apple I computer.

text: In what year did the IOC announce that Sydney would host the 2000 Olympics?
fact: The vote was held in Monte Carlo on 23 September, seven years before the Games.
